learning.reason: Test the candidate that will be distributed next, without mistaking success with the old current value for success with the candidate. Then switch the application's default version to the one that has been validated.
learning.concept: testSecret validates AWSPENDING, which is promoted with finishSecret.

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Migrate an unencrypted RDS database to an encrypted configuration
prompt: You need to encrypt an unencrypted RDS DB instance during a maintenance window. Writes can be stopped during the window, and you will validate the migrated database before switching the connection target. Which approach should you choose to determine the existing database's data and the encryption key to use?

choices.text: Copy a DB snapshot with encryption enabled, then restore a new DB from that copy.
choices.explanation: You can create an encrypted instance from the encrypted snapshot, validate it, and then switch from the old DB.

choices.text: Modify the existing DB instance, enable encryption, specify a key, and keep using the same storage.
choices.explanation: You cannot directly enable encryption on an existing unencrypted DB instance.

choices.text: Recreate the existing DB subnet group and have the encryption setting from the new subnets carry over to the existing volume.
choices.explanation: Network placement and encryption at rest for a database are separate settings.

choices.text: Require TLS for clients and assume that the existing DB's stored snapshots are encrypted by the same setting.
choices.explanation: TLS protects data in transit; it does not change encryption for stored data or snapshots.

learning.reason: You can create an encrypted instance from the encrypted snapshot, validate it, and then switch from the old DB.
learning.concept: Restore RDS from an encrypted copy of an unencrypted snapshot

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Keep a sensitive attribute in plaintext only for the client
prompt: You store orders in DynamoDB. The order ID is used for searches, and a sensitive attribute must be encrypted before writing so that even another team allowed to use DynamoDB GetItem cannot read it in plaintext. Only a designated application may retrieve the plaintext. What should you use?

choices.text: Use the AWS Database Encryption SDK to encrypt the sensitive attribute on the client, and allow only the designated application to use the key needed for decryption.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB handles the sensitive attribute as ciphertext, so permission to read the table alone cannot recover the plaintext.

choices.text: Require only TLS connections to the table, without evaluating decryption-key permissions for clients that can connect.
choices.explanation: Protecting data in transit does not hide the plaintext attribute from a client with read access.

choices.text: Encrypt only the DynamoDB backups and keep the operational table returning application attributes in plaintext.
choices.explanation: This does not address the problem of the sensitive attribute being returned in plaintext through the table's read path.

choices.text: Use a customer managed KMS key for encryption at rest on the table, and allow all teams to use ordinary GetItem on that table.
choices.explanation: Server-side encryption alone does not meet the requirement that a legitimate read return the attribute as ciphertext.

learning.reason: DynamoDB handles the sensitive attribute as ciphertext, so permission to read the table alone cannot recover the plaintext.
learning.concept: Selective client-side attribute encryption in DynamoDB

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Deny HTTP to S3 while preserving existing authorization
prompt: An S3 bucket has several IAM roles that handle data. For ordinary direct client requests only, you must forcefully deny HTTP while preserving the permissions currently allowed by policy. Exclude AWS service principals that access S3 from this change. Which statement should you add?

choices.text: Deny all requests from non-AWS services without checking aws:SecureTransport.
choices.explanation: This would also deny existing permissions for legitimate TLS clients, making the scope broader than required.

choices.text: Add an Allow only when TLS is used, and leave other IAM policies that currently allow HTTP in place.
choices.explanation: Adding an Allow alone cannot deny non-TLS requests if another authorization path grants access.

choices.text: Enable encryption at rest with an AWS KMS key and require IAM roles to retrieve only encrypted objects.
choices.explanation: Encryption at rest does not impose a condition that denies HTTP between clients and S3.

choices.text: Add an explicit Deny on the bucket and objects when aws:SecureTransport is false and aws:PrincipalIsAWSService is false.
choices.explanation: This denies direct non-TLS access while excluding service principals from the new Deny.

learning.reason: Deny direct non-TLS access while excluding service principals from the new Deny.
learning.concept: The S3 aws:SecureTransport condition and exclusion of AWS service principals

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Prevent plaintext database connections and endpoint impersonation
prompt: For all application connections to RDS for PostgreSQL, you need to reject plaintext sessions and verify that TLS clients connected to the correct RDS endpoint. The client-side parameters can be changed. Which two actions should you take? Select two.

choices.text: Enable rds.force_ssl in the DB parameter group to reject connections that do not use TLS.
choices.explanation: This is a server-side control that requires all clients to use encrypted connections.

choices.text: Allow the PostgreSQL port in the security group and treat any session that can reach that port as TLS-protected.
choices.explanation: Port reachability settings do not distinguish plaintext from TLS connections using the same port.

choices.text: Add the RDS CA to the client's trusted CA configuration and connect with sslmode=verify-full to verify the connection name as well.
choices.explanation: This verifies both a trusted certificate chain and the hostname of the requested endpoint.

choices.text: Set only sslmode=require on the client, without configuring CA and hostname verification separately.
choices.explanation: Requiring encryption alone does not provide the same assurance as verify-full, which also checks the correct hostname.

choices.text: Configure KMS encryption at rest for the DB instance and assume the endpoint is verified when authentication succeeds.
choices.explanation: Encryption at rest does not enforce TLS for connections or verify the endpoint certificate.

learning.reason: This is a server-side control that requires all clients to use encrypted connections. A trusted certificate chain and the hostname of the requested endpoint can both be verified.
learning.concept: Server-side enforcement with rds.force_ssl and client-side verification with verify-full

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Only encrypted objects are not replicated to another Region
prompt: Use cross-Region replication between S3 buckets in the same account. Ordinary objects are replicated, but objects written with SSE-KMS under the target prefix after the rule was created are not. How can you use a customer managed key at the destination as well?

choices.text: Specify a key from the source Region as the replica key and use the same ARN across Regions.
choices.explanation: The KMS key for replicas must be available in the destination bucket's Region.

choices.text: Specify a central key in the destination bucket's default encryption settings and keep the replication rule's existing scope.
choices.explanation: The destination's default settings alone do not add SSE-KMS source objects to the replication scope.

choices.text: Only add S3 permissions for the replication role on the rule, leaving the SSE-KMS object selection and KMS permissions unchanged.
choices.explanation: S3 permissions alone do not enable selection of SSE-KMS objects or grant the required operations on the encryption keys.

choices.text: Select SSE-KMS objects in the rule, specify a key in the destination Region, and grant the replication role the required KMS permissions.
choices.explanation: Explicitly selecting SSE-KMS objects and authorizing decryption at the source and encryption at the destination are both required.

learning.reason: Explicitly select SSE-KMS objects and authorize decryption at the source and encryption at the destination.
learning.concept: SSE-KMS object selection for replication and a replica key in the destination Region

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Provide artifact signatures to recipients without network access
prompt: A central deployment system signs artifacts. The signatures must be verified on devices without an external network connection, and the private key used for signing must remain within AWS's key management boundary. The devices do not have AWS credentials. How should you configure this?

choices.text: Encrypt the artifacts with a symmetric KMS key, then specify the same KMS key ARN on the devices to decrypt them offline.
choices.explanation: The key ARN alone does not let an offline device use a symmetric key; decryption and signature verification are also different operations.

choices.text: Create a MAC with a KMS HMAC key, then give the devices an HMAC public key obtained with GetPublicKey for comparison.
choices.explanation: HMAC uses a shared secret key and does not use a public key for asymmetric verification.

choices.text: Extract the private key from the asymmetric KMS key and store it on the devices, then re-sign each artifact on the device to check for a match.
choices.explanation: An asymmetric private key in KMS cannot be exported. The private key also does not need to be distributed to verify a signature.

choices.text: Sign with an asymmetric KMS key for signing, then distribute the signature and the retrieved public key to the devices for verification.
choices.explanation: You can sign without taking the private key outside KMS, then verify offline with the public key.

learning.reason: You can sign without taking the private key outside KMS, then verify offline with the public key.
learning.concept: An asymmetric KMS signing key and offline verification with its public key

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Restore SSE-KMS object ingestion for one external account only
prompt: An S3 bucket in account A contains accounting records encrypted with A's customer managed KMS key. Account B's ingestion role is allowed s3:GetObject for the target prefix by both accounts, but ingestion fails because KMS denies access. Where should you make changes without expanding permissions to other principals in B?

choices.text: Allow s3:GetObject for the same ingestion role again in A, and add kms:Decrypt only in B.
choices.explanation: Adding an IAM permission in B does not authorize an external role to use a key owned by A.

choices.text: Allow B to describe the key in A's key policy, and add kms:DescribeKey for the target key to B's role.
choices.explanation: This may allow retrieval of key information, but it does not grant permission to decrypt the ciphertext.

choices.text: Change the default encryption key configured for A's bucket to a key in B, and reread the existing objects with the same setting.
choices.explanation: The default encryption key applies to new writes. It does not change A's permissions required to decrypt existing objects.

choices.text: Allow B's ingestion role to decrypt in A's KMS key policy, and allow kms:Decrypt for the target key in B's ingestion role.
choices.explanation: For cross-account access, the key-owning account must allow the use, and the caller's IAM policy must also allow use of the key.

learning.reason: For cross-account access, the key-owning account must allow the use, and the caller's IAM policy must also allow use of the key.
learning.concept: Cross-account decryption requires permission on both the key and IAM sides

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Prevent administrators from deleting protected versions during the retention period
prompt: An S3 bucket used to store audit trails has versioning enabled. Each version of the target objects must be retained for seven years from creation, and neither deletion nor shortening the retention period may be possible even through an administrator's mistake. No storage location other than the bucket may be used. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Configure only an S3 legal hold, grant operations administrators permission to remove it, and ask them to remove it after seven years.
choices.explanation: If administrators have permission to remove the legal hold, they can release it early, so this does not meet the requirement that the fixed retention period cannot be changed.

choices.text: Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode and configure a seven-year retention period for the target versions.
choices.explanation: During the retention period, even a user with high-level administrative privileges cannot delete that version or shorten the configured retention period.

choices.text: Use S3 Object Lock in governance mode and grant administrators a bypass permission that allows them to override the retention settings.
choices.explanation: The bypass permission would allow deletion or modification during the retention period, so this does not meet the requirement.

choices.text: Keep versioning enabled and enable MFA Delete so that administrators can delete versions within seven years if they have MFA.
choices.explanation: This does not enforce the length of the retention period and allows an administrator who satisfies the authentication requirement to delete versions.

learning.reason: During the retention period, even a user with high-level administrative privileges cannot delete that version or shorten the configured retention period.
learning.concept: Committed retention using S3 Object Lock compliance mode

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Allow decryption only through S3
prompt: A report-retrieval role reads files encrypted with a customer managed KMS key in S3 in the Tokyo Region. The required S3 GetObject permission is already granted. You are reviewing the permissions for the same key and must allow only the decryption that S3 performs on the role's behalf as part of reading the object. No other decryption permission exists. Which condition should be added?

choices.text: Specify the Tokyo Region with aws:RequestedRegion and use only that condition to distinguish direct Decrypt calls from calls made through S3.
choices.explanation: The requested Region can be checked, but this condition cannot distinguish a direct KMS call by the role in the same Region from one made through S3.

choices.text: Add a GetObject condition to the S3 bucket policy and leave an unconditional Decrypt permission for the same role on the KMS key.
choices.explanation: A GetObject restriction does not control authorization for requests that the role sends directly to KMS.

choices.text: Limit the decryption permission to requests for which kms:ViaService matches the S3 service in the Tokyo Region.
choices.explanation: This distinguishes KMS calls made by the service on the user's behalf from calls sent directly by the role.

choices.text: Limit the decryption permission to KMS requests that use TLS and allow clients other than S3 to use the same condition.
choices.explanation: Checking the encrypted transport path does not determine whether the KMS request came from S3's delegated operation.

learning.reason: This distinguishes KMS calls made by the service on the user's behalf from calls sent directly by the role.
learning.concept: Restricting access to an integrated service through kms:ViaService

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Reject noncompliant template deployments and detect drift created through other paths
prompt: In Control Tower, for the same security requirement, noncompliant resource creation through CloudFormation must be rejected proactively, while drift caused by existing resources or changes made through the console must be detected. Multiple controls correspond to the requirements being used. Which combination is appropriate? Select two.

choices.text: Retrieve the audit report for the target service from AWS Artifact and compare the report's issue date when deploying the template.
choices.explanation: An AWS audit report does not evaluate the configuration of each customer's resources when they are created or afterward.

choices.text: Standardize target resource names using only an Organizations tag policy and replace configuration-compliance checks with it.
choices.explanation: Standardizing resource names or tags does not evaluate whether the specified security settings are compliant before or after provisioning.

choices.text: Keep snapshots for a long time in the Config delivery channel and use that same Config delivery alone to reject noncompliant CloudFormation creation.
choices.explanation: A configuration that stores evaluation data does not reject creation before a resource is created through CloudFormation.

choices.text: Enable a proactive control that evaluates target creation through CloudFormation.
choices.explanation: Evaluation through a CloudFormation hook can cause a noncompliant configuration to fail before provisioning.

choices.text: Enable a detective control that records drift in the target resources.
choices.explanation: Because it evaluates the state of actual target resources, it can cover changes made through paths other than CloudFormation.

learning.reason: Evaluation through a CloudFormation hook can cause a noncompliant configuration to fail before provisioning. Because detective controls evaluate the state of actual target resources, they can also cover changes made through paths other than CloudFormation.
learning.concept: Predeployment checks with proactive controls and evaluation with detective controls

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Restrict use of new Regions only for a specific OU
prompt: Production accounts in the regulated OU of Control Tower must not be able to use regional workloads outside the approved Regions. The testing environment in a different OU and required global services such as IAM must not be affected. What should be configured centrally?

choices.text: Change the default Region in the console for each account in the regulated OU and make regional APIs follow the default.
choices.explanation: The console default displayed to users is not a permissions boundary that enforces the Region specified by the CLI or SDK.

choices.text: Apply a Region deny control to the regulated OU and verify exceptions for the approved Regions and required global services.
choices.explanation: This applies a regional boundary only to part of the organization and distinguishes required operations that are not suitable for regional restrictions.

choices.text: Configure the target Regions of the AWS Config aggregator to include only the approved list and deny APIs outside that list.
choices.explanation: Config collection scope does not remove the permission to run APIs in each account.

choices.text: Apply Region deny across the entire landing zone and standardize the testing OU on the same Region list as production.
choices.explanation: This would also affect the testing environment in the other OU and would not restrict only the regulated targets.

learning.reason: This applies a regional boundary only to part of the organization and distinguishes required operations that are not suitable for regional restrictions.
learning.concept: OU-level Region deny and handling global services

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Apply organizational WAF protection to new public ALBs
prompt: A company manages public ALBs across multiple member accounts. The Firewall Manager administrator and all required prerequisites are already configured. In addition to existing ALBs, the company must apply the organization-wide AWS WAF rules to ALBs in the target OUs that are created in the future, without waiting for individual business teams to respond. What should be configured?

choices.text: Use the organization’s CloudTrail to record ALB creation in every account and associate a shared Web ACL only when creation is detected.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail records creation operations, but it does not configure automatic application of organizational WAF protection.

choices.text: Include each member account in an AWS Config aggregator and store the Web ACL rule definitions as aggregator settings.
choices.explanation: An aggregator collects configuration and compliance data; it does not deploy WAF rules or associations.

choices.text: Create a Firewall Manager AWS WAF policy with ALB as the resource type and apply automatic remediation to the target OUs.
choices.explanation: This applies centrally defined protection to resources within the defined scope and can automatically handle new target resources.

choices.text: Create one Web ACL only in the administrator account and assume that it is initially associated with every ALB in the organization.
choices.explanation: Creating an individual Web ACL does not automatically apply a common policy to new resources throughout the organization.

learning.reason: This applies centrally defined protection to resources within the defined scope and can automatically handle new target resources.
learning.concept: Scope of Firewall Manager AWS WAF policies and automatic remediation

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Find untagged resources separately from tag-value compliance reports
prompt: An organization manages the permitted values for the CostCenter tag through a basic tag-value compliance policy. Some existing EC2 instances do not have the CostCenter key at all, and the organization wants to continuously detect and list them. The tag-value policy must remain in place. What should be added?

choices.text: Specify the CostCenter tag as a resource search criterion and treat all matching instances as the list of untagged resources.
choices.explanation: A list matching a tag condition contains resources that have the tag; it does not identify missing tags.

choices.text: Create OUs with the same names as the permitted values, move the relevant accounts into them, and expect CostCenter to be inherited automatically by EC2 instances in those accounts.
choices.explanation: Changing an account’s OU membership does not automatically add CostCenter to existing EC2 instances.

choices.text: Add an AWS Config required-tag rule that evaluates whether EC2 instances have the CostCenter key.
choices.explanation: In addition to standardizing values that are present, this can detect existing resources for which the key itself is missing.

choices.text: Restrict the permitted CostCenter values to one value and expect instances without the tag to become noncompliant under the same evaluation.
choices.explanation: Basic tag-value compliance evaluates the specified tag when it exists and does not comprehensively cover existing instances with the tag missing.

learning.reason: In addition to standardizing values that are present, this can detect existing resources for which the key itself is missing.
learning.concept: Tag-value compliance and detecting missing tags on existing resources

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Let staff deploy only approved configurations through self-service
prompt: A platform team provides business units with AWS Service Catalog products whose encryption and logging settings are fixed. Staff must be able to launch the products, but they must not be able to create or modify the underlying resources directly at will. What should be configured?

choices.text: Place only template constraints on the Service Catalog product and grant all users permission to create resources directly.
choices.explanation: Template inputs can be restricted, but permissions granted directly to users are not limited to launching the product.

choices.text: Grant users broad create permissions for CloudFormation and the relevant AWS services, and instruct them in documentation to use those permissions only through the product.
choices.explanation: Documentation-based restrictions cannot prevent users from creating resources directly through APIs unrelated to the product.

choices.text: Share the Service Catalog portfolio as read-only and have business units deploy the original CloudFormation template with administrator permissions.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the requirement to permit self-service use of the product while separating users from the permissions used behind it.

choices.text: Attach a launch constraint to the product and have Service Catalog use a launch role with the permissions required for creation.
choices.explanation: The permissions required to launch the product are placed on the execution side, while users’ direct permissions can be limited to Service Catalog operations.

learning.reason: The permissions required to launch the product are placed on the execution side, while users’ direct permissions can be limited to Service Catalog operations.
learning.concept: Launch roles used for deployment and permissions for product users

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Assemble the cloud provider’s audit report and evidence of controls in the organization’s environment
prompt: An auditor separately requests AWS’s SOC report for the audit period and evidence that encryption requirements were operated in the company’s own accounts. In both cases, only authorized staff may obtain the evidence. Which two actions are appropriate? Select two.

choices.text: Save the history of accepting the service agreement with AWS and use it as the complete record of all AWS-side and company-side activities during the period.
choices.explanation: The record of accepting an agreement is separate from an audit report or resource evidence showing that controls were implemented.

choices.text: Obtain only this month’s AWS bill and use the charges to prove users’ encryption settings and AWS’s audit results.
choices.explanation: Billing amounts do not provide evidence of the audit results for the services involved or of individual encryption controls.

choices.text: Use only the SOC report from AWS Artifact to prove that encryption was enabled for every S3 bucket in the company’s accounts.
choices.explanation: An AWS-side report does not guarantee the configuration values of each resource managed by an individual customer.

choices.text: Compile the encryption status and remediation records for the company’s accounts from implementation records such as configuration evaluation results.
choices.explanation: This can explain the customer-side controls actually applied in the company’s environment and associate them with the audit period.

choices.text: Obtain from AWS Artifact the SOC report covering the appropriate audit period and service scope.
choices.explanation: This provides the third-party report on AWS-side controls relevant to the audit.

learning.reason: This provides the third-party report on AWS-side controls relevant to the audit. It can also explain the customer-side controls actually applied in the company’s environment and associate them with the audit period.
learning.concept: AWS Artifact reports and customer-maintained control evidence

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Preventing S3 Mispermissions to External Accounts at the Organization Level
prompt: An OU in an organization contains S3 buckets for sensitive data. Even if a member administrator accidentally allows an external IAM principal in a bucket policy, an organization-level boundary is required to prevent the external principal from performing the targeted S3 operations. How should this be implemented?

choices.text: Change the bucket names to an internally sensitive naming convention and leave bucket policies that allow external principals enabled.
choices.explanation: A bucket name is not evaluated as an authorization trust boundary and does not invalidate an incorrect Allow.

choices.text: Apply a resource control policy to the S3 resources in the target OU that denies the targeted operations from external IAM principals.
choices.explanation: An RCP limits how resources in the organization can be used and can be evaluated for requests from external principals.

choices.text: Detect external sharing with an AWS Config aggregator in the target OU and assume that external access is automatically stopped until the detection result is produced.
choices.explanation: Aggregating detection results does not cause access to be denied during the preceding authorization evaluation.

choices.text: Use only an SCP in the target OU to control the permissions of IAM principals that do not belong to member accounts.
choices.explanation: An SCP constrains principals in the organization’s target accounts; it does not directly constrain external IAM principals.

learning.reason: An RCP limits the use of target resources in the organization and can be evaluated for requests from external principals.
learning.concept: RCPs that protect organizational resources and SCPs that constrain organizational principals

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Separating OS and Application Update Responsibilities in the Execution Plan
prompt: You operate standard Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL and a business application that you deployed yourself on EC2. You must assign responsibility for OS patches and for updating the database driver embedded in the application. Which division of responsibility is appropriate?

choices.text: A user who can connect to the instance directly logs in to the standard RDS underlying OS and performs the same patching procedure as for EC2.
choices.explanation: For standard RDS, the provider operates the underlying OS; users do not directly manage its guest OS.

choices.text: AWS manages the underlying OS of standard RDS, while the user manages the EC2 guest OS and the driver in the user’s own application.
choices.explanation: Unlike the infrastructure of a managed database, the OS on EC2 and dependencies embedded by the user remain within the user’s management scope.

choices.text: Because both RDS and EC2 are used as AWS services, AWS manages both operating systems and the driver in the user’s application.
choices.explanation: Management of the EC2 guest OS and dependencies in the user’s application does not transfer to AWS.

choices.text: The user updates the driver on EC2, but AWS updates both the EC2 guest OS and the underlying OS of standard RDS.
choices.explanation: Unlike the underlying OS of standard RDS, the EC2 guest OS is within the user’s update responsibility.

learning.reason: Unlike the infrastructure of a managed database, the OS on EC2 and dependencies embedded by the user remain within the user’s management scope.
learning.concept: Infrastructure operations for managed services and guest OS management on EC2

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Deploying the Same Configuration Evaluations and Remediation Definitions Across an Organization
prompt: You operate the same AWS Config rules and remediation actions in multiple accounts in an organization. There is one target Region, and each account has already recorded the required configuration. How can you manage-version the template in the management account and deploy it to the target accounts in one operation?

choices.text: Add the rules only to the management account’s Config recorder and use the management account’s evaluation results as a substitute for the state of all member accounts.
choices.explanation: Recording only in the management account does not create rules or remediation settings in each member account.

choices.text: Configure all accounts to use the same aggregator with an AWS Config aggregator and have the aggregation configuration distribute the rules and remediation definitions.
choices.explanation: An aggregator is intended to read recorded configurations and evaluation results; it does not deploy definitions to member accounts.

choices.text: Define the rules and remediation actions in a conformance pack and deploy it to the member accounts in the target Region through AWS Config organization operations.
choices.explanation: This expands the rules and remediation definitions as one template unit and reduces manual configuration for each account.

choices.text: List the rule names and remediation actions in an Organizations backup policy and create AWS Config rules with the same names in each account.
choices.explanation: A backup policy manages backup plans; it does not deploy AWS Config rules or remediation actions.

learning.reason: The rules and remediation definitions can be deployed as one template unit, reducing manual configuration for each account.
learning.concept: AWS Config organization conformance packs in Organizations

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Reflecting Updates to Existing Findings in Tickets More Quickly
prompt: GuardDuty sends the initial detection to EventBridge immediately, but updating a ticket takes several hours after additional occurrences are added to the same finding. There are no suppression rules, and the ticket-processing operation itself completes immediately. What should be adjusted while keeping the detection target and ticketing unit unchanged?

choices.text: Periodically replay the original event from the EventBridge archive.
choices.explanation: The initial event does not include later occurrence counts, so replaying it does not configure notifications for the latest state.

choices.text: Reconfigure GuardDuty so that the finding ID changes, and create a new ticket for every recurrence.
choices.explanation: This removes the requirement to append the same finding to the existing ticket.

choices.text: Shorten the notification frequency for GuardDuty finding updates.
choices.explanation: Later occurrences of the same finding are notified at the configured frequency. They are handled separately from the initial notification.

choices.text: Shorten the maximum event age for the EventBridge target.
choices.explanation: This is the retry deadline when delivery fails; it does not control when GuardDuty issues an update.

learning.reason: Later occurrences of the same finding are notified at the configured frequency and are handled separately from the initial notification.
learning.concept: Notification intervals for new findings and recurrences of the same finding

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Detecting new vulnerabilities in existing images without repushing them
prompt: In a release Amazon ECR repository, the digests of deployed images must not change. You want existing eligible images to be evaluated automatically when vulnerability information is published later, and you want findings for the operating system and supported language packages in use. The images are within the scanning period. Which two settings should you configure? Select two.

choices.text: Choose scan-on-push only for enhanced scanning and extend the finding retention period.
choices.explanation: Retaining historical findings does not cause continued reevaluation when new vulnerability information is published.

choices.text: Configure a continuous scanning filter that matches the target repository.
choices.explanation: Inspector can reevaluate the target images and obtain findings based on newly published vulnerability information.

choices.text: Make image tags immutable and use adding a signature as a substitute for scanning.
choices.explanation: Immutable tags and signatures help identify and authenticate artifacts, but they do not inspect packages.

choices.text: Choose enhanced scanning with Amazon Inspector in the ECR registry.
choices.explanation: It can evaluate packages for both supported operating systems and programming languages.

choices.text: Enable only basic scan-on-push scanning and do not push the images again afterward.
choices.explanation: Scan-on-push evaluation does not provide continued evaluation based on information published later.

learning.reason: It can evaluate packages for both supported operating systems and programming languages. Inspector can reevaluate the target images and obtain findings based on newly published vulnerability information.
learning.concept: Continuous enhanced scanning with Amazon Inspector and ECR

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Investigating unused permissions through an organization-wide inventory
prompt: The security team wants to identify IAM roles and service permissions that have not been used in the past 90 days as candidates across the organization. External-sharing analysis is already in operation, and detected items must be sent to an assigned reviewer rather than having permissions deleted automatically. Which setting should you add?

choices.text: Run IAM policy validation on every role with permissions and treat the number of validation warnings as the unused period.
choices.explanation: Policy-document validation results do not show whether the permissions were actually used.

choices.text: Create an organization-wide unused access analyzer and set the activity-history evaluation period to 90 days.
choices.explanation: It reports candidates based on usage history and leaves the deletion decision to people.

choices.text: Set the CloudTrail retention period to 90 days and extract only roles that have never used a particular trail.
choices.explanation: Trail configuration alone does not analyze unused IAM permissions across the organization.

choices.text: Narrow the trust zone of the organization's external access analyzer and determine unused status solely from external-sharing settings.
choices.explanation: Whether resources permit external access is separate from usage history for identities and permissions within the organization.

learning.reason: It reports candidates based on usage history and leaves the deletion decision to people.
learning.concept: Organization-wide unused access analyzers and evaluation periods

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Determining whether an IAM principal was authenticated in EKS
prompt: In EKS, access to the Kubernetes API from a specific IAM role is failing. Control plane logs are enabled for the cluster. Before investigating Kubernetes RBAC authorization, you want to examine the processing from the IAM principal through Kubernetes authentication. Which log should you check first?

choices.text: Check the EKS control plane authenticator log.
choices.explanation: This log is used to examine the result of cluster authentication using IAM credentials and how the principal was handled.

choices.text: Check the scheduler log and treat the request as an authentication failure if no node is assigned to the IAM role.
choices.explanation: The scheduler determines Pod placement; it does not process user IAM authentication.

choices.text: Check only VPC Flow Logs and conclude that a source that established a TCP connection also passed IAM authentication.
choices.explanation: Network reachability can be determined, but the authentication result for the IAM principal cannot.

choices.text: Check only the controllerManager log and infer the login identity from resource reconciliation.
choices.explanation: Controller reconciliation and cluster-user authentication are separate processes.

learning.reason: This log is used to examine the result of cluster authentication using IAM credentials and how the principal was handled.
learning.concept: EKS authenticator logs and Kubernetes API audit logs

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Immediately notifying operations of emergency root use
prompt: Long-term CloudTrail trails for retention also deliver management events to CloudWatch Logs. When an operation by the root user is detected, the responsible staff must be notified without waiting for a daily review. Operations whose role session name merely resembles root must not be included. What should you configure?

choices.text: Create a metric filter that identifies root by the principal type in CloudTrail events, and send notifications from a CloudWatch alarm.
choices.explanation: Because it uses the principal type recorded in the operation log, it can detect root activity without relying on a simple string match against the session name.

choices.text: Extend the CloudWatch log-retention period and notify only when the number of retained days exceeds a threshold.
choices.explanation: Log retention and detecting the occurrence of a new root operation are independent concerns.

choices.text: Match the substring root in all IAM role session names and notify the matching count.
choices.explanation: Role session names are distinct from the root-user classification, which can cause false notifications or missed detections.

choices.text: Notify only when CloudTrail Insights detects an unusually high operation volume, and use the same condition to detect a single root operation.
choices.explanation: Detecting an anomalous operation volume is different from recording one operation by a particular principal type.

learning.reason: Because it uses the principal type recorded in the operation log, it can detect root activity without relying on a simple string match against the session name.
learning.concept: Metric filters based on the principal type in CloudTrail

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Distinguishing DNS query logs from endpoint query counts
prompt: Route 53 Resolver query logging is correctly associated with the development VPC. During an audit, the same name was queried repeatedly within a short period, but the queries made while the name was already cached do not appear individually. How should the reported count be interpreted?

choices.text: Treat the number of records in the stored DNS logs as the total number of queries and regard the missing records as evidence that no communication occurred.
choices.explanation: Some queries may have been resolved from the cache, so the absence of a record alone does not prove that no query was made.

choices.text: Queries answered by Resolver from its cache are not included in the logs. Client-side measurement is required to count all calls.
choices.explanation: Resolver query logs are not a complete record of every call, including cache hits.

choices.text: When caching is enabled, the query log contains no entries at all, including the first query for a name.
choices.explanation: A query for a name that is not yet cached is still subject to logging.

choices.text: Extending the log group retention period will preserve all queries that were previously answered from the cache.
choices.explanation: Retention applies to events that were collected; it cannot restore records that were never generated.

learning.reason: Resolver query logs are not a complete record of every call, including cache hits.
learning.concept: The recording scope of Resolver query logs and cached DNS responses

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Retrieving the details at the time of a large configuration change
prompt: A resource-change notification received from AWS Config contains only a configuration item summary and identifying information when the configuration is large. The audit record requires the complete configuration at the time of the notification, and the configuration may be updated again later. Which method should be used to retrieve it?

choices.text: Infer the possible configuration after the notification from the resource name and the Config rule compliance result, and use that inference as the audit record.
choices.explanation: A compliance decision and a name cannot reconstruct the recorded configuration values.

choices.text: Call a Describe operation for the target AWS service later and save the current values as the original change.
choices.explanation: If another change occurred before the investigation, the current values will not match the configuration at notification time.

choices.text: Create another SNS topic and redeliver the notification until the same summary arrives, then reconstruct the complete configuration.
choices.explanation: Receiving the same type of summary multiple times does not add the missing detailed data.

choices.text: Use the resource identifier and capture time in the notification to locate the corresponding point in AWS Config configuration history.
choices.explanation: Even when the notification cannot contain the complete configuration, the historical configuration item recorded by Config can be examined.

learning.reason: Even when the notification cannot contain the complete configuration, the historical configuration item recorded by Config can be examined.
learning.concept: AWS Config oversized notifications and the configuration timeline

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Restricting subscription creation for a central log destination to a specified organization
prompt: The receiving account has a CloudWatch Logs destination and a Kinesis stream as its delivery destination. The sending account has the IAM permission to create a subscription in the same Region, but it cannot use the destination from another account. How can the receiving account allow only sending accounts from a specified organization?

choices.text: Add only Kinesis read permission to the sending account and leave the log destination policy unchanged.
choices.explanation: Permission to read the delivery stream is separate from permission to use the CloudWatch Logs logical destination.

choices.text: Disallow subscriptions to the destination and register the other account's log group as a subscription source in a query saved in the receiving account.
choices.explanation: Sharing a query does not authorize a cross-account subscription.

choices.text: Add permission to create subscriptions to the logical destination's access policy, restricting the sending principals to the specified organization.
choices.explanation: The destination authorizes the eligible sending accounts, which can then create subscriptions together with the sending-side permissions.

choices.text: Extend the CloudWatch Logs retention period in the receiving account so that sending logs from the organization are included automatically.
choices.explanation: Retention does not change whether a sending account is authorized to use the destination.

learning.reason: The destination authorizes the eligible sending accounts, which can then create subscriptions together with the sending-side permissions.
learning.concept: Access policies for cross-account log destinations

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Receiving malware scan results without changing file tags
prompt: GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3 is being used. By policy, the tags of ingested objects cannot be changed by the scanning process. Even under this constraint, the organization must receive results for successful scans, errors, and scans that could not be performed, and track the status in a separate ledger. What should it receive?

choices.text: Receive the GuardDuty S3 object scan result event indicating completion through EventBridge, and record the target object and status.
choices.explanation: The result event can be processed without setting object tags.

choices.text: If the inspection plan is Active, treat every individual object as having been scanned successfully.
choices.explanation: The plan status does not provide the scan result for an individual object.

choices.text: Monitor only S3 ObjectCreated events and always regard an object as scanned successfully and safe immediately after arrival.
choices.explanation: An upload event does not indicate that scanning is complete or what its result means.

choices.text: Require the GuardDuty Malware Protection tag and treat objects whose tags cannot be written as successfully scanned.
choices.explanation: This violates the constraint that tags cannot be changed and missing tags cannot establish a successful scan.

learning.reason: The result event can be processed without setting object tags.
learning.concept: Scan-completion events and optional scan-result tags

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Distinguishing notified findings from compliance status
prompt: In Security Hub CSPM, a noncompliant control finding has been reported to the responsible person. The configuration has not yet been changed. Which field should be updated to retain the noncompliant assessment while recording operationally that the responsible person has been notified?

choices.text: Set Workflow.Status to NOTIFIED.
choices.explanation: This records the investigation tracking status without changing the control's technical compliance assessment.

choices.text: Change Compliance.Status to PASSED.
choices.explanation: This would treat an unrepaired configuration as passing, which is different from updating the workflow to indicate that it was notified.

choices.text: Set RecordState to ARCHIVED and remove the historical finding from the default response scope.
choices.explanation: Changing the storage state does not record a notification status for tracking an unresolved finding.

choices.text: Set Workflow.Status to RESOLVED and record that remediation was completed when the notification was sent.
choices.explanation: Sending a notification alone does not resolve the issue, so this would not reflect the fact that further action is still required.

learning.reason: Record the investigation tracking status without changing the control's technical compliance assessment.
learning.concept: Security Hub CSPM finding workflow and technical compliance assessment

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Investigating management operations older than 90 days
prompt: An S3 bucket used for auditing retains CloudTrail trail logs for one year. You need to extract events for a management operation reported 130 days ago across multiple Regions, filtering by ARN and time period. Which approach should you use without modifying the original files?

choices.text: Set the start date in CloudTrail event history to 130 days ago and remove only the Region filter.
choices.explanation: Event history is retained for 90 days, so broadening the time filter cannot search earlier events.

choices.text: Run an advanced query against the current configuration in AWS Config and retrieve the calling principal and operation time.
choices.explanation: A current-configuration query does not return logs of historical API operations.

choices.text: Disable and re-enable CloudTrail once starting today and have the 130-day-old events redistributed to the current trail.
choices.explanation: Enabling a trail does not regenerate past events. You must investigate the logs already stored in S3.

choices.text: Define an Athena table for the CloudTrail logs in S3 and filter them by time and target identifiers.
choices.explanation: Because the original logs for the relevant period are available, they can be investigated without relying on the event history display period.

learning.reason: Because the original logs for the relevant period are available, they can be investigated without relying on the event history display period.
learning.concept: Investigating stored CloudTrail logs with Athena

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Urgently shortening the usable period of issued download URLs
prompt: A presigned URL for a prepublication-materials prefix in S3 was configured to remain valid for one hour and was forwarded outside the company. You need to reject new downloads for that prefix when more than five minutes have elapsed since the URL was signed. The credentials used for signing are also used for other business operations. Which control is appropriate?

choices.text: Use the S3 lifecycle configuration to expire the target objects after five minutes and reject only URLs issued before expiration.
choices.explanation: A lifecycle configuration does not evaluate elapsed time for each signature and would unnecessarily delete the data itself.

choices.text: Disable the credentials used for signing across all operations and switch all prefixes other than the target prefix to different credentials.
choices.explanation: Although this could invalidate old URLs, it violates the requirement to keep the credentials available for other business operations.

choices.text: Restrict the policy to the target objects and presigned URL request pattern, and use an S3 policy to deny downloads for which s3:signatureAge exceeds five minutes.
choices.explanation: The request-time evaluation of signature age can target old URLs while avoiding impact on different prefixes.

choices.text: Change the URL validity period in the issuing application to five minutes from the next issuance onward and leave issued URLs unchanged.
choices.explanation: This shortens the expiration of future signatures but does not reject URLs that have already been issued.

learning.reason: Because signature age is evaluated when the request is made, old URLs can be targeted without affecting different prefixes.
learning.concept: Using s3:signatureAge to limit elapsed time since signing

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Managing a member-account incident in a dedicated security account
prompt: The organization uses AWS Security Incident Response. Incident management must be centralized in a dedicated security account, and responders must not receive everyday access to the organization's management account. Which configuration should be selected when enabling the service for the organization?

choices.text: Grant all incident responders administrator permissions in the Organizations management account and make the dedicated account read-only.
choices.explanation: This concentrates the permissions needed to handle cases in the management account, contrary to the requirement.

choices.text: Have each account create cases independently and copy case details outside the organization whenever responders change.
choices.explanation: This does not provide organization-wide case management through the dedicated account and disperses permissions and tracking.

choices.text: Share the central CloudTrail log bucket with the dedicated account and make that account the case manager solely through the sharing configuration.
choices.explanation: Log sharing and delegated administration of the incident response service are separate configurations.

choices.text: Designate the dedicated security account as the delegated administrator from the Organizations management account and manage cases in the dedicated account.
choices.explanation: This separates organization-level enablement from responders' day-to-day case management in another account.

learning.reason: Organization-level enablement and responders' day-to-day case management can be performed in different accounts.
learning.concept: Delegated administration and case management in AWS Security Incident Response

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Continue automated incident diagnosis while requiring approval only for isolation
prompt: A Systems Manager Automation runbook investigates where evidence is located after an incident alarm. Evidence queries must run automatically, and the subsequent step that isolates the production host must run only after approval from designated personnel. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Notify the designated personnel through SNS during diagnosis, then verify only that the notification was sent successfully immediately before isolation.
choices.explanation: Sending a message does not mean that isolation was approved.

choices.text: Keep diagnosis and isolation in order, but wait a fixed amount of time before performing isolation.
choices.explanation: The passage of a waiting period does not satisfy the condition that designated personnel granted approval.

choices.text: Place aws:approve after diagnosis and proceed to the isolation action only when approval from designated personnel succeeds.
choices.explanation: Human approval becomes an execution condition within the runbook, preventing isolation from proceeding based only on a notification.

choices.text: Restrict the execution role's permissions to diagnosis and assume that isolation permissions will be added automatically only when designated personnel approve in chat.
choices.explanation: Unless authorization and approval processing are implemented in the runbook, an external statement cannot serve as an execution condition.

learning.reason: Human approval can be made an execution condition within the runbook, preventing isolation from proceeding based only on a notification.
learning.concept: Controlling branching and approvers with Automation aws:approve

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Distinguish restore-job success from successful recovery of business data
prompt: In an AWS Backup restore test, a DB can be created in an isolated environment. However, the team's pass criteria require not only that the DB can start, but also that it pass an integrity check against baseline data. How should the business validation result be recorded in the existing restore-test result?

choices.text: Treat the business validation as successful when the restore job is COMPLETED, and do not query the restored resource.
choices.explanation: Being able to create the restored resource is separate from confirming that the required business data is valid.

choices.text: Remove the isolation controls, send production traffic to the restored DB first, and record the test only if it fails.
choices.explanation: This would affect users and would not satisfy the isolation and pre-validation requirements of a restore test.

choices.text: Trigger validation in the isolated environment when restoration completes, and report the result to AWS Backup as the validation status of the target restore job.
choices.explanation: This distinguishes infrastructure restoration success from post-restore data-validation success within the same test result.

choices.text: Run the same query against the original production DB and report it as the result of validating the restored instance.
choices.explanation: Success on the original DB does not confirm that the restored contents are correct and usable.

learning.reason: Infrastructure restoration success and post-restore data-validation success can be distinguished within the same test result.
learning.concept: Additional validation status for a restore job

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Prevent a confirmed compromised image from being restarted
prompt: The digest of an image deployed in a production ECS service has been confirmed to correspond to a modified artifact. The affected tasks have been isolated and evidence preserved. What should be done to restore the customer-facing service and ensure that the same artifact is not started during scale-out?

choices.text: Delete the image using a method that cannot preserve its history, wait for ECS to fail to start, and do not deploy a verified image.
choices.explanation: This preserves neither evidence nor availability and does not create a new deployment specification for recovery.

choices.text: Restart tasks without stopping them using the current task definition and check whether the suspicious changes disappear while retaining the same digest.
choices.explanation: Because the artifact itself is compromised, restarting the same image does not remove the cause.

choices.text: Deploy a task definition that references a different, safety-verified digest, and confirm that tasks using the old digest are no longer running.
choices.explanation: This replaces the deployment artifact that was the source of the compromise, so rescheduling can use a healthy specification.

choices.text: Manually restore files only in the running containers and leave the task definition's referenced image unchanged.
choices.explanation: Changing only existing tasks means that subsequent tasks will still start from the compromised artifact.

learning.reason: Replace the deployment artifact that was the source of the compromise so that rescheduling also uses a healthy specification.
learning.concept: Investigated deployment artifacts and redeployment with verified integrity

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Safely verify that the isolation runbook actually starts
prompt: A tabletop exercise has confirmed roles and contact information. Next, the organization must verify the behavior from ingesting a detection event through the isolation runbook's permissions and the evidence it produces. The organization can use a dedicated test account and synthetic events. What should it do?

choices.text: Inject representative events into a reproduction environment limited to the test scope, then compare the success criteria from startup through the isolation result and records.
choices.explanation: This exercises the notification, permission, and runbook integration points without changing production resources.

choices.text: Make an arbitrary production instance the isolation target and let everyone try the procedure without limiting the targets.
choices.explanation: This creates unnecessary impact on production hosts when a test environment is available.

choices.text: Perform only a syntax check on the runbook and treat the exercise as complete without executing event delivery or isolation actions.
choices.explanation: A syntax check cannot confirm that the flow from detection through actual processing works.

choices.text: Add only another tabletop exercise without execution and determine whether the related API permissions are effective from the diagram.
choices.explanation: This may be suitable for confirming operational decisions, but it does not provide evidence that the event rule or execution role works.

learning.reason: Execute the integration points for notifications, permissions, and the runbook in a test environment without changing production resources.
learning.concept: Technical incident-response exercises in a test environment

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Reprocess only the missed incident events from the affected time period
prompt: The event bus used for incident notifications has archived events in advance. You need only the corrected aggregation rule to reprocess the stored events from the affected time period. The other rules have already processed the same events, and duplicate notifications must be avoided. What should you do?

choices.text: Create only a new EventBridge rule and wait for the archived events from the specified period to arrive automatically.
choices.explanation: Creating a new rule does not start a replay from the archive.

choices.text: Specify the incident time period and replay the events while limiting the destination to the corrected aggregation rule on that event bus.
choices.explanation: Restricting both the time range and the destination delivers the historical events only to the corrected processing path.

choices.text: Delete the archive, recreate it with the same settings, and retrieve the old events from the new archive.
choices.explanation: Creating a new archive does not restore historical events that were already present in the previous archive.

choices.text: Replay the events to the original bus for all rules and delete duplicate rule results afterward.
choices.explanation: Unnecessary rules would rerun side effects such as notifications.

learning.reason: Restricting both the time range and the destination delivers the historical events only to the corrected processing path.
learning.concept: Specifying the archive time range and replay destination rule

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Hand off a copy of the evidence to the investigators
prompt: The team has collected logs and metadata for an incident investigation. Subsequent queries must not modify the originals, and the team must be able to verify who collected and transferred the evidence and whether the copy matches the content at the time of preservation. Select the three steps, in order, to protect the collected originals before beginning the investigation.

choices.text: Proceed with the analysis using the verified investigation copy.
choices.explanation: Using a verified copy for the investigation prevents analysis changes from affecting the originals.

choices.text: Delete unnecessary rows from the originals to make them easier to investigate, and treat that state as the only preserved version.
choices.explanation: Changing the originals compromises their integrity as records of what was collected.

choices.text: Record the identifiers of the originals, the collectors, and the collection times, then store the originals in a protected repository.
choices.explanation: This preserves the starting point for later verifying the provenance and identity of the transferred evidence.

choices.text: Create an investigation copy and verify that it matches the original content and that the transfer records are complete.
choices.explanation: Before beginning the investigation, verify that the copy accurately reflects the preserved evidence.

learning.reason: Preserve the starting point for verifying the provenance and identity of the transferred evidence. Before beginning the investigation, verify that the copy accurately reflects the preserved evidence. Use a verified copy for the investigation to prevent analysis changes from affecting the originals.
learning.concept: Evidence preservation, an identity-verified copy, and analysis that does not modify the originals

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Apply a per-source limit only to the authentication path
prompt: A public service is associated with AWS WAF. Apply a limit per source IP only to authentication requests. Traffic from the same IP to static resources must not be included in the limit calculation. AWS WAF can access the correct source IP. Which configuration should you choose?

choices.text: Observe authentication requests with the WAF Count action and do not add a rate-based condition.
choices.explanation: This observes the request count but does not enforce a limit on traffic that exceeds a threshold.

choices.text: Use a rate-based rule aggregated by IP address, with a scope-down condition that includes only the authentication-path URI.
choices.explanation: This aggregates only matching requests separately for each source IP.

choices.text: Target only the authentication path and aggregate all matching requests into one group to apply the limit.
choices.explanation: Although the path is restricted, this does not set separate limits for each source IP.

choices.text: Use an IP-based rate-based rule that includes all paths, then allow only static files in a later stage.
choices.explanation: Static files are included in the rate aggregation before the later allow decision is evaluated.

learning.reason: This aggregates only matching requests separately for each source IP.
learning.concept: The aggregation key and scope-down condition of a rate-based rule

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Prepare a viewer certificate that can be configured for CloudFront
prompt: You will provide a custom domain to CloudFront viewers. The origin is an ALB in the Tokyo Region, and the certificate for the ALB is in ACM in Tokyo. How should you enable viewer HTTPS for the custom domain?

choices.text: Add CloudFront's default hostname to the ALB certificate and do not configure a certificate for the custom domain in CloudFront.
choices.explanation: Changing the origin certificate does not cause CloudFront to present a certificate for the custom domain between the viewer and CloudFront.

choices.text: Specify the ARN of the existing certificate in Tokyo for CloudFront and assume that associating it with the origin makes it available to the viewer side as well.
choices.explanation: The Region requirements for an ACM certificate associated with the origin differ from the requirements for a viewer certificate.

choices.text: Choose redirect to HTTPS in the viewer protocol policy and leave the certificate only on the ALB.
choices.explanation: A redirect does not configure the certificate for the custom domain at CloudFront to which the client connects.

choices.text: Provision a viewer certificate in ACM in US East (N. Virginia) and associate it with CloudFront.
choices.explanation: The ACM certificate that CloudFront uses for viewer HTTPS must be in us-east-1. It is handled separately from the certificate for the ALB in Tokyo.

learning.reason: The ACM certificate that CloudFront uses for viewer HTTPS must be in us-east-1. It is handled separately from the certificate for the ALB in Tokyo.
learning.concept: Certificate Regions for CloudFront viewers and an ALB origin

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Allowing subscribers to use multiple files under the same URLs
prompt: For video delivered through CloudFront, playback loads a manifest and many media files. Only users who are entitled to view the content should be allowed to access it for a limited time. The player can handle cookies, but the URLs for individual files cannot be rewritten. Direct access to the origin is already blocked. Which approach should be adopted?

choices.text: Add the user ID to the cache key for the video and reject unauthorized users through cache separation alone.
choices.explanation: Using separate caches does not check the user's entitlement or the signature expiration time.

choices.text: Enable signing for access to the origin and configure no requirements for the individual files delivered to the CloudFront viewer.
choices.explanation: Allowing CloudFront to access the origin does not evaluate the viewer's entitlement to watch the content.

choices.text: Issue a signed URL only for the manifest URL and assume that the same signature is automatically propagated to individual file access.
choices.explanation: Being able to read the manifest does not authorize reading media at other URLs.

choices.text: After authentication, issue a signed cookie that permits the group of files under the target video path.
choices.explanation: This provides time-limited access to multiple URLs based on a cookie without adding signature parameters to each file.

learning.reason: This provides time-limited access to multiple URLs based on a cookie without adding signature parameters to each file.
learning.concept: CloudFront signed cookies for authorizing multiple restricted files

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Connecting to S3 from on premises without using the internet
prompt: EC2 instances in an application VPC currently use an S3 gateway endpoint. An on-premises process connected to the same VPC through a VPN now also needs to connect to S3 without traversing the public internet. What should be added while preserving the EC2 instances' existing routes?

choices.text: Provide an S3 interface endpoint reachable from the VPN side and the corresponding DNS configuration.
choices.explanation: A gateway endpoint is used within the source VPC, while an interface endpoint with reachable ENIs can be used from on premises.

choices.text: Add the on-premises IAM principals to the S3 gateway endpoint policy so that a route from the VPN is established automatically.
choices.explanation: Changing permissions does not add an unsupported network path to the gateway endpoint.

choices.text: Specify the gateway endpoint ID as a static next hop on the on-premises router.
choices.explanation: The ID cannot be used directly as a next hop outside the VPN, and a gateway endpoint cannot be used from outside the VPC.

choices.text: Point the existing VPC internet gateway to S3 DNS and communicate with public S3 using the on-premises private IP address.
choices.explanation: This does not provide the path through an interface endpoint for private S3 connectivity.

learning.reason: A gateway endpoint is used within the source VPC, while an interface endpoint with reachable ENIs can be used from on premises.
learning.concept: Reachability of S3 gateway and interface endpoints

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Making the Kubernetes API private from the internet
prompt: All worker nodes in an EKS cluster use the API from within the VPC. Administrators operate it from a connected corporate network. The VPC DNS and the management-side routes are already configured, and API access from public addresses is not required. What should be changed?

choices.text: Use a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy to deny pod ingress while leaving the EKS cluster's public API setting enabled.
choices.explanation: Pod application-traffic settings do not change the public reachability of the AWS-managed cluster API.

choices.text: Keep the public API enabled, specify a dummy public CIDR, and have administrators connect through the public DNS name.
choices.explanation: This does not provide an appropriate normal connection path for administrators, nor does it disable the API's public path.

choices.text: Remove only the public IP addresses from the EKS nodes while keeping the cluster's public endpoint within its current reachability range.
choices.explanation: Even when the nodes are private, the Kubernetes API's public access setting is independent.

choices.text: Enable the cluster's private endpoint and disable the public endpoint.
choices.explanation: This limits API connectivity to the VPC and connected networks. IAM and RBAC authorization continue to apply.

learning.reason: This limits API connectivity to the VPC and connected networks. IAM and RBAC authorization continue to apply.
learning.concept: Private API endpoint access for EKS

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Detecting and stopping boot with an unauthorized bootloader
prompt: Use a supported Nitro-based EC2 instance and a supported operating system. If boot files are modified, auditing after the operating system has started is too late. How can you allow boot only with a verified signing chain?

choices.text: Encrypt the root EBS volume and treat the decrypted boot files as having valid signatures whenever the volume is encrypted.
choices.explanation: Block encryption protects data at rest; it does not enforce trusted signatures for the boot chain.

choices.text: Run Systems Manager Inventory after the first boot and stop the operating system from starting if noncompliant boot files were used.
choices.explanation: Inventory after boot cannot enforce a condition before startup.

choices.text: Require IMDSv2 and use the metadata session token as the UEFI boot signature as well.
choices.explanation: Metadata tokens and signature verification of the binaries that start the operating system are independent.

choices.text: Prepare trusted signing information in the supported AMI and apply UEFI Secure Boot.
choices.explanation: UEFI can verify signatures for bootloaders and other components and reject an unexpected boot chain before startup.

learning.reason: UEFI can verify signatures for bootloaders and other components and reject an unexpected boot chain before startup.
learning.concept: EC2 UEFI Secure Boot and signature verification at boot

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Fixing the Evaluation Order for Audited Exceptions and General Denials
prompt: You operate AWS Network Firewall stateful rules across multiple rule groups. You need to apply an explicit exception only to specific business traffic and apply a general denial to everything else. Which method fixes the intended order, including across separate rule groups?

choices.text: Use action-order evaluation and fix the priority of all actions solely through the YAML order written in each group.
choices.explanation: Action order organizes rules by action type, so the written order alone does not guarantee priority across multiple groups.

choices.text: Configure a policy that uses strict order and its associated rule groups, placing exception evaluation before the general denial.
choices.explanation: Evaluation follows the configured group order and the order within each group, allowing the exception to be evaluated before the general denial is reached.

choices.text: Split the stateful rule log destinations across multiple destinations and give priority to the rules in the group that writes its logs first.
choices.explanation: The destinations for result logs do not affect the order in which rules are evaluated.

choices.text: Use strict order, but place the general denial before the exception and assume that later rules can override all denials.
choices.explanation: A matching earlier denial stops the traffic, so an exception placed later cannot be evaluated as intended.

learning.reason: Evaluation follows the configured group order and the order within each group, allowing the exception to be evaluated before the general denial is reached.
learning.concept: Strict-order stateful evaluation and rule-group priority

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Retiring Only Old TLS Protocols on a Public ALB
prompt: For the HTTPS listener of a public ALB, an audit requires that TLS 1.0 and 1.1 not be accepted. Clients support TLS 1.2 or later, and the current ACM certificate and backend configuration must remain unchanged. What should you change?

choices.text: Replace the current ACM certificate with a new certificate having the same name, without changing the listener's security policy.
choices.explanation: Updating the certificate does not specify the minimum TLS version enabled by the listener.

choices.text: Use AWS WAF to reject requests whose HTTP header says TLS 1.0.
choices.explanation: TLS version negotiation occurs before the application-layer headers and cannot be replaced by a header value.

choices.text: Change the port number of the HTTPS target group so that the minimum TLS version for client connections changes as well.
choices.explanation: The backend port and the version negotiated by clients with the listener are separate settings.

choices.text: On the ALB's HTTPS listener, select a security policy that supports only TLS 1.2 or later.
choices.explanation: The listener can restrict the TLS versions that clients can select when connecting to the ALB.

learning.reason: The listener can restrict the TLS versions that clients can select when connecting to the ALB.
learning.concept: HTTPS listener security policies and TLS negotiation

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Preventing Overwrites of Deployed Tags
prompt: You maintain release tags for distribution in a single ECR repository. Re-pushing the same release tag must be rejected, while dev-latest used for testing must remain replaceable. What should you select in the single-repository configuration?

choices.text: Select immutable tag mode and configure an exclusion filter that excludes dev-latest from immutability.
choices.explanation: This rejects tag overwrites by default while allowing the agreed-upon single tag to be overwritten.

choices.text: Make the entire repository immutable and overwrite dev-latest with a normal push to the same tag each time.
choices.explanation: Immutability applies to all tags, so overwrites of dev-latest are also rejected.
