choices.text: Make all tags mutable and attach a long retention lifecycle policy to the release tags.
choices.explanation: A retention policy manages stored data; it does not reject overwrites of existing tags.

choices.text: Make all tags mutable and assume that a tag is automatically fixed whenever a vulnerability scan starts for it at push time.
choices.explanation: Scanning and the repository setting that determines whether tags can be overwritten are independent.

learning.reason: This rejects tag overwrites by default while allowing the agreed-upon single tag to be overwritten.
learning.concept: ECR immutable tag mode and exclusion filters

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Using Temporary Storage with a Read-Only Container Root
prompt: In a Linux ECS task, you must prevent the application's main filesystem from being modified. However, the same application creates temporary files in /tmp while running. Which design meets this requirement without expanding write access across the host?

choices.text: Make the container's root filesystem read-only and mount a writable volume only at the required /tmp path.
choices.explanation: This protects the application root while isolating temporary writes to a defined mount.

choices.text: Make the root writable and tell the file-writing application the /tmp path through an environment variable.
choices.explanation: Even if the application can choose its usual storage path, this does not enforce restrictions on writes to the root.

choices.text: Make the root read-only and mount a read-only volume at /tmp as well.
choices.explanation: The application cannot create the temporary files required for operation.

choices.text: Make the image repository read-only and assume that the same file permissions apply to a started container.
choices.explanation: Registry permissions do not configure the writable layer of a running container.

learning.reason: This protects the application root while isolating temporary writes to a defined mount.
learning.concept: ECS readonlyRootFilesystem and the writable mount scope

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Separate PrivateLink connection candidates from approved connections
prompt: An internal team provides a PrivateLink endpoint service. Two specified consumer accounts must be able to request connections, but connections must not be established until the provider individually approves them. Which two settings should be configured for the endpoint service? Select two.

choices.text: Restrict the principals that can request connections to the specified consumer accounts.
choices.explanation: This limits which consumers can submit connection requests to the permitted principals.

choices.text: Enable private DNS for the endpoint service and treat a connection as approved when DNS validation succeeds.
choices.explanation: DNS name validation confirms that the provider can use the name; it does not approve each connection request.

choices.text: Allow all principals and rely only on the provider to reject requests from accounts other than the specified accounts.
choices.explanation: Accounts other than the specified ones could still submit requests, so this does not limit the request scope as required.

choices.text: Require connection approval and accept only requests that the provider has approved.
choices.explanation: Even requests from permitted principals must not be established until they are individually approved.

choices.text: Keep permission for the specified accounts but do not require connection approval, so connections are established when requested.
choices.explanation: Although the consumers are limited, connections would be established without individual approval.

learning.reason: Limit requesters to the permitted principals, and require individual approval before establishing a connection even when the request comes from a permitted principal.
learning.concept: Endpoint service settings for permitted principals and connection acceptance

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Have separate teams manage shared VPC routes and business traffic permissions
prompt: A network account shares VPC subnets using AWS RAM. Administrators in a consumer account manage their own EC2 instances and security groups. They must be able to allow traffic for a business application without being given operational permission to change the shared subnet's egress routes. Which division of responsibilities is appropriate?

choices.text: The VPC owner manages the routes, while the participant manages the business security groups it owns.
choices.explanation: The shared routes remain under the owner account's control, while the participant can manage the entry points for its own workloads.

choices.text: Transfer instance ownership between the provider and participant each time, and have one account manage both egress routes and application permissions.
choices.explanation: Ownership transfers are unnecessary and do not match the purpose of using sharing to divide responsibilities.

choices.text: Allow participants to create their own EC2 instances, but do not allow the participant account's Identity and Access Management administrators to create or manage security groups.
choices.explanation: Participants are allowed to create and manage security groups that they own.

choices.text: Grant the participant the same route-change permissions as the owner as soon as it joins AWS RAM, and allow security groups to be operated only centrally.
choices.explanation: Using a shared subnet does not delegate the owner's route-management permissions to participants.

learning.reason: Keep shared routes under the owner account's control while allowing participants to manage the entry points for their own workloads.
learning.concept: Resources that shared-subnet owners and participants can operate

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Assigning AWS permissions to Pods without broadening the worker role
prompt: Two business Pods run on supported EC2 nodes in an EKS cluster. Only one of them needs to read a restricted area in Amazon S3. You do not want to create a cluster OIDC provider or add S3 permissions to the node role. What should you configure?

choices.text: Run the Pod Identity Agent on the supported nodes and associate the target service account with a least-privilege IAM role.
choices.explanation: This separates credentials for the target Pod at the service-account level and avoids increasing node permissions.

choices.text: Use a Kubernetes RoleBinding to grant the target Pod permissions named s3:GetObject.
choices.explanation: RBAC authorizes Kubernetes operations; it does not issue AWS credentials or IAM permissions for S3.

choices.text: Add S3 read permissions to the role for the entire node group and rely on operational procedures to prevent other Pods from accessing S3.
choices.explanation: This broadens the node role and does not meet the requirement to avoid increasing node permissions or assign roles per Pod.

choices.text: Pass the role ARN to only the target Pod as an environment variable without deploying an Agent or configuring an association.
choices.explanation: An ARN is not a credential; the Pod needs a mechanism to obtain credentials for the permitted role.

learning.reason: This separates credentials for the target Pod at the service-account level and avoids increasing node permissions.
learning.concept: The EKS Pod Identity Agent and service-account-level associations

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Separate ECS image retrieval permissions from permissions for the running business API
prompt: An ECS task can retrieve an image from a private ECR repository and write output to CloudWatch Logs. After startup, the SDK inside the container is denied access to DynamoDB. What should be changed to separate image and log permissions from the application's table permissions?

choices.text: Add DynamoDB permissions to the task execution role and assume that the SDK inside the container receives credentials from the same role.
choices.explanation: The execution role provides permissions that ECS uses for startup and logging; it is separate from the task role used by the application.

choices.text: Put the table ARN in the ECR repository policy and treat successful image retrieval as permission to use the business API.
choices.explanation: A registry policy does not authorize the application's DynamoDB operations after startup.

choices.text: Add the DynamoDB table to the log group's resource policy and allow table operations whenever log writing succeeds.
choices.explanation: Permission to write logs and DynamoDB authentication and authorization are independent.

choices.text: Grant the task role the permissions required for the target table while retaining the image and log permissions on the task execution role.
choices.explanation: The AWS credentials used by the SDK inside the container come from the task role.

learning.reason: The AWS credentials used by the SDK inside the container come from the task role.
learning.concept: The ECS agent's task execution role and the application task role

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Reverting a shared IAM policy to a validated version with the same ARN
prompt: A single customer managed IAM policy is attached to many roles. Immediately after changing the default version to v4, a required operation was denied. The validated v3 remains as a nondefault version. How can you revert the policy while preserving its attachments and policy ARN?

choices.text: Copy v3 to create a different managed policy, then reattach it to each role one at a time.
choices.explanation: This might restore the permissions, but it does not preserve the original ARN and attachments.

choices.text: Delete the current default version, v4, first and wait for the remaining latest version to become the default automatically.
choices.explanation: The default version cannot be deleted first; another version must be made the default before deletion.

choices.text: Set v3 as the default version of the managed policy.
choices.explanation: Attachments that reference the same ARN use the version that is currently set as the default.

choices.text: Reattach the same policy to every role and select v3 as a parameter for each attachment.
choices.explanation: Role attachments do not use a method that specifies an arbitrary policy version.

learning.reason: Attachments that reference the same ARN use the version that is currently set as the default.
learning.concept: Default versions of managed policies and their attachments

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Checking the status of long-term credentials across an entire account
prompt: An auditor wants a list showing MFA, the active status of long-term access keys, and their update dates for the root user and all IAM users in one AWS account. An analysis of usage frequency under policies and retrieval of the credential values are not needed. Which report should be obtained?

choices.text: Export service last accessed information and infer MFA and key status from the service names listed there.
choices.explanation: Service usage history is not a report that records whether MFA is configured and keys are active for each user.

choices.text: Generate and retrieve the IAM credential report.
choices.explanation: The report collects information about MFA and access key status and update details for users in the account.

choices.text: Export the list of IAM groups and their memberships, and assume that the root user belongs to one of the groups.
choices.explanation: Group information does not contain credential status, and the root user is not managed through IAM groups.

choices.text: Download the current CloudTrail trail configuration and reinterpret its log delivery status as credential status.
choices.explanation: Trail delivery settings do not provide a current account-wide list of credential statuses.

learning.reason: The report collects information about MFA and access key status and update details for users in the account.
learning.concept: Statuses recorded by the IAM credential report

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Keeping management-account access assignments limited to authorized administrators
prompt: The delegated administrator for IAM Identity Center manages user assignments to member accounts. However, the team at the delegated account must not be allowed to operate access to the Organizations management account. Which account should manage permission-set assignments to the management account?

choices.text: Use the organization’s log archive account instead of the delegated administrator and add access to the management account there.
choices.explanation: Changing the delegated account’s purpose does not change the special restriction on the management account.

choices.text: Have an administrator with permissions in the Organizations management account manage assignments to that management account.
choices.explanation: Access settings for the management account itself are handled separately because they cannot be delegated to the delegated administrator.

choices.text: Allow the delegated account to assign access to the management account only after synchronization with the external IdP is stopped.
choices.explanation: Whether synchronization with an external IdP is enabled does not determine whether management-account assignments can be delegated.

choices.text: Have the delegated administrator assign the management account in the same way as a member account, while the management side only performs audits.
choices.explanation: A delegated administrator cannot operate access to the management account in the same way as for ordinary member accounts.

learning.reason: Access settings for the management account itself are handled separately because they cannot be delegated to the delegated administrator.
learning.concept: Identity Center delegated administration and the Organizations management-account exception

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Authentication succeeds, but no AWS role is available through SAML
prompt: A SAML assertion from the internal IdP is trusted, and the user authenticates successfully in the IdP. To allow the user to select one specified existing IAM role in AWS, what information must be included in the assertion? The role’s trust policy is already configured.

choices.text: Put the user’s email address in NameID so that AWS automatically selects an IAM role permitted by the organization.
choices.explanation: The authenticated user name and the specification of which AWS role the user may assume are separate pieces of information.

choices.text: Put only the role ARN in RoleSessionName and have AWS infer the corresponding SAML provider from the account ID.
choices.explanation: The session-name attribute cannot replace the pair consisting of the role ARN and the provider ARN.

choices.text: Put the role name in the SessionDuration attribute and have AWS select the role to assume from that name.
choices.explanation: SessionDuration specifies the session length; it is not the attribute used to associate the user with a role.

choices.text: In the AWS-specific Role attribute, specify the pair consisting of the assigned IAM role ARN and the corresponding SAML provider ARN.
choices.explanation: The assertion identifies the appropriate role that AWS can present to the user and the trusted issuer associated with that role.

learning.reason: The assertion identifies the appropriate role that AWS can present to the user and the trusted issuer associated with that role.
learning.concept: The role ARN and provider ARN included in the SAML Role attribute

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Correctly Estimating the Duration of a Chained Role Session
prompt: A user uses temporary credentials for an operations role to assume a work role in another account. The work role has a maximum session duration of 4 hours, but requesting 2 hours fails. How should this be designed to maintain the chain without interrupting a long-running job?

choices.text: Change the work role's maximum session duration to 12 hours and request 2 hours through the same chain.
choices.explanation: Increasing the role's own limit does not change the 1-hour limit for role chaining.

choices.text: Change the work role's session name so that a different restriction is selected for a 2-hour chained session.
choices.explanation: The session name is used for identification; it does not change whether the session is chained or alter its time restriction.

choices.text: Treat each session as lasting at most 1 hour and arrange for long-running processing to reacquire credentials through the normal path.
choices.explanation: When a role that has already been assumed is used to assume another role, increasing the target role's configured duration does not extend the time limit.

choices.text: Increase the maximum duration of the initial operations role and assume that the same duration will be inherited by all chained sessions.
choices.explanation: The configured duration of the initial session does not replace the duration limit for a subsequent chained session.

learning.reason: When a role that has already been assumed is used to assume another role, increasing the target role's configured duration does not extend the time limit.
learning.concept: The 1-hour maximum for role chaining and renewable credentials

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Allowing Lambda Invocation Only from a Specific Event Rule
prompt: You want one EventBridge rule to invoke a Lambda function that formats tickets. The execution role that allows the function to read business data is already configured. What authorization should be added so that no other rule is allowed to invoke the same function?

choices.text: In the function's resource policy, allow the EventBridge service principal and restrict the source to the ARN of the specified rule.
choices.explanation: Separate from the function's permissions while it runs, authorization can be configured for the target rule to invoke the function.

choices.text: Add permission to the function's execution role allowing Lambda invocation from all EventBridge rules.
choices.explanation: An execution-role policy is not where permission is granted for an external service to invoke the function.

choices.text: Allow the EventBridge service to invoke every function in the account and determine which rule it was in the function code.
choices.explanation: The permission scope is too broad and does not meet the requirement to deny invocation from rules other than the specified rule through authorization.

choices.text: Narrow the EventBridge rule's event filter and configure no service-invocation permission on the function.
choices.explanation: Narrowing event-selection criteria does not add the authorization required to invoke the Lambda function.

learning.reason: Separate from the function's permissions while it runs, authorization can be configured for the target rule to invoke the function.
learning.concept: The Lambda resource policy and the EventBridge source rule

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Providing Short-Lived AWS Credentials to Workers Using Existing Internal Certificates
prompt: On-premises audit workers send data to S3. A trusted internal CA issues X.509 certificates for the workers, and OIDC is not available. The workers must obtain short-lived credentials for an IAM role limited to the destination, without storing long-term AWS keys. What should be configured? Select two.

choices.text: Import the internal certificate into ACM and specify the certificate ARN as the access key for S3 operations.
choices.explanation: An ACM certificate ARN does not provide IAM credentials for signing AWS API calls.

choices.text: Register the internal CA as a trust anchor in IAM Roles Anywhere.
choices.explanation: This allows the existing PKI to be used to validate certificates issued to authorized workers.

choices.text: Associate the worker's role with an EC2 instance profile and access the instance metadata from on premises.
choices.explanation: This is not an appropriate authentication path for a worker that does not belong to that EC2 instance.

choices.text: Create an IAM OIDC provider by specifying only the audience for AWS tokens, and pass the X.509 certificate as an OIDC token.
choices.explanation: The certificate itself is not a token signed by an OIDC issuer.

choices.text: Configure a role restricted to permissions for the destination and make it available through an IAM Roles Anywhere profile.
choices.explanation: AWS can be accessed using temporary credentials for a role corresponding to the worker's certificate.

learning.reason: This allows the existing PKI to be used to validate certificates issued to authorized workers. AWS can be accessed using temporary credentials for a role corresponding to the worker's certificate.
learning.concept: IAM Roles Anywhere trust anchors and non-AWS workloads

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Performing Required Tasks Without Retaining Long-Term Root Credentials in Member Accounts
prompt: In Organizations, you are auditing the root credentials of existing member accounts. You want to eliminate the routine management of long-term root credentials and have approved personnel perform narrowly scoped root-required tasks for short periods. Which feature should you use?

choices.text: Create a role with AdministratorAccess in each member account and perform every task, including tasks restricted to the root user, through that same role.
choices.explanation: Some root-specific tasks cannot be performed by a normal IAM administrator.

choices.text: Use centralized root access for the organization and have authorized members perform privileged tasks in restricted root sessions.
choices.explanation: This eliminates long-term root credentials for individual member accounts and limits the scope and duration of authorized work.

choices.text: Create root access keys for each member account, store them in a shared organizational repository, and let the required personnel use them permanently.
choices.explanation: This retains long-term root credentials and does not provide short-lived sessions limited to the required tasks.

choices.text: Sign in as the root user of the Organizations management account and assume that all member root credentials are part of the same session.
choices.explanation: Signing in as the management account's root user is different from a constrained session for a target member account.

learning.reason: This eliminates long-term root credentials for individual member accounts and limits the scope and duration of authorized work.
learning.concept: Centralized root access and privileged tasks in member accounts

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Deny access to a protected prefix even when another policy allows reads
prompt: An existing IAM role in the same account is allowed to perform S3 reads by some operational policies. For audit purposes, reads from a specific prefix must be denied even if another Allow is later added to this role. Other reads must continue to work. What should be configured?

choices.text: Remove only the Allows found in the policies currently identified and assume that the other policies will never allow the operation.
choices.explanation: This cannot deny the request if another permission is applied later.

choices.text: Add an inline policy that does not include an Allow for the protected prefix and make that omission take precedence over permissions in other policies.
choices.explanation: The absence of permission in one document does not invalidate permission in another document.

choices.text: Set an explicit Deny for the relevant actions on the prefix in a policy applied to the role.
choices.explanation: An explicit deny takes precedence even when another Allow applies to the same request.

choices.text: Deny reads for every key in the bucket and add Allows in another policy for prefixes outside the protected area.
choices.explanation: Because an explicit deny takes precedence over another permission, this would also stop the existing reads.

learning.reason: An explicit deny takes precedence even when another Allow applies to the same request.
learning.concept: Precedence of a narrowly scoped explicit deny

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Separate the cache for API routes with different authorization decisions
prompt: A Lambda authorizer for an HTTP API uses the simple response format. For the same authenticated user's token, the function returns different authorization decisions for the viewing and approval routes. How should it be configured so that caching is retained while decisions are maintained separately for each route?

choices.text: Keep only the token as the identity source and increase the cache retention time.
choices.explanation: Increasing the retention time does not add the route to the cache key.

choices.text: Record the route name in the response body and use only the user's token as the authorizer cache key.
choices.explanation: Information in the business response does not determine the authorizer cache key.

choices.text: Include the route key in the authorizer identity sources in addition to the token.
choices.explanation: Even with the same token, route-specific cache entries are used, so each decision is retained separately.

choices.text: Remove the token from the authorizer identity sources and use only the route key to identify authenticated users.
choices.explanation: A route name does not identify the user by token or separate decisions for different users on the same route.

learning.reason: Even with the same token, route-specific cache entries are used, so each decision is retained separately.
learning.concept: HTTP API authorizer caching and identity sources

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Obtain temporary credentials for AWS resources after sign-in
prompt: A web application authenticates users with a Cognito user pool. The application must issue short-term AWS credentials to the frontend so authenticated users can perform limited S3 operations with the AWS SDK. The user pool will continue to be used. What should be added?

choices.text: Configure a Cognito identity pool that trusts the user pool and an authenticated role with a restricted permission scope.
choices.explanation: The identity pool exchanges the user pool token for temporary credentials that can sign AWS API requests, and the role limits the permissions.

choices.text: Configure the user pool ID token directly in the SDK as the S3 access key.
choices.explanation: The application JWT is not the AWS session credentials required to sign AWS API requests.

choices.text: List the user pool group names as IAM principals in the bucket policy.
choices.explanation: User pool group names are not IAM principals for an AWS resource policy.

choices.text: Place the user pool app client's client secret in the frontend and use it as the S3 secret access key.
choices.explanation: A client secret is not a key for signing AWS API requests and is not credentials to distribute to users.

learning.reason: The identity pool exchanges the user pool token for temporary credentials that can sign AWS API requests, and the role limits the permissions.
learning.concept: User pool JWTs and identity pool AWS credentials

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Limit a KMS key's use to one log group
prompt: Audit logs are stored in CloudWatch Logs, and a customer managed KMS key is associated with the log group. The key must be usable by CloudWatch Logs only for encryption operations on one specified log group. Other log groups must continue using their existing protection. How should the key policy be configured?

choices.text: Fix the log group's retention period and assume that only log groups with the same number of days can use KMS.
choices.explanation: Log retention is not a condition used to determine the key's target from a KMS request.

choices.text: Tag the key with the log group name and, without conditions, allow all CloudWatch Logs groups to use the key.
choices.explanation: Naming or tagging the key alone does not scope an unconditional service permission to the target log group.

choices.text: Make only the application role that produces the logs the key user and do not allow CloudWatch Logs to use the key.
choices.explanation: The service that performs encryption for the log group could not use the key, so the associated protection would not work.

choices.text: Allow the CloudWatch Logs service principal for the target Region and restrict the permission to the specified log group ARN in the encryption context.
choices.explanation: Evaluating the ARN supplied by CloudWatch Logs prevents use by other log groups in the same service.

learning.reason: Evaluating the ARN supplied by CloudWatch Logs prevents use by other log groups in the same service.
learning.concept: The log group ARN in the encryption context that CloudWatch Logs passes to KMS

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Reduce S3 KMS calls for new objects while retaining the specified customer managed key
prompt: A large number of small files in S3 are protected with SSE-KMS. The responsible team wants to reduce the number of KMS requests for new files while continuing to use the existing customer managed key. Object permissions are maintained separately, and the key policy already allows the bucket context. What should be changed?

choices.text: Extend the KMS key rotation period and expect fewer API requests for each object write.
choices.explanation: The rotation period does not change how requests are made when S3 uses data keys.

choices.text: Change default encryption to SSE-S3 and assume that the current customer managed KMS key will still be used for new files.
choices.explanation: SSE-S3 cannot maintain protection with a customer managed KMS key.

choices.text: Stop recording S3 data events in logs and treat the number of KMS requests actually executed as reduced.
choices.explanation: Changing audit logging does not increase or decrease the number of cryptographic operations required by SSE-KMS.

choices.text: Keep SSE-KMS and the current customer managed key, and enable S3 Bucket Key on the bucket.
choices.explanation: S3 can use a short-lived bucket-level key to reduce KMS requests generated when new objects are encrypted.

learning.reason: S3 can use a short-lived bucket-level key to reduce KMS requests generated when new objects are encrypted.
learning.concept: S3 Bucket Key with SSE-KMS and new objects

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Restrict the target application’s mount to a single access point
prompt: An EFS file system is shared for two purposes. For a specific application role, mounting should be allowed only when the specified access point is used and the connection uses TLS. The NFS mount target is reachable from the same subnet, and the design should not rely only on ordinary file permissions. What should be used?

choices.text: In the EFS file system policy, restrict the target role’s ClientMount to requests that satisfy both the approved access point and TLS requirements.
choices.explanation: Even from the same network, authorization can specify the permitted mount path and protect the connection.

choices.text: Specify the access point name in the application’s mount path, but allow direct mounts in the file system policy.
choices.explanation: Specifying the preferred path in ordinary configuration does not prevent other paths from being authorized.

choices.text: Apply encryption at rest to EFS and allow any mount without TLS when the file system is encrypted.
choices.explanation: Encryption at rest is separate from the access point and TLS controls used by a client to mount the file system.

choices.text: Open the security group for the NFS port to the entire shared subnet and have the access point restriction inferred from the file path.
choices.explanation: Allowing network reachability does not evaluate the IAM principal, access point, and TLS conditions together at connection time.

learning.reason: Even from the same network, authorization can specify the permitted mount path and protect the connection.
learning.concept: Access point and TLS conditions for EFS mount authorization

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Reject unintended broad permissions in a new secret policy
prompt: A team updates a Secrets Manager secret resource policy from CI. It wants to preserve narrow delegation to approved principals while having the service reject, at application time, any policy that grants access to broad principals. What should be configured?

choices.text: Add private to the policy’s display name and assume that the name automatically determines whether it can be applied.
choices.explanation: Naming a resource policy does not inspect the permissions granted by the policy.

choices.text: Associate an encryption key with the secret and assume that updates to policies with broad access are always rejected.
choices.explanation: Encryption configuration is different from validating the contents of a resource policy.

choices.text: Enable BlockPublicPolicy in the request that sets the policy.
choices.explanation: The service can validate whether the policy allows broad access and reject the specified request.

choices.text: Review access logs after applying the policy and leave it in place if no inappropriate reads have occurred.
choices.explanation: Post-application logging cannot prevent the policy from being applied and may miss broad permissions that have not yet been used.

learning.reason: The service can validate whether the policy allows broad access and reject the specified request.
learning.concept: BlockPublicPolicy validation with PutResourcePolicy

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Maintain listener associations when updating an imported certificate
prompt: A certificate issued by a partner certificate authority was imported into ACM, and multiple ALB listeners reference the same certificate ARN. The updated certificate, its corresponding private key, and the chain have been received. What should be done to keep the certificate authority unchanged and avoid changing the ARN on each listener?

choices.text: Delete the old certificate first and import a certificate with the same private key, assuming that the previous ARN will be reused.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve the existing associations, and a new import does not guarantee recreation with the same ARN.

choices.text: Re-import the updated certificate, key, and chain for the existing ACM certificate ARN.
choices.explanation: The certificate can be updated while associated resources continue to use the same ARN.

choices.text: Import the update as a new ACM certificate and assume that the original ARN will be overwritten because the domain name is the same.
choices.explanation: A new import does not update an existing certificate ARN while preserving its references.

choices.text: Add the old certificate’s domain to Route 53 and wait for the externally issued certificate to be renewed automatically by ACM.
choices.explanation: Imported external certificates are not eligible for ACM managed renewal.

learning.reason: The certificate can be updated while associated resources continue to use the same ARN.
learning.concept: ACM certificate re-import and the existing ARN

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Remove currently public EBS snapshots from public access
prompt: An audit found that EBS snapshots in one Region are already public. You want to stop both new public-sharing operations and public access to snapshots that were already made public, while allowing private sharing with specified accounts. Which setting should you choose?

choices.text: Set the EBS snapshot Block Public Access setting in the target Region to the mode that blocks all public sharing.
choices.explanation: This blocks new public sharing and public access to snapshots that were previously made public.

choices.text: Manually remove the public permission from one known snapshot and configure no restriction on future public-sharing operations.
choices.explanation: This can remove public access from the known resource, but it does not stop existing and future public access across the Region.

choices.text: Use the mode that blocks only new public sharing and expect it to stop existing public access at the same time.
choices.explanation: The new-public-sharing-only mode does not stop existing access to snapshots that were already public.

choices.text: Enable the default for new EBS encryption and assume that existing unencrypted snapshots will become private through this setting alone.
choices.explanation: The default encryption setting does not retroactively change the public-sharing state of existing snapshots.

learning.reason: This blocks new public sharing and public access to snapshots that were previously made public.
learning.concept: The two modes for restricting public sharing of EBS snapshots

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Restore backups with multiparty approval independent of the production account
prompt: An organization uses an AWS Backup logically air-gapped vault. If the production management path is unavailable, an account in a separate recovery organization must obtain recovery access after agreement by multiple approvers. The required prerequisites for both organizations are satisfied. What should be done in advance? Select two.

choices.text: Allow only administrators in the production account to access the original vault and use that path during an incident.
choices.explanation: This retains a dependency on the production management path, which may be unavailable during a failure.

choices.text: Grant permanent recovery permissions through the vault policy to every person responsible for the recovery account.
choices.explanation: If each person can recover without approval, the configuration does not require multiparty agreement.

choices.text: Create an approval team for the recovery organization and share it with the vault-owning side and the recovery account by using AWS RAM.
choices.explanation: This lets independent personnel approve recovery instead of relying on the production management path, with both sides referencing the same approval team.

choices.text: Associate the approval team with the vault so that the recovery side can request approval for access.
choices.explanation: This links recovery access to the target vault with approval by multiple parties.

choices.text: Set the default vault's retention period to the maximum and assume that access will be granted to the recovery account without configuring multiparty approval.
choices.explanation: Backup retention settings alone do not configure a recovery-access path or approval for another organization.

learning.reason: This lets independent personnel approve recovery instead of relying on the production management path, with both sides referencing the same approval team. It also links recovery access to the target vault with approval by multiple parties.
learning.concept: The recovery organization's approval team and a logically air-gapped vault

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Return decrypted results only to an approved isolated compute environment
prompt: You process sensitive data with Nitro Enclaves. Communication with the parent EC2 instance is required, but the parent must not be able to read the plaintext data key obtained through decryption. What should you do to restrict KMS processing based on the measurements of an approved enclave? Select two.

choices.text: Give the enclave a fixed name and use a standard key policy to unconditionally allow all decryption requests from the parent EC2 instance.
choices.explanation: A name and ordinary permissions alone do not cause KMS to verify the measurements of the target enclave.

choices.text: Add attestation conditions for the approved enclave measurements to the KMS grant.
choices.explanation: This authorizes the request only after verifying the measurements of the specified compute environment.

choices.text: Allow ordinary Decrypt operations only to the parent EC2 instance's instance role and pass the resulting plaintext to the enclave.
choices.explanation: The parent obtains the plaintext, so this does not meet the requirement to keep the parent outside the trusted boundary.

choices.text: Specify the enclave's attestation document in the decryption request and decrypt the result inside the enclave using the recipient's encrypted result.
choices.explanation: Because the result is protected with the public key in the document, the plaintext data key is not returned to the parent, which does not have the corresponding private key.

choices.text: Encrypt the parent EC2 instance's EBS volumes and assume that encrypting the KMS plaintext obtained by the running OS at rest will hide it from the parent.
choices.explanation: Encryption at rest for the volume does not isolate plaintext obtained by the running parent.

learning.reason: This authorizes the request only after verifying the measurements of the specified compute environment. Because the result is protected with the public key in the document, the plaintext data key is not returned to the parent, which does not have the corresponding private key.
learning.concept: KMS enclave attestation and protection with the recipient's public key

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Encrypted data became unreadable after imported key material expired
prompt: A symmetric KMS key containing externally generated key material entered PendingImport after the material expired. The encrypted data remains, and the original copy of the material was safely preserved. How can you make the existing ciphertext readable without creating new ciphertext?

choices.text: Call EnableKey only and wait for the expired material to be restored automatically inside KMS.
choices.explanation: Enabling the key does not reimport key material that has expired.

choices.text: Import unrelated new material into the same KMS key and expect the previous ciphertext to be readable with the new material.
choices.explanation: The same key identifier does not substitute for the original key material associated with the ciphertext.

choices.text: Create a separate AWS-generated key, switch the alias, and treat the existing ciphertext as compatible with the new key.
choices.explanation: A new key with different material cannot decrypt ciphertext created with the previous key.

choices.text: Reimport the preserved original key material into the same KMS key.
choices.explanation: Restoring the material associated with the ciphertext to the same key enables that KMS key to decrypt the existing data.

learning.reason: Restoring the material associated with the ciphertext to the same key enables that KMS key to decrypt the existing data.
learning.concept: Expiration of imported KMS key material and reimporting the same material

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Do not disconnect existing database connections solely because an authentication token expires
prompt: An RDS engine that supports IAM database authentication is in use. The application keeps authenticated database sessions in a connection pool. Existing connections continue to work after 15 minutes from token issuance, but a new connection is rejected when it uses an expired token. What should be changed?

choices.text: Use a valid IAM token for new connections, and manage the existing connection pool according to the database's normal connection lifetime.
choices.explanation: The token expiration limits authentication for a connection; it is not intended to automatically disconnect a session after authentication.

choices.text: Treat every established connection as invalid and forcibly disconnect it when the token used to create the connection expires.
choices.explanation: Established sessions do not need to be terminated solely because the token expires.

choices.text: Use the same initial token indefinitely from every application and assume that new connections are treated the same as existing sessions.
choices.explanation: A new connection evaluates token validity during authentication, so an expired token cannot be reused.

choices.text: Extend the TLS certificate lifetime and assume that the IAM token can also be used for new connections for the same period.
choices.explanation: The server certificate lifetime does not change the expiration of an IAM database authentication token.

learning.reason: The token expiration limits authentication for a connection; it is not intended to automatically disconnect a session after authentication.
learning.concept: IAM authentication token lifetime and established sessions

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Review only the few necessary samples from a finding summary
prompt: A staff member reviews Macie sensitive data findings. Ordinary findings do not include the original sensitive values, and only approved investigators can retrieve specific samples from valid findings. Limit the S3 read access to the source data and the required KMS permissions to those investigators. What should be configured?

choices.text: Forward existing findings to Security Hub and assume that each sample can be recovered regardless of the owner's KMS permissions.
choices.explanation: Forwarding findings does not replace the configuration or source-data permissions required to retrieve samples.

choices.text: Configure Macie sensitive data sample retrieval so that only authorized investigators can request samples from the findings they need to examine.
choices.explanation: This separates ordinary finding summaries from separately authorized access to original sensitive-data samples.

choices.text: Give everyone who can read findings the source S3 bucket's GetObject permission, making finding access and sample access identical.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to separate permission to view findings from permission to read sensitive values in the source objects.

choices.text: Add discovered values to an allow list and configure Macie to include the same values in plaintext in future findings.
choices.explanation: An allow list is used to exclude matching values from detection; it does not configure plaintext output in findings.

learning.reason: This separates ordinary finding summaries from separately authorized access to original sensitive-data samples.
learning.concept: Macie findings and controlled retrieval of sensitive data samples

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Allow only the disaster-recovery role to decrypt locally
prompt: An application replicates data encrypted with a multi-Region KMS key to another Region. The corresponding replica key is already available. Allow the local recovery role to decrypt only with the local key without affecting administrative permissions in the primary Region. What should be configured?

choices.text: Add the recovery role only to the primary Region's key policy and assume that automatic synchronization grants the same permission locally.
choices.explanation: Key material may be shared, but key policies are not automatically synchronized.

choices.text: Allow the recovery role all KMS operations in the primary Region and infer permissions for the local key from the copied ciphertext.
choices.explanation: This unnecessarily broadens permissions and does not configure authorization to access the local key.

choices.text: Configure the replica key policy and the necessary IAM permissions for the recovery role specifically for the local key.
choices.explanation: Even when keys interoperate, authorization is independent in each Region through its key policy.

choices.text: Make the replica's tags identical to the primary key's tags so that the local role can decrypt without IAM permissions.
choices.explanation: Matching tags do not grant permission to use a KMS key.

learning.reason: Even when keys interoperate, authorization is independent in each Region through its key policy.
learning.concept: Shared key material and independent replica authorization

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Prepare the required permissions before enrolling an existing account in Control Tower
prompt: An existing member account is being enrolled in an OU registered with Control Tower. Account-specific prerequisites have been verified, and the account must be eligible for baseline deployment through manual enrollment. What must be configured for Control Tower to operate in the target account?

choices.text: Create a read-only role with an arbitrary name that can be assumed only by an operations employee's personal account, and delegate baseline deployment during enrollment to it.
choices.explanation: It is read-only and lacks the specified trust path, so it cannot perform enrollment and the required changes.

choices.text: Create the AWSControlTowerExecution role in the target account and allow Control Tower to assume it through the specified path from the management account.
choices.explanation: This establishes the execution path needed to deploy the baseline to the target account during manual enrollment.

choices.text: Give the management account the target account's root credentials so that Control Tower can use those keys for enrollment.
choices.explanation: This shares unnecessary long-term root credentials instead of using the authorized execution role for baseline deployment.

choices.text: Point an AWS Config aggregator at the target account and assume that successful aggregation permits enrollment without an execution role.
choices.explanation: Aggregating recorded data does not replace the authorization required to deploy the baseline.

learning.reason: This establishes the execution path needed to deploy the baseline to the target account during manual enrollment.
learning.concept: The AWSControlTowerExecution role and trust for existing members

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Centralize results while keeping evaluation and recording settings in each environment
prompt: An audit team wants to search AWS Config evaluation results and recorded configurations from multiple accounts and Regions in one place. Because the management team changes the rules in each environment, adding central search must not change the original rules. What should be configured?

choices.text: Apply a new conformance pack to every account in the organization and replace all existing rules with the central template.
choices.explanation: This controls deployment and does not meet the goal of aggregating results while preserving the existing rules.

choices.text: Create a recorder only in the central account, stop the recorders in the other accounts, and record all configurations there.
choices.explanation: A recorder in the central account cannot record the original data from the other locations.

choices.text: Do not use AWS Config recorders; store a list of CloudTrail users centrally as the current configuration compliance status.
choices.explanation: API activity history is not the Config configuration data or rule evaluation results themselves.

choices.text: Aggregate the target configuration data into a central AWS Config aggregator and continue the original recording and evaluations.
choices.explanation: This enables searches across accounts and Regions, and aggregation itself does not change the rules in the source environments.

learning.reason: This enables searches across accounts and Regions, and aggregation itself does not change the rules in the source environments.
learning.concept: The aggregation-only behavior of an AWS Config aggregator

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Use the effective policy inherited by a member as the starting point for backup investigation
prompt: A backup policy exists at the Organizations root, an OU, and a member account. In the target member account, you find a backup interval that differs from what was expected. Which item should you retrieve to verify what is applied to that member after the settings are merged?

choices.text: Output only the document directly attached to the nearest OU and assume that settings from the root and account hierarchy are not applied.
choices.explanation: The final result can include inherited content from other hierarchy levels and settings specific to the account.

choices.text: Check only the backup service access status in Organizations and conclude that the expected interval is applied if it is enabled.
choices.explanation: The service integration status alone does not show the specific merged policy for the target account.

choices.text: Retrieve the effective backup policy for the target member account.
choices.explanation: This shows the content inherited and merged through the hierarchy as the policy applied to that account.

choices.text: Check only whether an AWS Backup job existed yesterday and reconstruct the policy text for the entire hierarchy from that one job.
choices.explanation: A job provides evidence of execution status but does not show the policy text merged by the organization.

learning.reason: This shows the content inherited and merged through the hierarchy as the policy applied to that account.
learning.concept: The effective backup policy merged for a member in Organizations

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Use AWS measurements and external approval records in the same assessment
prompt: You are using an existing AWS Audit Manager assessment. AWS configuration data can be collected periodically, but records of approvals performed in an external workflow are also required. Which two methods should you use so that reviewers can trace the sources? Select two.

choices.text: Keep all records outside the assessment and do not associate evidence with the same control.
choices.explanation: This makes it difficult for reviewers to verify the relationship between controls and evidence.

choices.text: Enter the AWS configuration data and external records only in the description field of the policy document, without referring to the original records.
choices.explanation: A description alone cannot preserve traceability to the evidence used and the approval records.

choices.text: Import the external approval records as manual evidence for the relevant control so that the associated approvals can be identified.
choices.explanation: Evidence that AWS cannot collect automatically can be reviewed by associating it with the appropriate control.

choices.text: Use a control that automatically collects configuration information from the corresponding AWS data source.
choices.explanation: This periodically records AWS-side evidence in the same assessment.

choices.text: If a configuration snapshot exists for the target account, omit additional evidence by assuming that the external approval also occurred.
choices.explanation: An AWS configuration cannot automatically prove who approved something in a separate approval system.

learning.reason: AWS-side evidence can be recorded periodically in the same assessment, while evidence that AWS cannot collect automatically can be associated with the appropriate control for review.
learning.concept: Automatic collection and manual evidence in Audit Manager

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Do not control service-linked role behavior using only SCPs
prompt: An SCP denying a specific operation was configured for a target OU in the organization. The operation is denied for an operations role, but an administrative process using an AWS service-linked role continues the operation. The activity will be audited, and the service-side scope will be controlled as needed. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: Shorten the session duration of the target service-linked role so that the SCP denial is enforced for that role as well.
choices.explanation: Session duration and the scope of principals that can be constrained by an SCP are separate matters.

choices.text: Attach the same denial to another OU to give the SCP higher priority, which will make it apply to the service-linked role.
choices.explanation: Attaching the denial repeatedly does not change the SCP exception for service-linked roles.

choices.text: SCPs do not constrain service-linked roles. Control their behavior through the target service's feature settings or deployment scope.
choices.explanation: SCP behavior differs for ordinary operations principals and service-linked roles used by a service for specific operations.

choices.text: Rename the service-linked role administratively and have the same service use it with the same permissions.
choices.explanation: There is no mechanism that changes SCP behavior by renaming the role.

learning.reason: SCP behavior differs for ordinary operations principals and service-linked roles used by a service for specific operations.
learning.concept: The scope of SCPs and the exception for service-linked roles

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Checking Encryption Standards in CI Without Creating AWS Resources
prompt: A repository contains multiple CloudFormation templates. During the review stage, you need to check specified encryption properties and public-access settings. The inspection job must not receive AWS credentials, and it must report the location and reason for each violating template. What should you add?

choices.text: Deploy AWS Config rules across the organization and assume that they automatically evaluate local CI templates even when no stacks are created.
choices.explanation: AWS Config evaluates the configuration of resources in an AWS environment; it is not a credential-free way to apply policies to local files.

choices.text: Define CloudFormation Guard rules and apply them to the templates in a local CI inspection.
choices.explanation: This checks whether template properties satisfy declared conditions without deploying anything to AWS.

choices.text: Submit all templates with CloudFormation CreateChangeSet and give the inspection job none of the permissions required for submission.
choices.explanation: Sending change sets to AWS requires credentials, and this is not itself a local security-policy inspection.

choices.text: Run only JSON or YAML syntax validation and conclude that all encryption settings are effective when the format is valid.
choices.explanation: Valid syntax does not ensure that the required properties or permitted values are present.

learning.reason: The templates can be checked against declared property conditions without deploying them to AWS.
learning.concept: Local declarative policy inspection with CloudFormation Guard

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Stopping Direct Regional Ingress While Continuing Updates from Private Subnets
prompt: In a Region with multiple VPCs, you need to centrally block unauthorized inbound traffic through internet gateways. Applications in private subnets must continue obtaining updates through NAT gateways. Which VPC Block Public Access setting should you use?

choices.text: Disable VPC Block Public Access and verify only through operational reports that there is no direct inbound traffic to EC2.
choices.explanation: This may provide observation, but it does not centrally enforce blocking of unauthorized inbound traffic at the Region level.

choices.text: Use the mode that blocks only inbound traffic from internet gateways.
choices.explanation: This blocks inbound connections initiated from the internet while preserving permitted outbound traffic through NAT gateways.

choices.text: Select the mode that blocks traffic in both directions and applies it to every route without exception.
choices.explanation: This would also prevent the required outbound traffic from the applications using NAT gateways.

choices.text: Configure exclusions that allow traffic from the internet for every VPC and do not apply inbound restrictions.
choices.explanation: Central blocking of direct inbound traffic would not be effective.

learning.reason: This blocks inbound connections initiated from the internet while preserving permitted outbound traffic through NAT gateways.
learning.concept: Comparing inbound-only and bidirectional VPC Block Public Access modes

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Resolving Detected Landing Zone Drift Through the Authorized Process
prompt: In a Control Tower landing zone, a managed baseline resource was changed manually, and the console reported landing zone drift. The required prerequisites and dependencies have been repaired, and you need to realign the baseline with Control Tower. Which procedure should you follow?

choices.text: Delete all related managed stacks and replace them for each member account using separate IaC.
choices.explanation: This could break Control Tower's management relationships and is not the authorized reset procedure for restoring alignment.

choices.text: Review the reported drift, then perform a landing zone reset in Control Tower and verify the result.
choices.explanation: This reapplies Control Tower-managed settings through the authorized operation and lets you confirm the baseline state.

choices.text: Mark the relevant items as notified in AWS Config audit results and make no changes to the Control Tower configuration.
choices.explanation: Processing an evaluation notification does not resolve the baseline discrepancy detected by Control Tower.

choices.text: Register one new member account and assume that this alone automatically repairs the drift in the existing landing zone.
choices.explanation: Registering another member is not an operation that resets the existing managed configuration.

learning.reason: The authorized operation reapplies Control Tower-managed settings and allows the baseline state to be verified.
learning.concept: Detecting landing zone drift and reapplying the baseline through a reset

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Managing an Exception OU While Maintaining Organization-Wide Standards
prompt: You use Security Hub CSPM central configuration and have associated a common policy with a parent OU. For a specific child OU, the central configuration must manage a different set of standards and controls for regulatory compliance. Without returning to manual configuration by members, how should you apply the different configuration only to that child OU?

choices.text: Change the target child OU to self-managed and have each member manually configure the standards.
choices.explanation: This abandons the required central management even if it avoids the parent configuration.

choices.text: Create a separate central configuration policy containing the required standards and explicitly associate it with the target child OU.
choices.explanation: A child OU specified directly does not inherit the parent policy and uses the separately centrally managed configuration.

choices.text: Add both sets of standards to the policy configured for the parent OU and automatically apply the same configuration to the other child OUs.
choices.explanation: This fails the requirement to change only the target child OU and affects other environments.

choices.text: Filter the display of findings in the home Region for the child OU and consider the central policy changed.
choices.explanation: Display filters for aggregated results do not configure the standards or controls that are actually in effect.

learning.reason: A child OU specified directly does not inherit the parent policy and can use a separately centrally managed configuration.
learning.concept: Explicit child-OU central policies and inheritance from a parent OU

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Recording Requests Denied by a VPC Endpoint Policy
prompt: A security team needs to investigate API requests made through VPC endpoints for S3 owned by the organization that were denied by an endpoint policy. An existing trail that retains only management events does not provide the required records. What should be added?

choices.text: Enable S3 network activity events in CloudTrail and filter them to the target endpoint and denial errors.
choices.explanation: This event type records API activity through VPC endpoints and denials caused by endpoint policies.

choices.text: Record only S3 write management events in the existing trail and assume that all denied requests are included as management events.
choices.explanation: Network activity events are a different event type from management events.

choices.text: Reconstruct all denials that occurred before requests reached the target endpoint from S3 object-level logs.
choices.explanation: The location and type of event recording are different, so the required endpoint denials cannot be observed directly.

choices.text: Count REJECT entries in VPC Flow Logs and classify IAM denials at the application layer as network denials.
choices.explanation: A flow rejection does not indicate the result of API authorization by an endpoint policy.

learning.reason: This event type records API activity through VPC endpoints and denials caused by endpoint policies.
learning.concept: CloudTrail network activity events

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Comparing Anomalous Management API Error Rates with Historical Baselines
prompt: A CloudTrail trail continuously records write management events. The team wants to detect a sudden increase in the failure rate based on normal behavior and avoid setting fixed thresholds for individual APIs. Which trail feature should be added?

choices.text: Set the log retention period with an S3 lifecycle rule and monitor lifecycle notifications as the management API error rate.
choices.explanation: Expiration events do not contain management API error rates or deviations from normal behavior.

choices.text: Enable detection of API error rates with CloudTrail Insights in the trail.
choices.explanation: Insights can compare management events with normal patterns and handle anomalous API error rates as Insights events.

choices.text: Enable detection of API call rates only in the trail and equate changes in the failure rate with the total number of calls.
choices.explanation: If successful calls become failures, the failure rate can increase even when the total number of calls remains unchanged.

choices.text: Enable CloudTrail log file integrity validation and treat failed digest comparisons as a sudden increase in API errors.
choices.explanation: Digests are used to investigate modified or missing log files; they do not learn API error rates.

learning.reason: Insights can compare management events with normal patterns and handle anomalous API error rates as Insights events.
learning.concept: Analyzing API error rates with CloudTrail Insights

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Scanning Packages on Instances That Cannot Be Managed with SSM
prompt: Amazon Inspector continuously evaluates EC2. On some supported Linux instances, SSM Agent cannot be used for maintenance reasons. The instances meet the EBS configuration and tagging requirements for Inspector agentless scanning, while existing agent-based scanning of managed nodes must continue. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Use EC2 hybrid scanning to scan eligible unmanaged instances without an agent.
choices.explanation: This preserves agent-based scanning for managed nodes while scanning the EBS data of unmanaged instances that meet the requirements.

choices.text: Use only ECR image scanning and substitute its results for the installed packages on EC2.
choices.explanation: Container image scan results differ from evaluating software on the actual storage of EC2.

choices.text: Attach only Inspector read permissions to the EC2 instance profile and treat the instances as agent-scanned without SSM.
choices.explanation: Permission to view findings does not change agent communication or the scanning method.

choices.text: Keep the agent-based method and wait for results to appear for nodes that are not managed with SSM.
choices.explanation: The agent-based method alone does not scan unmanaged nodes under these conditions.

learning.reason: This preserves agent-based scanning for managed nodes while scanning the EBS data of unmanaged instances that meet the requirements.
learning.concept: Inspector hybrid EC2 scanning

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Prioritizing Detailed Investigation Across Many Buckets
prompt: An organization is classifying, for the first time, many S3 buckets containing backups and ingested data. Before scanning all objects in bulk, it wants to prioritize detailed inspection based on the results for representative objects. Which Macie feature should be used?

choices.text: Use automated sensitive data discovery for the target account and select buckets for further investigation from the discovery results.
choices.explanation: It can select and inspect objects and use the results for an initial assessment of many buckets.

choices.text: Use S3 Inventory to inspect only size and modification date, analyze no object content, and determine from those attributes whether sensitive information is present.
choices.explanation: Inventory attributes alone cannot evaluate whether the content contains sensitive information.

choices.text: Immediately run a one-time job for each bucket that includes all objects and obtain all results first.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to limit cost and time before setting the priority order.

choices.text: Classify data sensitivity from the bucket encryption settings alone and determine that encrypted data contains no sensitive data.
choices.explanation: Whether data is encrypted at rest does not indicate the sensitivity of the object content.

learning.reason: It can select and inspect objects and use the results for an initial assessment of many buckets.
learning.concept: Continuous inventory and sampling with Macie automated discovery

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Resolve insufficient subnet capacity when enabling log types
prompt: You attempt to add control plane log types to a long-running EKS cluster, but the update reports insufficient free IP addresses in the relevant subnets. What should you do without changing the API exposure or IAM permissions?

choices.text: Ensure the required free IP addresses are available in each target subnet of the EKS cluster, then retry the update.
choices.explanation: Changing the log configuration requires up to five free IP addresses in each cluster subnet.

choices.text: Add all CloudWatch Logs permissions to the IAM role and leave the subnet address shortage unchanged.
choices.explanation: IAM permissions alone do not reserve the network addresses required for the update.

choices.text: Shorten the CloudWatch Logs retention period and wait for IP addresses to return to the EKS cluster subnets.
choices.explanation: The log retention period does not change VPC IP allocation.

choices.text: Enable the public API endpoint so that the cluster subnets are not used when updating the log configuration.
choices.explanation: Public API access and available subnet capacity for configuration updates are separate requirements.

learning.reason: Changing the log configuration requires up to five free IP addresses in each cluster subnet.
learning.concept: Free IP addresses required in cluster subnets when updating the log configuration

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Determine whether delayed log delivery is caused by receiver-side throttling
prompt: A CloudWatch Logs subscription sends audit logs to Kinesis Data Streams. Delivery is delayed during periods of heavy business activity. The relevant logs match the filter. Before reviewing the destination capacity, what should you use to confirm that throttling occurred during delivery?

choices.text: Examine only CloudWatch IncomingBytes and conclude that the destination rejected the data if the ingestion volume is high.
choices.explanation: The volume ingested by the source log is not the number of times the destination rejected delivery.

choices.text: Conclude that Kinesis-side throttling cannot occur if the number of source log groups has not increased.
choices.explanation: Even with a fixed number of source log groups, peak data volume can increase and restrict delivery.

choices.text: Check the subscription's DeliveryThrottling and correlate it with the Kinesis-side write-throttling metric.
choices.explanation: This confirms delivery throttling on the CloudWatch Logs side and allows correlation with destination metrics by time period.

choices.text: Extend the destination retention period and treat the absence of throttling as proven even if the logs arrive late.
choices.explanation: The issue may be the amount that can be written per unit of time, rather than how long data can be retained.

learning.reason: This confirms delivery throttling on the CloudWatch Logs side and allows correlation with destination metrics by time period.
learning.concept: The subscription's DeliveryThrottling and delivery to the destination

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Identify the original source in a relayed flow
prompt: You are analyzing VPC Flow Logs collected at the ENI of a NAT gateway in a test environment. You need to distinguish the relay interface address from the original packet source and classify traffic from multiple private subnets. What should you add to the log?

choices.text: Add the source port to the log and reconstruct the original subnet CIDR from the port number.
choices.explanation: There is no correspondence between a port number and the subnet used that would allow the original IP address to be reconstructed.

choices.text: Add only interface-id to the log and interpret that ID as the source IP attached to the packet.
choices.explanation: The ID of the observed interface is different from the source address of the original packet.

choices.text: Use only srcaddr and assume that the value collected at the NAT-side ENI is always the workload's original address.
choices.explanation: Depending on the observation point, the relaying address may be recorded, so it does not necessarily match the original packet source.

choices.text: Add pkt-srcaddr to a custom format and examine it together with srcaddr.
choices.explanation: This lets you compare the original packet-level source with the source associated with the interface at the observation point.

learning.reason: This lets you compare the original packet-level source with the source associated with the interface at the observation point.
learning.concept: Interface-level and packet-level addresses in Flow Logs

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: TLS details are unavailable for traffic through a pass-through load balancer
prompt: An NLB uses a TCP listener and passes encrypted traffic through unchanged so that TLS is terminated at the backend. You enabled the NLB's legacy S3 access logs, but the TLS version used by the connection is not recorded. How can you record the version used by the actual connection while keeping the termination point unchanged?

choices.text: Use the protocol column in VPC Flow Logs and interpret its value as the TLS version used by the connection.
choices.explanation: protocol represents the IP protocol number, not the result of TLS negotiation.

choices.text: Broaden the S3 bucket delivery policy so that the TCP listener sends legacy TLS access logs.
choices.explanation: Changing the destination permissions does not enable TLS connection log generation by a TCP listener.

choices.text: Change the NLB listener to TLS and assume that the client's TLS is passed through while failing to verify the independence of the backend TLS connection.
choices.explanation: A TLS listener terminates client-side TLS at the NLB, which changes the termination point.

choices.text: Keep the current TCP listener and record connection details at the backend that actually terminates TLS.
choices.explanation: The NLB produces legacy TLS access logs for traffic processed by a TLS listener. In this case, negotiation occurs at the backend.

learning.reason: The NLB produces legacy TLS access logs for traffic processed by a TLS listener. In this case, negotiation occurs at the backend.
learning.concept: NLB legacy TLS access logs and backend TLS termination

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Correcting the placement of the destination for undelivered S3 access logs
prompt: S3 access logging is enabled, but the audit bucket intended as the destination is in a different account and Region. The S3 server access logging method must be retained, and the logs will be collected on the central auditing side later. What should be prepared as the initial delivery destination?

choices.text: Configure only a replication rule for the central bucket and assume that it will automatically receive the initial server access log delivery.
choices.explanation: Replication copies objects after they have been delivered; it does not replace an initial delivery destination that fails the requirements.

choices.text: Keep the central bucket in the different account and Region and add only permission for the log delivery service to access it.
choices.explanation: A destination policy does not change the account and Region requirements.

choices.text: Create a destination that allows log delivery in the same account and Region as the source, and centralize the stored logs through a separate process.
choices.explanation: This satisfies the requirements for the initial access log delivery; central aggregation can be designed after the logs are stored.

choices.text: Change the source bucket's CORS configuration to allow the audit bucket.
choices.explanation: Browser cross-origin controls do not affect the delivery requirements for S3 server access logs.

learning.reason: This satisfies the requirements for the initial access log delivery; central aggregation can be designed after the logs are stored.
learning.concept: The account and Region of the destination for S3 server access logs

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Routing only findings for critical assets to high priority
prompt: Security Hub CSPM has many findings of the same type. The importance of an asset can be identified from finding attributes, and only findings for specific critical assets should have their severity increased and be shown to the responsible team. The handling of configuration checks and other findings must remain unchanged. What should be configured?

choices.text: Only aggregate findings in the home Region and assume that severity will automatically increase according to asset importance.
choices.explanation: Aggregation delivers findings to a central location. A separate configuration is required to change severity based on asset conditions.

choices.text: Set the workflow status of all findings for critical assets to Resolved.
choices.explanation: This marks unresolved findings as resolved instead of increasing their investigation priority.
