choices.text: Select critical assets by using finding attributes and configure a Security Hub CSPM automation rule to change the severity.
choices.explanation: This changes triage attributes only for matching findings while preserving the original configuration-evaluation conditions.

choices.text: Disable the controls in all accounts and have the responsible team create investigation records for critical assets manually.
choices.explanation: This stops the required configuration checks and does not preserve findings for assets that are not critical.

learning.reason: This changes triage attributes only for matching findings while preserving the original configuration-evaluation conditions.
learning.concept: A CSPM automation rule that updates severity attributes based on finding conditions

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Removing an investigation host from the production path of Auto Scaling
prompt: One EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group behind an ALB must be preserved. The host must remain running for investigation but be removed from load balancing. At the same time, the current desired capacity must be maintained by adding a healthy replacement host. The required limits and capacity are already available. What should be done?

choices.text: Move the instance to Standby without reducing the desired capacity.
choices.explanation: The instance is removed from load balancing without being terminated. The group launches a replacement to satisfy the desired capacity.

choices.text: Enable scale-in protection only for the instance and use the same settings for the load balancer targets and the group's desired capacity.
choices.explanation: Scale-in protection alone does not remove the instance from the load balancer and add a replacement.

choices.text: Treat the instance as unhealthy and remove it through the normal Auto Scaling replacement process.
choices.explanation: An unhealthy-instance replacement can terminate the host that is needed for investigation.

choices.text: Move the instance to Standby and reduce the desired capacity by one instance.
choices.explanation: The instance is preserved, but reducing desired capacity prevents a replacement from being launched to maintain the same number of running instances.

learning.reason: The instance is removed from load balancing without being terminated. The group launches a replacement to satisfy the desired capacity.
learning.concept: Moving an instance to Standby without reducing desired capacity

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Restricting which principals can make changes in a member account under investigation
prompt: Multiple unauthorized changes have been found in one of the company's member accounts. Without waiting to enumerate individual IAM policies, the organization needs to temporarily suppress resource changes by ordinary business roles. A separate investigation role must still be able to view evidence. Which measure should be used?

choices.text: Apply an SCP to the account according to the investigation plan, deny the targeted changes by ordinary principals, and validate the investigation access path.
choices.explanation: This applies constraints to multiple IAM roles at once, while approved investigation access can be verified separately.

choices.text: Remove the account from the organization, leave the permissions of each business role unchanged, and wait for the changes to stop.
choices.explanation: Removing the account from the organization does not stop the change permissions held by its ordinary roles.

choices.text: Create only an AWS Config rule that detects configuration changes and restore account changes when necessary.
choices.explanation: Detection and remediation do not proactively suppress the targeted operations while the investigation is in progress.

choices.text: Attach a permissions boundary only to the investigation role and leave the permissions of the other business roles unchanged.
choices.explanation: This does not constrain the business roles that must be restricted; it only limits the investigation side.

learning.reason: This applies constraints to multiple IAM roles at once, while approved investigation access can be verified separately.
learning.concept: Account-level permission limits and the investigation access path

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Properly Reporting an Issue with an AWS Service You Do Not Control
prompt: An investigation confirmed that a public service on AWS operated by a third party outside your organization is serving impersonation pages targeting your users. Protection on your side is complete. Without accessing the third party’s account or the AWS service itself, what should you do?

choices.text: Apply an SCP from your organization’s management account to stop the service in the external AWS account.
choices.explanation: Your organization’s SCP cannot be attached to an account outside the organization and does not grant permission to stop a third party’s service.

choices.text: Add the third party’s account to the scope of your environment’s CloudTrail trail so that its account activity is recorded.
choices.explanation: Your trails cannot collect activity from a third-party account for which you have no administrative authority.

choices.text: Organize the observed public URL, timestamps, impact, and other details, then contact the AWS Trust & Safety abuse-reporting channel.
choices.explanation: Abusive activity conducted by a third party using AWS is handled through a channel separate from reporting a vulnerability in an AWS product.

choices.text: Classify the incident as a vulnerability in an AWS product and contact only the product-vulnerability channel without evidence of a product defect.
choices.explanation: Abuse of a user’s service and a defect in an AWS product have different reporting contacts and investigation scopes.

learning.reason: Abusive activity conducted by a third party using AWS is handled through a channel separate from reporting a vulnerability in an AWS product.
learning.concept: Reporting third-party abuse on AWS versus vulnerabilities in AWS products

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Stopping New Consumption from a Business Queue Only During an Incident Investigation
prompt: You need to retain new events arriving in SQS for investigation. Lambda is invoked through both the target queue and another path, and the other path must remain active. Canceling executions already in progress is unnecessary, and the SQS retention period is sufficiently longer than the investigation. Which operation has the smallest impact?

choices.text: Set Lambda’s reserved concurrency to zero and expect only the target queue to stop being consumed.
choices.explanation: This affects concurrency for the entire function and therefore also stops the other invocation path.

choices.text: Purge the queue while leaving the current consumption configuration unchanged.
choices.explanation: Messages needed for the investigation would be lost, and consumption of newly arriving messages would continue.

choices.text: Increase the queue’s visibility timeout while leaving event source mapping polling enabled.
choices.explanation: The visibility timeout does not stop polling itself, so newly arriving messages may still be received.

choices.text: Disable only the event source mapping for the target SQS queue.
choices.explanation: This stops new polling from the target queue while preserving the other invocation paths for the same function.

learning.reason: This stops new polling from the target queue while preserving the other invocation paths for the same function.
learning.concept: Disabling an SQS event source mapping at the mapping level

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Handling a Temporary Token Issued for a Deleted Pod
prompt: During incident response in EKS, a time-limited projected service account token was issued to the Pod under investigation. It is a Kubernetes API token bound to this Pod. Evidence has been preserved, and deletion of the Pod is authorized. What happens to the same token after the Pod is deleted?

choices.text: Deleting the Pod invalidates all tokens, including those for other service accounts in the same namespace.
choices.explanation: The credentials associated with the target Pod are invalidated; credentials throughout the namespace are not invalidated.

choices.text: The token can always be used until its normal expiration, and the state of the Pod to which it is bound is not checked during authentication.
choices.explanation: The Kubernetes API validates tokens bound to a Pod.

choices.text: Once the bound Pod no longer exists, Kubernetes API validation makes the token invalid.
choices.explanation: Because the validity of objects bound to the token is also checked, this token is distinguished from tokens used by other Pods with the same service account.

choices.text: The Pod’s token remains valid in the Kubernetes API until the EC2 instance profile is replaced.
choices.explanation: Kubernetes bound tokens and an EC2 IAM instance profile are separate authentication mechanisms.

learning.reason: Because the validity of objects bound to the token is also checked, this token is distinguished from tokens used by other Pods with the same service account.
learning.concept: The lifetime of a Pod-bound token validated by the Kubernetes API

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Do Not Change a Recovered Service Based Only on an Old Noncompliant State
prompt: AWS Config automatic remediation isolated a business resource based on a previous noncompliant evaluation. At the time the remediation ran, the responsible operator had already corrected the configuration. Keep the automatic remediation mechanism, but from the next attempt onward, make changes only when the resource is still noncompliant based on its latest state. What should be added?

choices.text: Record the evaluated event ID in a work log and start remediation without retrieving the current state.
choices.explanation: Tracking the notification does not determine whether the configuration is noncompliant at the time of remediation.

choices.text: Read the current resource configuration again before the remediation action and make the change only if the condition is met.
choices.explanation: Even if remediation is triggered by an old compliance summary, it can exit without making a change when the current configuration is already compliant.

choices.text: Increase the number of automatic remediation attempts and repeatedly perform the same change whenever the first noncompliance notification is received.
choices.explanation: Increasing retries does not prevent unnecessary changes based on an outdated evaluation.

choices.text: Broaden the remediation execution role and rewrite all target settings regardless of their current state.
choices.explanation: Expanding authorization does not resolve the difference between the evaluation-time and execution-time states; it only broadens the impact.

learning.reason: Even when remediation is triggered by an old compliance summary, it can exit without making a change if the current configuration is already compliant.
learning.concept: The evaluation snapshot used by automatic remediation and checking the current state immediately before execution

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Determine which rule blocked a legitimate request
prompt: A legitimate order request was rejected by a Web ACL. The WAF logs contain records for multiple non-terminating Count rules and one terminating rule. Before proceeding with the next approved configuration change, where should you verify the rule that actually determined the rejection?

choices.text: Use the most frequent label across all logs as the rule that rejected this individual request.
choices.explanation: Aggregating labels does not provide evidence that a rule selected the terminating action for this particular request.

choices.text: Identify the rule with the lowest priority among the rules attached to the same Web ACL as the source of the rejection without examining the log contents.
choices.explanation: Termination depends on which rule matched, so priority alone cannot identify the source.

choices.text: Treat the first Count rule displayed in the list of non-terminating rules as the rule that determined the rejection.
choices.explanation: A Count match does not end evaluation; a different rule may reject the request afterward.

choices.text: Inspect the terminating rule and action, and if termination occurred in a rule group, also inspect the terminating rule within that group.
choices.explanation: This identifies the action that actually ended request processing and distinguishes it from matches that were only counted.

learning.reason: Identify the action that actually ended request processing and distinguish it from matches that were only counted.
learning.concept: Distinguishing terminating rules from non-terminating matches in AWS WAF logs

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Avoid duplicate tickets when the same incident finding is redelivered
prompt: The operational requirement is to have one ticket per finding within an account; appends and redeliveries must not create new tickets. Even if the processor loses its response, the ticket service provides duplicate prevention through an idempotency key. Which key should be used when creating a new ticket?

choices.text: Create the idempotency key from the finding's originating account and immutable finding ID.
choices.explanation: Redeliveries and appends for the same finding produce the same key, allowing the receiving service to prevent duplicate creation within the validity period.

choices.text: Generate a random ID for every ticket-creation attempt and always use a different key for redeliveries.
choices.explanation: The key differs every time the same finding is processed, so the ticket service cannot recognize the duplicate.

choices.text: Use only the event receipt time as the key and treat all findings received in the same second as one finding.
choices.explanation: This does not prevent the same finding from arriving at different times and can incorrectly merge separate findings.

choices.text: Save the finding ID in the application's memory after ticket creation and continue reading the same memory from other function executions.
choices.explanation: State is not shared reliably between processes or after a restart, so this cannot handle a lost response after successful ticket creation.

learning.reason: The same key is produced for redeliveries and appends of the same finding, allowing the receiving service to prevent duplicate creation within the validity period.
learning.concept: Idempotency using a stable business identifier rather than an event-delivery ID

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Keep the current database and compare it with the rows before the unauthorized change
prompt: The time when data was unauthorizedly changed in RDS has been identified, and the recovery window that includes the moment immediately before the change is still available. Because the running database also contains newer legitimate writes, you need to compare the data before the change without replacing the current database. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Restore the current database in place to its pre-change contents and lose the legitimate latest writes for the comparison.
choices.explanation: This conflicts with the requirement to preserve the current database, and RDS point-in-time recovery creates a separate database.

choices.text: Replicate the current database to a new read replica and use it to view the data from immediately before the change.
choices.explanation: Replicating current data does not produce the state of the database at a specific point in the past.

choices.text: Take the latest manual snapshot, restore it immediately, and assume that the changed rows have returned to their old values.
choices.explanation: A snapshot taken after the change cannot provide the state immediately before the change.

choices.text: Specify a recoverable time before the change, restore it to a new database, and compare it with the current database through an isolated connection path.
choices.explanation: Because this creates a new instance, it does not overwrite the current database and provides the data from the specified time for comparison.

learning.reason: A new instance is created, so the current database is not overwritten and data from the specified time can be examined.
learning.concept: A separate database created by RDS point-in-time recovery

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Do not allow oversized input whose contents cannot be inspected
prompt: For the protected payment API, request bodies exceeding the allowed limit must be rejected automatically. When a request exceeds the AWS WAF body-inspection limit, it must not be allowed without validation, while bodies of normal size must continue to the existing inspection. Which mitigation should be added to the payment path?

choices.text: Add a body-size constraint rule to the path and set Oversize Handling to MATCH so that oversized requests are rejected.
choices.explanation: This processes input beyond the inspection limit as an explicit rejection condition while allowing normal input to proceed to subsequent inspection.

choices.text: When the body is oversized, inspect only the portion that can be inspected and always treat the entire body as inspected if that portion has no issue.
choices.explanation: Partial inspection cannot establish that the entire body has been inspected.

choices.text: Increase the amount of access logging for the payment path and have an operator handle oversized bodies after they reach the application.
choices.explanation: This increases audit records but does not automatically reject oversized requests.

choices.text: Treat an oversized body as a non-match, require no further body inspection, and retain the default allow behavior.
choices.explanation: This does not configure rejection for input that cannot be inspected.

learning.reason: Process input beyond the inspection limit as an explicit rejection condition while allowing normal input to proceed to subsequent inspection.
learning.concept: Oversize Handling for requests exceeding the body-inspection limit

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Using real service health to distinguish overload from an attack
prompt: An ALB is protected by Shield Advanced. Sudden legitimate traffic spikes are normal, and the organization does not want to classify traffic as an attack based only on an increase in traffic. A Route 53 health check that verifies the target service already exists. What should be done to use this information in Shield Advanced detection?

choices.text: Uniformly lower the WAF request limit and do not evaluate the health check status.
choices.explanation: Although this would make it easier to block sudden increases, it does not use service health to distinguish legitimate growth from abnormal activity.

choices.text: Store the health check results in an individual S3 file and record only the file name in a tag on the protected resource.
choices.explanation: Storing the results in S3 or adding a tag does not integrate service health with Shield Advanced.

choices.text: Associate the health check with the target Shield Advanced protection.
choices.explanation: This adds the protected resource's health to detection decisions, allowing Shield Advanced to evaluate situations that are difficult to distinguish based on traffic alone.

choices.text: Use the health check only with a Route 53 failover record and assume that it is automatically reflected in Shield Advanced detection settings.
choices.explanation: A setting used for DNS routing does not automatically associate the health check with the Shield Advanced protection.

learning.reason: This adds the protected resource's health to detection decisions, allowing Shield Advanced to evaluate situations that are difficult to distinguish based on traffic alone.
learning.concept: Associating a Route 53 health check with Shield Advanced protection

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Observing authorized test traffic at the packet level without changing its original path
prompt: In an isolated test VPC, an organization wants to inspect, at the packet level, traffic from an authorized synthetic client. Using the corresponding EC2 network interface, it wants to obtain copies of the target traffic without placing an inspection device inline. What should be configured?

choices.text: Configure a custom VPC Flow Logs format to output the payload of every packet.
choices.explanation: Flow logs contain network-flow metadata and do not store the payload of individual packets.

choices.text: Change the route table so that all business packets for the target are forwarded to an observation device, and treat the device as receiving a copy of the traffic.
choices.explanation: This changes the original path and makes the observation device part of the forwarding path, so it does not meet the non-inline requirement.

choices.text: Reconstruct the test client's packets from EC2 management events in CloudTrail for the same period.
choices.explanation: AWS API audit events do not contain the payload of the test client's network traffic.

choices.text: Configure a Traffic Mirroring session using the ENI as the source, filtering only the test traffic, and copy it to an analysis destination.
choices.explanation: Traffic Mirroring can replicate traffic matching the filter to an observation target without changing the original packet path.

learning.reason: Traffic Mirroring can replicate traffic matching the filter to an observation target without changing the original packet path.
learning.concept: The source, target, and filter for VPC Traffic Mirroring

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Inspecting restricted TLS traffic from managed devices
prompt: An organization must inspect only outbound TLS traffic from organization-managed devices to approved business destinations, in accordance with its policies. It can securely configure all target devices to trust a specified CA. Traffic outside the scope must not be inspected. Which preparations are required? Select two.

choices.text: Without enabling any option, treat the TLS payload as already inspected based on network metadata from VPC Flow Logs.
choices.explanation: Recording network flows does not decrypt TLS or evaluate application content.

choices.text: Inspect all outbound traffic from the corporate network and record unauthorized destinations without distinguishing them.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to limit inspection to the approved scope.

choices.text: Associate a Network Firewall TLS inspection scope limited to the approved traffic.
choices.explanation: Only traffic passing through the specified scope can be decrypted and inspected by the applicable stateful rules.

choices.text: Specify only the display name of the ACM certificate on the public server, without preparing the trust settings or CA for managed devices.
choices.explanation: The destination server's certificate alone does not configure the CA used for outbound inspection or trust on the client devices.

choices.text: Prepare the CA certificate required for outbound inspection and configure the target clients to trust that CA.
choices.explanation: The target clients can validate the certificate used on the inspection path and treat the connection as a normal TLS connection.

learning.reason: The target clients can validate the certificate used on the inspection path and treat the connection as a normal TLS connection. Only traffic passing through the specified scope can be decrypted and inspected by the applicable stateful rules.
learning.concept: The CA and traffic scope for Network Firewall outbound TLS inspection

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Rejecting creation of Pods that violate standards in tenant namespaces
prompt: In an EKS namespace, an organization wants to reject the creation of new Pods that violate an approved Pod Security Standards profile. A separate infrastructure namespace must retain its existing policy, and requests must not be accepted after merely issuing a warning. Which setting should be used?

choices.text: Restrict outbound traffic with a NetworkPolicy in the namespace and assume that privileged Pods will also be rejected at creation time by the same policy.
choices.explanation: Pod communication rules are separate from enforcement of the security profile in a Pod specification.

choices.text: Set Pod Security Admission in the target namespace to enforce mode for the specified profile.
choices.explanation: This rejects creation of new Pods that violate the profile in the target namespace.

choices.text: Enable ECR vulnerability scanning for container images and assume that ECR will also reject violating Pod specifications through the Kubernetes API.
choices.explanation: Image evaluation does not authorize or reject Pod specifications on a per-namespace basis.

choices.text: Set warn in the target namespace and treat requests that produce a warning for the client as rejected by the API.
choices.explanation: warn reports a warning; it does not reject the request in that mode.

learning.reason: This rejects creation of new Pods that violate the profile in the target namespace.
learning.concept: Namespace-specific enforce mode for Pod Security Admission

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Record authorized container investigation output in a dedicated log
prompt: During operational investigation using ECS Exec, the organization must collect not only connection records but also interactive session output in a CloudWatch log group dedicated to auditing. This must be separate from ordinary application logs. The image includes the required tools. Which configuration meets these requirements?

choices.text: Set the ECS Exec logging setting to NONE and assume that the task's standard log driver will always capture interactive output as well.
choices.explanation: This setting sends no session logs, so it does not provide an audit trail of interactive operations.

choices.text: Extend only the retention period of the existing application logs and leave the ExecuteCommand logging setting unchanged.
choices.explanation: Changing the retention period does not separate ECS Exec output into a dedicated log group.

choices.text: Enable CloudTrail and assume that the ExecuteCommand API event body always includes the interactive output.
choices.explanation: Auditing an API call and collecting the output of operations performed within the session are separate capabilities.

choices.text: Set the ExecuteCommand logging setting for the ECS cluster to OVERRIDE, and configure a dedicated log group and the required log-delivery permissions.
choices.explanation: This specifies the destination for session output and collects it separately from the application's own log destination.

learning.reason: This specifies the destination for session output and collects it separately from the application's own log destination.
learning.concept: ECS Exec OVERRIDE logging and session auditing

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Scan for missing patches before applying fixes
prompt: A standardized Systems Manager Patch Manager baseline is available. The production environment is currently in a change-freeze period, so patches cannot be installed and systems cannot be rebooted. However, the organization wants to collect missing-patch and compliance information in preparation for the next maintenance window. What should it run?

choices.text: Create a State Manager association that updates all packages to the latest versions, and save the resulting inventory as the missing-patch list.
choices.explanation: This changes the production environment and does not query the unapplied status based on the specified baseline.

choices.text: Run Install and set only the reboot option to NoReboot.
choices.explanation: Preventing a reboot does not prevent changes caused by patch installation.

choices.text: Run a baseline-based Scan on the target nodes.
choices.explanation: This checks compliance status and applicable patches without installing patches.

choices.text: Export only a host-name list from Systems Manager Inventory and treat every existing node as compliant.
choices.explanation: A list alone cannot determine missing patches against the baseline.

learning.reason: This checks compliance status and applicable patches without installing patches.
learning.concept: The difference between RunPatchBaseline Scan and Install

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Separate east-west communication between production and test while retaining shared connectivity
prompt: A production VPC and a test VPC are connected to the same Transit Gateway. Both VPCs must be able to connect to specified shared services, but routes between production and test must not be propagated to each other. What should be configured?

choices.text: Use the same security group name in subnets in both VPCs, and use that name to suppress route propagation between them.
choices.explanation: Security groups do not separate Transit Gateway routes or determine their propagation destinations.

choices.text: Associate the attachments with separate route tables and configure only the routes to the required shared services in each one.
choices.explanation: This separates forwarding destinations by attachment, retains access to shared services, and does not distribute routes between production and test.

choices.text: Remove the shared-services attachment and connect the VPCs directly through one route table.
choices.explanation: This removes access to the required shared services and leaves the inter-VPC connection that should be isolated.

choices.text: Exchange routes for all attachments through one default route table and assume that Transit Gateway distinguishes production from test by workload name.
choices.explanation: Transit Gateway does not separate routes based only on names.

learning.reason: This separates forwarding destinations by attachment, retains access to shared services, and does not distribute routes between production and test.
learning.concept: Transit Gateway attachment association and route propagation

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Require both user attributes and device posture for an internal application
prompt: Only employees who belong to a company-designated group and use a compliant managed device should be able to access an internal web application. The organization wants to avoid a design in which users see a broad network range after connecting to a VPN. The required identity provider and device-management service are available. Which configuration meets these requirements?

choices.text: Set only the corporate-network CIDR in the ALB security group and treat everyone connecting from that network as a member of the designated group.
choices.explanation: A source network does not represent a user's group membership or the device's compliance status.

choices.text: Allow everyone to connect to a shared VPN and add no additional user or device conditions to the application.
choices.explanation: This provides no fine-grained application access control and does not restrict the network range exposed after the VPN connection.

choices.text: Associate Verified Access with supported user-identity and device-trust providers, and evaluate both in the application's access conditions.
choices.explanation: Each application can require both the user's group membership and the device's compliance status.

choices.text: Use Verified Access to check only the user's group and do not evaluate device-trust information in the policy.
choices.explanation: This can verify the designated group but cannot reject noncompliant devices.

learning.reason: Each application can require both the user's group membership and the device's compliance status.
learning.concept: User and device trust information evaluated by Verified Access

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Distributing Existing Inspection Appliances Across Multiple Devices
prompt: An organization inspects approved VPC traffic using supported virtual security appliances. It must avoid pinning traffic to a single appliance and incorporate inspection into routing without changing the original application destination. Which AWS feature distributes the load across multiple inspection appliances?

choices.text: Use Route 53 to return the inspection appliance name with weighted responses, and change all application destination DNS names to the appliance name.
choices.explanation: This changes the name resolution visible to users, violating the requirement to inspect traffic without changing the original destination.

choices.text: Copy traffic with VPC Flow Logs and send it to the inspection appliances, assuming that allow and deny decisions will be applied inline to the actual workload packets.
choices.explanation: Flow records only provide observed traffic information; they do not send traffic through an inspection path or control forwarding.

choices.text: Use Gateway Load Balancer with the supported appliances as targets, and direct the relevant routes to a Gateway Load Balancer endpoint.
choices.explanation: This incorporates the appliances into an inline path without changing the application destination and distributes traffic across multiple targets.

choices.text: Use ALB HTTP path rules to route all IP traffic destined for the application to the virtual appliances.
choices.explanation: ALB is an HTTP-oriented entry point and does not provide a transparent network-inspection path that preserves the original destination.

learning.reason: It incorporates the inspection appliances into an inline path without changing the application destination and distributes traffic across multiple targets.
learning.concept: Gateway Load Balancer and endpoints for inspection appliances

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Failing Closed When DNS Inspection Cannot Be Confirmed
prompt: An organization uses Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall in an approved VPC. Internal policy requires queries that were not inspected to be denied when DNS Firewall cannot respond. The impact must be limited to the target VPC. What should be configured?

choices.text: Permanently disable DNS support for the VPC and eliminate all name resolution, including queries during normal operation.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to continue approved use during normal operation.

choices.text: Enable fail open so that queries continue normally even when Firewall does not respond.
choices.explanation: This allows queries when an inspection result cannot be obtained, contrary to the requirement.

choices.text: Extend the Resolver query-log retention period and treat DNS as having denied the query only when inspection is unavailable.
choices.explanation: Log settings do not control whether queries pass during an outage.

choices.text: Disable fail open for DNS Firewall in the target VPC so that queries fail when inspection does not respond.
choices.explanation: Queries are not allowed to pass when the rule-evaluation result cannot be confirmed.

learning.reason: Queries are not allowed to pass when the rule-evaluation result cannot be confirmed.
learning.concept: fail open and fail closed in Resolver DNS Firewall

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Connecting an Authenticated Public API to a Private Backend
prompt: An API Gateway HTTP API is called by existing clients with authentication. The backend is an internal ALB in the same AWS account, and no public entry point may be created for the backend. How should the integration be configured while preserving the API's public exposure?

choices.text: Create a VPC link and specify the internal ALB listener as the private integration target of the HTTP API.
choices.explanation: The API can connect to the VPC backend without exposing the internal ALB to the internet.

choices.text: Replace the internal ALB with an internet-facing ALB and control access operationally by allowing only use from API Gateway.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement not to create a public entry point for the backend.

choices.text: Delete the public API called by clients and require everyone to connect directly to the internal ALB through a VPN.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve the existing public API entry point.

choices.text: Change only the API resource name to private so that the existing public HTTP integration can reach the internal ALB.
choices.explanation: Changing a name does not create a network path to an integration target inside the VPC.

learning.reason: The API can connect to the VPC backend without exposing the internal ALB to the internet.
learning.concept: VPC links for HTTP API private integrations

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Restricting Operational Shell Access to the Responsible Service and Approved Sessions
prompt: Private connectivity is already configured, and operators use Session Manager to manage only EC2 instances tagged for their responsible service. They must also be prevented from using arbitrary session documents; only sessions using an audit-configured document may be allowed. What should be reflected in the permissions?

choices.text: Allow the operator IAM identity to use StartSession on all instances, and rename EC2 instances to distinguish those outside the operator's responsibility.
choices.explanation: Name-based classification alone does not deny sessions to instances outside the operator's responsibility.

choices.text: Configure the audit document ARN but allow the operator to use StartSession on all instances.
choices.explanation: Restricting the document still allows connections to hosts outside the operator's responsibility.

choices.text: Allow StartSession to EC2 instances with the target tag and restrict usable session documents to the audit document ARN.
choices.explanation: The operator's IAM permissions can separately control the connection targets and the sessions that may be used.

choices.text: Add the responsible-service tag to the SSM Agent role and allow the operator to use all documents.
choices.explanation: A tag on the agent itself does not restrict the operator's authorization to use session documents.

learning.reason: The operator's IAM permissions can separately control the connection targets and the sessions that may be used.
learning.concept: Authorization for StartSession target instances and session documents

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Reviewing Excessive Deployment Permissions Using Observed APIs
prompt: A CI role has many permissions. Based on CloudTrail records from a representative past release period, you want to create a policy whose candidates are the operations that were actually used. Because some legitimate paths are used rarely, you will not replace the policy automatically; an administrator will review the resource scope. Which approach should you use?

choices.text: Use IAM Access Analyzer policy generation, and review the resources and infrequently required operations before associating the candidates.
choices.explanation: Candidates can be derived from activity during the observation period, while legitimate operations not observed and the resource scope can be reviewed separately.

choices.text: Run the organization’s external access analyzer and use resources with findings that allow external access as the list of CI operations.
choices.explanation: External-sharing findings are not candidates for the business operations performed by the target role.

choices.text: Record only the total number of CloudTrail events and assume that all existing permissions were used on days with a high event count.
choices.explanation: Permission usage cannot be determined from the aggregate event count.

choices.text: Without providing new candidates to policy validation, adopt only the permissions in the current policy that have no syntax warnings as used permissions.
choices.explanation: Syntax validation does not extract the operations actually used from CloudTrail.

learning.reason: Candidates can be derived from activity during the observation period, while legitimate operations not observed and the resource scope can be reviewed separately.
learning.concept: Policy generation based on CloudTrail operation history

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Rotating a SCIM Access Token Without Interrupting Group Synchronization
prompt: A token used for SCIM synchronization from an external IdP to IAM Identity Center is nearing expiration. You must preserve current authentication and account assignments, and you can disable the old token after confirming the synchronization target’s connection. Assuming that a new token can be added, what should you do?

choices.text: Increase the IAM Identity Center user session duration and assume that the SCIM token expiration is extended as well.
choices.explanation: The portal session duration and the synchronization API token expiration are separate settings.

choices.text: Issue a new token, update the IdP’s SCIM integration, confirm that synchronization succeeds, and then disable the old token.
choices.explanation: This confirms that synchronization can use the new credentials without changing the current access assignments.

choices.text: Delete the old token first, wait for IdP SCIM authentication to fail, and then issue a new one.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the requirement to keep existing synchronization active until testing is complete.

choices.text: Rotate only the IdP’s SAML signing certificate and continue using the expired SCIM integration token.
choices.explanation: SAML authentication and the token used for SCIM provisioning are separate.

learning.reason: This confirms that synchronization can use the new credentials without changing the current access assignments.
learning.concept: Issuing a new SCIM token, updating the IdP, and disabling the old token

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Connecting a Private Worker to a Regional STS Endpoint
prompt: In a VPC with no internet egress, you configured an STS interface endpoint in the same Region and private DNS. The existing SDK configuration fails because it uses the global hostname. What should you change while preserving the role permissions and operational network?

choices.text: Disable private DNS and add a route that connects to the global STS address through NAT.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to avoid creating internet egress.

choices.text: Continue using the global STS hostname, add permissions to the role, and enable the network path as well.
choices.explanation: Increasing IAM permissions does not change the DNS resolution or destination selected by the default hostname.

choices.text: Specify the IAM hostname instead of STS and assume that any IAM API issues credentials for role assumption.
choices.explanation: Role assumption is an API operation to STS and cannot be replaced with another IAM API.

choices.text: Configure the SDK to use the STS endpoint for the appropriate Region and confirm that the hostname resolves to the VPC endpoint.
choices.explanation: Using the regional hostname allows the already provisioned private connection to be used.

learning.reason: Using the regional hostname allows the already provisioned private connection to be used.
learning.concept: STS interface endpoints and regional calls

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Allowing Only a Specific API Route to a System Using an AWS Role
prompt: An internal worker in the same account already uses temporary credentials from an AWS role. Without adding an external JWT issuer, you must allow access to only one route of an API Gateway HTTP API. What should you configure? Select two.

choices.text: Configure AWS_IAM authorization on the target route and send requests signed with AWS credentials from the worker.
choices.explanation: API Gateway can validate the AWS signature and evaluate the caller as an AWS principal.

choices.text: Set the worker’s role name in the API Gateway access logs and leave API authorization as NONE.
choices.explanation: A logging value does not validate the caller, and public requests are not rejected by authorization.

choices.text: Allow execute-api:Invoke for the target route in the worker’s role.
choices.explanation: The existing role can restrict access to the API route that it is actually permitted to invoke.

choices.text: Grant the worker’s role only API Gateway configuration permissions and assume that they also apply to the data plane.
choices.explanation: API management operations and invocation permissions through execute-api are separate.

choices.text: Pass the worker’s role access key directly as a Bearer token to the HTTP API JWT authorizer.
choices.explanation: An AWS access key is not a token signed by a JWT issuer.

learning.reason: API Gateway can validate the AWS signature and evaluate the caller as an AWS principal. The existing role can restrict access to the API route that it is actually permitted to invoke.
learning.concept: AWS_IAM authorization and execute-api invocation permissions for an HTTP API

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Replace an Existing EC2 Instance’s IAM Role Without Stopping It
prompt: An application running on an EC2 instance must transition from the instance profile initially associated with the instance so that it receives a new, more restricted AWS role. The new profile is ready, and the instance cannot be stopped. Which EC2 operation should be used?

choices.text: Replace the IAM instance profile association on the running EC2 instance and verify with the SDK that it obtains the new credentials.
choices.explanation: The association that provides AWS credentials to EC2 can be updated while the instance is running.

choices.text: Recreate the AMI, terminate the original EC2 instance, and launch another instance with the new role.
choices.explanation: This can launch a new instance, but it does not meet the requirement to avoid stopping the existing EC2 instance.

choices.text: Change only the default version of the launch template and assume that the association on the existing instance changes immediately.
choices.explanation: The launch template configuration does not change the profile currently attached to an existing instance.

choices.text: Store access keys for the new role permanently on the host as environment variables and continue using the old profile.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to obtain temporary role credentials through the EC2 association.

learning.reason: The association that provides AWS credentials to EC2 can be updated while the instance is running.
learning.concept: Replacing an IAM instance profile association on a running instance

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Limit the Permissions Used by a Service Role for a Shared Stack
prompt: An existing stack has a CloudFormation service role associated with it. Stack updates are delegated to several operations staff members, but they should not need to specify another unvalidated role, and stack operations must not expand permissions beyond their business responsibilities. What should be reviewed?

choices.text: Remove only iam:PassRole from the staff members and allow stack updates while leaving the existing service role broadly permitted.
choices.explanation: The already associated role is used by later stack operations, so reviewing PassRole alone does not restrict an overly privileged role.

choices.text: Distinguish staff members only through stack tags while keeping the current service role and stack-update permissions.
choices.explanation: Adding tags alone restricts neither update authorization nor the permissions of the role.

choices.text: Give the service role administrator permissions and consider the setup restricted because the staff members have no direct IAM permission to operate resources.
choices.explanation: The permissions of the service role used to perform changes are separate from the staff members’ permissions to operate resources directly.

choices.text: Grant the stack service role only the least privilege required for the target resources and restrict staff members’ updates to approved stack operations.
choices.explanation: Because the associated role is used for stack operations, both the role itself and the resources it can affect must be restricted.

learning.reason: Because the associated role is used for stack operations, both the role itself and the resources it can affect must be restricted.
learning.concept: Delegating stack operations and controlling the execution role of an existing stack

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Grant Temporary Read Access Based on Groups of Analytics Users
prompt: The analytics platform can identify users from IAM Identity Center. The data is stored in a shared S3 bucket, and each group has a different readable prefix. Location registration and user authentication integration are already complete. How should authorization be provided without using permanent shared keys?

choices.text: Add directory group names as filters in S3 Storage Lens and treat the range shown in reports as read permission.
choices.explanation: Usage visibility and permission to read S3 objects are separate concerns.

choices.text: Duplicate fixed keys for the same IAM user for each group and have the application infer the prefix-based access range.
choices.explanation: Shared permanent credentials do not meet the requirement to obtain short-lived credentials for each group.

choices.text: Create grants for the directory groups and permitted prefixes, then read using temporary credentials scoped to the authorized range.
choices.explanation: The credentials obtained can be limited to the specified resources, with the range managed according to the user’s group.

choices.text: Grant a common execution role read access to every prefix and assume that anything hidden by the analytics UI is also denied by authorization.
choices.explanation: Hiding data in the interface is different from restricting the underlying AWS credentials to a data range.

learning.reason: The credentials obtained can be limited to the specified resources, with the range managed according to the user’s group.
learning.concept: Data-scope grants and credentials with S3 Access Grants

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Move to New EKS Access Management While Keeping Existing Users
prompt: EKS currently maps existing IAM principals through the aws-auth ConfigMap. The team will manage new principals with access entries through the EKS API. All existing mappings will be migrated gradually, and legacy users must not be locked out from the beginning of the migration. What should be done? Select two.

choices.text: Change to API-only mode first and assume that principals not yet registered as access entries can still authenticate as before.
choices.explanation: This removes the path used by principals that are registered only in the ConfigMap at the start of the migration.

choices.text: Delete the old ConfigMap first and assume that legacy users can continue operating as long as their IAM permissions allow access to all AWS APIs.
choices.explanation: IAM permissions for AWS APIs alone do not provide the same authentication path to the cluster.

choices.text: Register the new IAM principals as access entries and grant only the required cluster access.
choices.explanation: The access of new principals required to begin the migration can be managed individually through the new method.

choices.text: Keep the authentication mode as CONFIG_MAP and wait for access entries to be generated automatically through the EKS API.
choices.explanation: In ConfigMap-only mode, access entries are not enabled.

choices.text: Set the cluster to the API_AND_CONFIG_MAP authentication mode.
choices.explanation: This enables access entries while preserving authentication through the existing ConfigMap.

learning.reason: API_AND_CONFIG_MAP enables access entries while preserving authentication through the existing ConfigMap. New principals required to begin the migration can then be managed individually through the new method.
learning.concept: Phased EKS authentication migration with API_AND_CONFIG_MAP

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Assigning business API scopes to a batch that has no human sign-in
prompt: Two internal backends call a business API without human interaction. A Cognito user pool is the issuer, and the API uses a predefined custom scope for read access. Neither a browser nor a user identity is involved in the path. Which approach should be used?

choices.text: Use an authorization code flow that requires user interaction in the application, and require an operator to sign in for every batch run.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement for operation without interaction.

choices.text: Enable the client credentials flow for a server-side client and include the required custom scope.
choices.explanation: The workload authenticates as a client and can obtain an access token without a user sign-in.

choices.text: Treat the temporary AWS credentials issued by a Cognito identity pool as the JWT's custom scope.
choices.explanation: Credentials used to sign requests to AWS resources are different from OAuth scopes consumed by a business API.

choices.text: Do not place a client secret in a public client, and request arbitrary scopes without authenticating either the user or the client.
choices.explanation: Machine-to-machine access does not mean that access should be allowed without client authentication.

learning.reason: The workload authenticates as a client and can obtain an access token without a user sign-in.
learning.concept: Cognito machine-to-machine authentication and OAuth client authentication

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Managing files from another account with the bucket owner's policies
prompt: An ETL process in another account uploads output files to the target S3 bucket. The bucket-owning account must manage the objects, and no ETL client may depend on specifying ACLs. Upload permissions can be coordinated through the bucket policy and IAM. Which S3 setting should be used?

choices.text: Set Object writer, allow the sending account to own the objects, and infer the bucket owner's permissions from the ACL.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement that the bucket owner consistently own the objects.

choices.text: Set Bucket owner preferred and require an ACL for each client that grants control to the bucket owner.
choices.explanation: Even though ownership can be aligned, this configuration depends on the uploader specifying an ACL.

choices.text: Set Bucket owner enforced and manage access through bucket and IAM policies.
choices.explanation: This disables ACLs, makes the bucket owner the object owner, and does not require users to specify ACLs.

choices.text: Block only public access and leave the object ownership setting and ACLs unchanged.
choices.explanation: Changing only public-access behavior does not standardize object ownership or ACLs for cross-account-created objects.

learning.reason: ACLs are disabled, the bucket owner owns the objects, and users are not required to specify ACLs.
learning.concept: S3 Object Ownership and Bucket owner enforced

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Verifying a policy with conditions through simulation and real-world testing
prompt: An administrator is testing conditional permissions in a new IAM policy. Before actually calling an AWS service API, the administrator evaluates the policy with different expected condition values and also verifies the actual permissions in a test environment before applying the policy. What should the administrator do?

choices.text: Specify the condition context values and simulate the policy, then verify the result in a test environment that closely resembles the real environment.
choices.explanation: This allows the administrator to compare the policy document and condition results without applying the policy. Actual authorization involving configurations that were not reproduced can be checked separately.

choices.text: Omit all values required by the conditions when running the simulation, and assume that the real API will always produce the same result.
choices.explanation: Evaluation can differ depending on the condition inputs and the actual service and policy configuration.

choices.text: Confirm that there is no event for the target API in CloudTrail and conclude that the candidate policy authorizes the operation.
choices.explanation: Whether an API operation that has not been executed would be allowed by the new configuration cannot be determined from the absence of a previous record.

choices.text: Make the production change only with an administrator role that has broader permissions, and treat its success as the authorization result of the candidate policy.
choices.explanation: Success by a different principal is not evidence that the candidate policy's conditions work as expected.

learning.reason: The policy document and condition results can be compared without applying the policy. Actual authorization involving configurations that were not reproduced can be checked separately.
learning.concept: IAM Policy Simulator context inputs and verification in the actual environment

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Restricting only one job session without changing the standard role
prompt: A data operations role maintains multiple tables. For a one-time investigation job, only reads from one table should be allowed when the same role is assumed. The permissions of the role for other executions cannot be changed, and the job does not need permissions beyond those of the original role. What should be passed?

choices.text: Temporarily replace the managed policy used by all jobs and restore it after the investigation is complete.
choices.explanation: The permission change would also affect executions other than the investigation.

choices.text: In the role-assumption request, specify a session policy that allows only reads from the target table.
choices.explanation: The session is limited to operations allowed by both the role and the additional session constraint.

choices.text: Add the table ARN as a principal in the role's trust relationship and thereby restrict reads by the investigation job.
choices.explanation: The trust policy controls who can assume the role; it does not restrict the tables accessed by a session.

choices.text: Set the target table name as the role-assumption session name and assume that IAM reduces permissions based on the name alone.
choices.explanation: A session name is an identifying value and does not restrict target resources without explicit authorization rules.

learning.reason: The session is limited to operations allowed by both the role and the additional session constraint.
learning.concept: Restricting permissions through the intersection of an STS session policy

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Perform the first approved read without waiting for grant propagation
prompt: A workload worker must decrypt specified data using a newly created KMS grant. The grant is currently subject to propagation delay, although both the grant details and the worker's credentials are correct. How should the worker start the first operation immediately without broadening the key policy?

choices.text: Create the same grant repeatedly and assume that all of them become effective immediately once the count increases.
choices.explanation: Creating additional grants does not provide a way to use one approved grant immediately.

choices.text: Switch the alias of the KMS key in use and assume that the current grant is immediately attached to another key as well.
choices.explanation: Changing an alias does not transfer a grant from the original key to another key.

choices.text: List the grant ID as a principal in the key policy and do not use the grant token.
choices.explanation: A grant ID is not a user's principal, nor is it the token passed to KMS to recognize a newly created grant.

choices.text: Pass the grant token returned when the grant was created in the worker's decryption request.
choices.explanation: Even before the permission has propagated everywhere, KMS can evaluate a request that uses the grant.

learning.reason: Even before the permission has propagated everywhere, KMS can evaluate a request that uses the grant.
learning.concept: KMS grant tokens and eventual consistency

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Make the vault immutable after verifying the retention settings
prompt: A vault for long-term backups needs a period immediately after deployment during which its settings and restores can be tested. After that period, the vault must be operated so that even an administrator with powerful permissions cannot unlock it. Which Vault Lock setting should be used?

choices.text: Specify only the retention period in the backup plan and do not configure vault locking.
choices.explanation: A normal retention-period setting does not forcefully reject deletion by a highly privileged user during that period.

choices.text: Configure the compliance mode grace period, verify the configuration within that period, and wait for it to elapse.
choices.explanation: The configuration can be reviewed during the grace period; after it elapses, the lock cannot be changed or deleted.

choices.text: Tag the vault as immutable and count the verification period from the day the tag is applied.
choices.explanation: A tag alone does not configure the Vault Lock grace period or its immutable behavior.

choices.text: Configure governance mode and assume that unlocking becomes impossible after the period elapses, regardless of administrative permissions.
choices.explanation: In governance mode, authorized users can change or delete the configuration.

learning.reason: The configuration can be reviewed during the grace period; after it elapses, the lock cannot be changed or deleted.
learning.concept: AWS Backup Vault Lock compliance mode and the grace period

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Check revocation status with a per-certificate query
prompt: An organization issues new client certificates with AWS Private CA. Consumers must use the supported online feature to check whether a certificate has been revoked without downloading the entire revocation list. What should be enabled on the CA?

choices.text: Manage status using only the certificate's DNS record as a substitute for OCSP, and do not configure a revocation method on the CA.
choices.explanation: The presence or absence of a normal DNS record is not evidence of a revocation status confirmed by the CA.

choices.text: Enable managed OCSP so that supported clients can query the certificate's revocation status.
choices.explanation: OCSP returns the status of an individual certificate rather than distributing a list of revoked certificates to clients.

choices.text: Remove the CA certificate from the trust store each time and infer whether it is subject to revocation from failures for all certificates.
choices.explanation: This cannot determine the revocation status of a specific certificate and would also affect valid certificates.

choices.text: Enable only a CRL and have each client retrieve the list, assuming that an individual query will not read the entire list.
choices.explanation: With a CRL, the revocation list is retrieved to determine the status.

learning.reason: OCSP returns the status of an individual certificate rather than distributing a list of revoked certificates to clients.
learning.concept: AWS Private CA managed OCSP and CRLs

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Retrieve the latest secret in the recovery Region
prompt: An application may fail over to another Region. A single Secrets Manager secret is rotated in the primary Region. In the failover Region, the application must read a secret protected by a local KMS key without operating two independent rotation processes. What should be configured?

choices.text: Delete the primary secret, write the value manually in both Regions, and maintain one rotation state.
choices.explanation: This does not configure the primary secret's normal rotation together with a replica that automatically receives updates.

choices.text: Create an independent secret with the same name in the failover Region, set its initial value, and assume it will automatically follow rotation in the primary Region.
choices.explanation: Creating a secret with the same name does not establish a replication relationship.

choices.text: Have every client in the failover Region reference only the primary Region and assume that the value remains updated even when the primary Region cannot be reached.
choices.explanation: This does not provide a local copy for use during a Regional outage.

choices.text: Create a replica of the primary secret in the failover Region and specify the KMS key to use there.
choices.explanation: Updates to the primary are reflected in the replica, allowing the failover Region to read its local secret.

learning.reason: Updates to the primary are reflected in the replica, allowing the failover Region to read its local secret.
learning.concept: A replica in another Region that receives updates from the primary secret

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Store Macie discovery results as long-term audit records
prompt: For Macie sensitive data discovery, you want to retain evaluation details for the long term, including objects in which no sensitive data was found and objects that could not be inspected. The destination is a specified S3 bucket, using a customer managed key. What should you configure?

choices.text: Select only the Macie findings you need and treat every file with no sensitive data as included in the same finding.
choices.explanation: The set of sensitive data findings differs from the set of discovery results, which also includes results with no finding.

choices.text: Configure a repository for Macie sensitive data discovery results and provide the required permissions for the destination bucket and KMS key.
choices.explanation: You can output and retain object-level analysis results, not just findings, in a location you manage.

choices.text: Enable only bucket encryption and wait for automatic retention without configuring Macie’s output settings.
choices.explanation: Even if the bucket uses KMS, Macie does not deliver detailed results unless you configure the repository destination.

choices.text: Enable sensitive data sample viewing in Macie and treat the values that can be displayed as the audit trail for all objects.
choices.explanation: Retrieving samples does not retain the evaluation results for all objects.

learning.reason: You can output and retain object-level analysis results, not just findings, in a location you manage.
learning.concept: Repository for storing Macie sensitive data discovery results

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Meet a control requiring two layers of storage encryption
prompt: New objects in an S3 bucket used for auditing must receive two independent layers of server-side encryption at rest, using a specified customer managed KMS key. The write clients must not implement custom encryption. Which method should you choose?

choices.text: Choose DSSE-KMS for the bucket’s default encryption, using the specified customer managed key.
choices.explanation: S3 performs two layers of encryption at rest and can use the required KMS key.

choices.text: Enable only SSE-S3 and add the ARN of the customer managed key to a bucket tag.
choices.explanation: Adding the ARN to a tag does not change how SSE-S3 manages keys.

choices.text: Require TLS, use SSE-S3, and count encryption in transit and encryption at rest as two storage layers.
choices.explanation: Protection with TLS in transit does not count as a layer of encryption at rest.

choices.text: Enable the S3 Bucket Key for SSE-KMS and assume that one SSE-KMS encryption becomes two layers.
choices.explanation: The Bucket Key optimizes KMS usage; it does not provide the two encryption operations of DSSE-KMS.

learning.reason: S3 performs two layers of encryption at rest and can use the required KMS key.
learning.concept: Two-layer server-side encryption with S3 DSSE-KMS

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Allow only the KMS operations required by SQS producers and consumers
prompt: An SQS queue uses a customer managed KMS key. The producer role sends messages, and the consumer role receives them. The SQS send and receive permissions are already correct. Which KMS permissions are required for the corresponding key? Select two.

choices.text: Allow the producer role to use kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt on the key.
choices.explanation: These permissions are required in the path for creating and validating data keys when the SQS producer is authorized.

choices.text: Assume that every user who knows the queue URL can use KMS without changing the SQS key policy.
choices.explanation: A queue identifier does not grant authorization to use a KMS key.

choices.text: Grant the consumer role only kms:GenerateDataKey and do not add permission to decrypt stored messages.
choices.explanation: The permissions required to decrypt existing messages would be missing.

choices.text: Allow the consumer role to use kms:Decrypt on the key.
choices.explanation: The consumer must be allowed to decrypt with the corresponding key to consume encrypted messages.

choices.text: Add only kms:Encrypt to the producer role and assume that data-key generation and decryption can be used without permission.
choices.explanation: This does not provide the SSE-KMS permissions required by the producer.

learning.reason: The producer needs kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt in the data-key path, while the consumer needs kms:Decrypt to consume encrypted messages.
learning.concept: Different SSE-KMS permissions for SQS producers and consumers

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Batch-validate the integrity of existing S3 data
prompt: For a large archive, the expected checksums after writing are recorded in a ledger. Obtain comparison checksums in bulk from the current contents of the existing S3 objects without downloading them to the application. How should you do this?

choices.text: Compare only the sizes in S3 Inventory and assume that byte-for-byte contents are identical when the sizes match.
choices.explanation: Different contents can have the same size. Comparing sizes is not a content checksum.

choices.text: Pass the targets to an S3 Batch Operations checksum computation job and compare the completion report with expected values generated using the same method.
choices.explanation: The checksums are computed from the objects in storage, allowing validation without retrieving the full object bodies in the application.

choices.text: Compare the ETag of every object directly with a checksum of any method recorded in the ledger.
choices.explanation: An ETag does not necessarily represent the same content checksum for every upload method.

choices.text: Update the bucket’s encryption at rest and verify the identity of each object solely from the encryption type.
choices.explanation: The encryption configuration is separate from whether the object’s current contents match the expected value.

learning.reason: Checksums can be computed from the objects in storage, allowing validation without retrieving the full object bodies in the application.
learning.concept: Computing checksums with S3 Batch Operations and comparing them with known values

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Investigate per-version encryption at rest without relying on access records
prompt: For a large versioned S3 bucket, an auditor must periodically review the at-rest encryption status of each object version in a report. The team will not operate custom collection that calls the S3 API for each object. What should be configured?

choices.text: Retrieve the bucket's current default encryption configuration once and assume that the same encryption is used for all existing versions.
choices.explanation: The current default configuration does not show the per-version encryption status of versions written previously.

choices.text: Include all versions in S3 Inventory and output the encryption status as an additional field.
choices.explanation: Object versions and their encryption status can be individually reconciled in a periodic report.

choices.text: Record CloudTrail read events for only one month and treat versions that were never read as encrypted.
choices.explanation: Read events cannot verify the at-rest encryption status of objects that were not accessed.

choices.text: Output only the total size from storage metrics and infer the encryption method of every version individually.
choices.explanation: An aggregate size does not show which encryption method each version uses.

learning.reason: Object versions and their encryption status can be individually reconciled in a periodic report.
learning.concept: All versions and encryption-status attributes in S3 Inventory

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Use the latest SecureString at runtime without updating the stack
prompt: The SecureString used by an application is updated in Systems Manager Parameter Store. A value configured through the current CloudFormation dynamic reference is not reflected in the application's configuration unless the stack is updated. Which design periodically retrieves the latest value at runtime without storing plaintext in the template?

choices.text: Pin an old SecureString version in the application configuration and retrieve that same pinned version again when an update is detected.
choices.explanation: Retrieving the same version does not make the new value available.

choices.text: Leave the current CloudFormation dynamic reference unchanged and assume that the already configured value is immediately re-evaluated even without an update.
choices.explanation: A dynamic reference is resolved during stack processing; it does not continuously redistribute values to the application's configuration independently.

choices.text: Pass the parameter name to the application and have its runtime role periodically retrieve the value from Parameter Store.
choices.explanation: The secret itself is not stored in the stack, and changes can be reflected according to the application's retrieval frequency.

choices.text: Expose the plaintext value in the template's Outputs and assume that Outputs change in real time when Parameter Store is updated.
choices.explanation: This exposes the plaintext secret in the template's outputs and does not provide a mechanism for retrieving the latest value at runtime.

learning.reason: The secret itself is not stored in the stack, and changes can be reflected according to the application's retrieval frequency.
learning.concept: CloudFormation value resolution and application retrieval at runtime

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Migrate cache clients to TLS in stages
prompt: A team must enforce encryption in transit for an existing compatible ElastiCache for Redis OSS replication group. Multiple clients cannot be updated at once, and clients not yet updated must continue operating during the migration period. Which approach satisfies both requirements?

choices.text: Configure encryption at rest only and conclude that encryption in transit from clients is also enforced.
choices.explanation: Encryption of storage and TLS for client connections are independent settings.

choices.text: Start with preferred, which allows both TLS and non-TLS connections, then switch to required after all clients have migrated to TLS.
choices.explanation: Clients can be migrated sequentially, after which non-TLS connections can be disallowed.

choices.text: Change to required immediately and assume that non-TLS clients automatically maintain the same connections.
choices.explanation: Clients that do not use TLS will no longer be permitted to connect.

choices.text: Finish the migration by changing only to preferred and treat all non-TLS connections as already rejected by the service.
choices.explanation: preferred also accepts non-TLS connections, so it does not meet the final-state requirement.

learning.reason: Clients can be migrated sequentially, after which non-TLS connections can be disallowed.
learning.concept: Migration using preferred and required for encryption in transit

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Resume decryption with a KMS key whose scheduled deletion was canceled
prompt: A KMS key with AWS-generated key material is in PendingDeletion. The deletion has not occurred, and approval has been granted to cancel it and verify decryption. Select the three operations in order to verify recovery by decrypting existing ciphertext with the same key.

choices.text: Cancel the scheduled deletion of the key.
choices.explanation: Because deletion has not occurred, canceling the schedule starts the process of making the key usable again.

choices.text: Enable the key.
choices.explanation: After cancellation, the key becomes Disabled, so it must be enabled before cryptographic operations can be performed.

choices.text: Decrypt the existing ciphertext used for recovery verification.
choices.explanation: Finally, verify that existing ciphertext can be decrypted with the original key.

choices.text: Change the original key to a different alias and leave the scheduled deletion in place.
choices.explanation: Changing an alias does not change the key's scheduled deletion or its cryptographic-operation state.

learning.reason: Cancel the schedule before deletion, enable the key after it returns to Disabled, and finally verify that existing ciphertext can be decrypted with the original key.
learning.concept: The order for explicitly enabling a key that returns to Disabled after cancellation of scheduled deletion

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Capturing Brief Configuration Changes That Daily Recording Would Miss
prompt: An AWS Config customer-managed recorder records many resource types daily. For security groups, rules that are added and reverted within a sufficiently short interval must also be recorded. All other resource types must remain on daily recording. What should be configured?

choices.text: Change the default recording frequency to continuous and continuously record all other resource types without individual overrides.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to keep unspecified resource types on daily recording.
