choices.text: Override the security group resource type to use continuous recording while retaining the default daily recording for all other resource types.
choices.explanation: This records only the specified resource type whenever its configuration changes.

choices.text: Increase aggregator updates and assume that the aggregator centrally fills in changes that were not recorded by the source account's daily recording.
choices.explanation: Aggregation does not reconstruct configurations that the source recorder did not record.

choices.text: Extend the retention period of the S3 destination used by AWS Config and assume that brief changes not collected daily will also be stored.
choices.explanation: Changing the retention period does not add intermediate states that were never recorded.

learning.reason: The specified resource type can be configured to be recorded whenever its configuration changes.
learning.concept: Overriding the recording frequency for a specific resource type

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Deploying the Same Security Foundation to New Members
prompt: Use CloudFormation StackSets to deploy audit roles and other resources to an OU. When an account is added to the OU, deploy the resources automatically; when an account is removed from the OU, retain those resources for investigation. The Organizations integration is already prepared. Which two settings should be configured? Select two.

choices.text: Manually create stacks with the same name in each member's Region and do not use StackSets deployment when accounts are added to the OU.
choices.explanation: This does not provide organization-wide deployment that follows the addition of members.

choices.text: For the behavior when an account is removed from the target, choose the setting that retains the stack in the target account.
choices.explanation: When the account is removed from the organization or target OU, the stack is not deleted and remains in the account.

choices.text: Disable automatic deployment and assume that adding an account to the OU will automatically create the stack in the new account.
choices.explanation: With the setting that follows account additions disabled, the stack is not created automatically.

choices.text: Configure a service-managed StackSet targeting the OU and enable automatic deployment.
choices.explanation: When a new member account enters the target OU, the stack can be deployed to the target Regions.

choices.text: Choose the setting that deletes the associated stack when an account leaves the target, and assume that the resources do not need to be investigated before deletion.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to retain resources for investigation after the account leaves the target.

learning.reason: When a new member account enters the target OU, the stack can be deployed to the target Regions. When the account leaves the organization or target OU, the stack is not deleted and remains in the account.
learning.concept: StackSets automatic deployment and stack retention on removal

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Enforcing a Safe EC2 Account Attribute Across an OU
prompt: In a regulated OU, keep the EC2 Serial Console account setting in a state where the feature itself is disabled. In addition to IAM controls over who can change the setting, the organization wants to use a method that specifies account attributes for the EC2 service. What should be configured?

choices.text: Set serial-console-off as an EC2 tag and assume that the entire account inherits the same effect.
choices.explanation: An instance tag does not change the account-level Serial Console setting.

choices.text: Close the SSH port in a security group and assume that the Serial Console account attribute is automatically disabled as well.
choices.explanation: Network rules for instances and the EC2 Serial Console account setting are separate.

choices.text: Only record attribute changes with CloudTrail and assume that the setting remains disabled as long as a record exists.
choices.explanation: Recording operations does not disable the attribute.

choices.text: Use an EC2 declarative policy to specify that Serial Console access is disabled and apply it to the target OU.
choices.explanation: The organization can declare and apply the relevant EC2 account attribute.

learning.reason: The organization can declare and apply the relevant EC2 account attribute.
learning.concept: Organizations EC2 declarative policies and account attributes

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Reporting Noncompliant Inbound Rules in Each Team's Security Groups
prompt: In an organization that meets the prerequisites for Firewall Manager, apply a common inbound standard to the security groups in a target OU. At this stage, report violating rules without automatically deleting or replacing the teams' existing rules. Which approach should be selected?

choices.text: Aggregate only rejected traffic from VPC Flow Logs and treat the result as a complete list of violating rules, including unused configuration rules.
choices.explanation: Traffic records cannot provide a comprehensive audit of configuration rules that have not yet been used.

choices.text: Enforce a common security group, enable automatic remediation, and replace all existing groups.
choices.explanation: This changes business-owned rules instead of auditing them first.

choices.text: Apply a content audit policy to the target OU, disable automatic remediation, and review the results.
choices.explanation: This compares the contents of existing security groups with the standard and reports findings at this stage.

choices.text: Configure only HTTP rules in an AWS WAF Web ACL and use them to evaluate inbound port rules in all security groups.
choices.explanation: A Web ACL does not audit the configuration list of security groups.

learning.reason: The contents of existing security groups can be compared with the standard and treated as findings at this stage.
learning.concept: Firewall Manager security group content auditing

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Accept an AWS agreement centrally for the entire organization
prompt: An authorized contracts administrator reviewed an agreement offered to the organization in AWS Artifact. The agreement should apply to all members of the target AWS Organizations organization. Which procedure should be used to avoid repeating the same acceptance process in each member account?

choices.text: Accept it as an account agreement in any member account and assume that it is automatically applied across the organization.
choices.explanation: Acceptance by an individual account is not acceptance by the management account of an organization agreement.

choices.text: Download the AWS audit report in Artifact and treat the download as acceptance of the organization agreement.
choices.explanation: Downloading a report does not put the agreement into an accepted state.

choices.text: Tag the Organizations OU with the agreement name and consider the accounts consented when they have the corresponding tag.
choices.explanation: Organization resource tags are not an operation for accepting an organization agreement in AWS Artifact.

choices.text: Use the appropriate permissions in the organization's management account to accept it as an organization agreement in Artifact.
choices.explanation: An agreement that applies across the organization can be processed through the organization agreement operation.

learning.reason: An agreement that applies across the organization can be processed through the organization agreement operation.
learning.concept: Organization agreements and account agreements in AWS Artifact

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Consolidate findings when the same control appears in multiple standards
prompt: In Security Hub CSPM with multiple standards enabled, findings for the same resource and control are created separately for each standard, resulting in duplicate remediation work for the same configuration. All required standards must remain enabled, but the findings should be consolidated at the control level. Which setting should be configured?

choices.text: Enable control finding consolidation.
choices.explanation: Even when the same control is included in multiple standards, findings for each evaluated resource can be consolidated across standards.

choices.text: Enable only cross-Region aggregation and assume that findings from different standards will be consolidated when they are collected in the same Region.
choices.explanation: Cross-Region delivery and consolidation of control findings across standards are separate features.

choices.text: Keep only one standard to avoid duplication and replace the requirements of the other standards with logs.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the condition that multiple required standards must remain enabled.

choices.text: Periodically archive every finding except the first one and stop checking which standard and control produced it.
choices.explanation: This only hides findings afterward and does not change the unit at which findings are generated. It can also cause other important findings to be missed.

learning.reason: Even when the same control is included in multiple standards, findings for each evaluated resource can be consolidated across standards.
learning.concept: Consolidated control findings in Security Hub CSPM

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Grant separate permissions for resolving a shared table name and reading its rows
prompt: A table shared from another account through Lake Formation is read with Athena. The administrator on the receiving side can delegate permissions for the shared resource, and a resource link has already been created in the catalog. The analytics role should be allowed only to view the link and read rows from the table. Which two permissions should be verified? Select two.

choices.text: Grant only permission to view the link and assume that SELECT on the target is granted automatically.
choices.explanation: Permissions on the resource link and on the target table are independent.

choices.text: Grant SELECT on a different table that does not use the resource link and assume that the permission applies to the target when the names match.
choices.explanation: Matching names alone do not cause authorization on a different table to be evaluated for the target.

choices.text: Allow the analytics role DESCRIBE on the receiving side's resource link.
choices.explanation: This grants the link permission needed to view the appropriate shared resource in the catalog.

choices.text: Allow the analytics role SELECT on the shared target table.
choices.explanation: Separate from permission to view the link, this grants permission to read data from the source table.

choices.text: Make the analytics role a data lake administrator so that it can grant permissions on other unauthorized tables as well.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the condition of granting only permission to view the specified link and read the target.

learning.reason: Grant the link permission needed to view the appropriate shared resource in the catalog. Separately grant permission to read data from the source table.
learning.concept: DESCRIBE on a resource link and SELECT on the target table

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Stop new launches of an old version while preserving existing deployments
prompt: An old version of a Service Catalog product contains a network configuration that has been retired. A tested newer version is available. The deployed products that use the old version must not be deleted immediately, but the path that allows new launches using the old version must be stopped. What should be done?

choices.text: Terminate all provisioned products that use the old version and wait for each team to launch a new one.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the requirement to preserve running environments.

choices.text: Remove the product itself from the portfolio so that both the new and old versions are hidden from all users.
choices.explanation: This does not allow the approved new version to continue being offered.

choices.text: Make the old version inactive and leave the new approved version active.
choices.explanation: This prevents new launches using the old version without terminating products that have already been launched.

choices.text: Leave the old version active and merely write that it must not be used in the version description.
choices.explanation: A note does not enforce rejection of new launches.

learning.reason: Prevent new launches using the old version without terminating products that have already been launched.
learning.concept: Deactivating a product version in Service Catalog

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Automatically Expose Resources Shared with an OU to New Members
prompt: Network resources used by multiple accounts support sharing through AWS RAM. You want accounts newly added to a specific OU to use the resources without individually accepting resource-sharing invitations. What should you configure? (Choose two.)

choices.text: From the Organizations management account, enable sharing within the organization in AWS RAM.
choices.explanation: This satisfies the prerequisite for resource sharing based on Organizations membership.

choices.text: Prefix the resource name with the Organizations OU name and do not configure sharing in AWS RAM.
choices.explanation: Naming alone does not grant the cross-account permissions required to use supported resources.

choices.text: Keep sharing within the organization disabled and send sharing invitations to each account ID.
choices.explanation: This does not automatically follow account membership changes and leaves the individual-invitation process in place.

choices.text: Share only with the management account and tag that account with the name of the OU it contains.
choices.explanation: Members that are not specified as sharing principals are not authorized to use the shared resources.

choices.text: Create a resource share with the target OU as the principal.
choices.explanation: The share follows members of the OU, and accounts in the integrated organization do not need to accept individual invitations.

learning.reason: This satisfies the prerequisite for resource sharing based on Organizations membership. The share follows members of the OU, and accounts in the integrated organization do not need to accept individual invitations.
learning.concept: OU-based sharing through AWS RAM integration with Organizations

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Aggregate Unresolved Findings by Resource
prompt: You are reviewing high-severity unresolved findings in Security Hub CSPM. You need to produce the count for each resource under the same conditions every time and review resources with the highest counts first. Which reusable mechanism leaves the finding status unchanged?

choices.text: Update the workflow status of all findings to NOTIFIED and search by resource name afterward.
choices.explanation: This does not produce the same aggregate and also changes the finding status.

choices.text: Enable only one standard and estimate the number of unresolved resources from that standard's control list.
choices.explanation: The standard's list does not show finding counts by resource, and this also changes the existing evaluation scope.

choices.text: Use an automation rule to add a priority to findings that match the severity condition, then use the severity-based counts on the dashboard.
choices.explanation: Adjusting priority by updating findings does not create a reusable aggregation by resource ID.

choices.text: Create a custom insight filtered by severity and workflow status, and group it by resource ID.
choices.explanation: This reuses the target conditions and lets you review findings related to the same resource as one aggregate.

learning.reason: This reuses the target conditions and lets you review findings related to the same resource as one aggregate.
learning.concept: Custom insight filters and grouping

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Verify Runtime Monitoring Coverage Even When There Are No Findings
prompt: In an EKS environment that uses GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring, a cluster has no new runtime findings. You do not want to assume that the environment is healthy solely because there are no findings; you need to determine whether the security agent can monitor the cluster. What should you check?

choices.text: If the image has no findings in the ECR scan results, assume that runtime data can also be collected after startup.
choices.explanation: Image scanning does not verify runtime coverage.

choices.text: In GuardDuty runtime coverage, check the target cluster's status and the reason it is uncovered, if applicable.
choices.explanation: This checks whether monitoring data can be received from the target instead of relying on the presence or absence of findings.

choices.text: Assume that GuardDuty runtime signals are arriving solely because EKS Kubernetes audit logs are being recorded.
choices.explanation: API-operation auditing and coverage by the agent used for Runtime Monitoring are separate.

choices.text: Determine that the agent is healthy if the number of findings in the GuardDuty findings list is zero.
choices.explanation: There may be no findings when monitoring data is not reaching GuardDuty.

learning.reason: This checks whether monitoring data can be received from the target instead of relying on the presence or absence of findings.
learning.concept: Resource-level coverage status for Runtime Monitoring

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Scan Lambda Dependencies and Proprietary Code Separately
prompt: You are using Inspector's standard Lambda scanning to check the dependencies of ZIP functions that use supported runtimes. You want to keep standard scanning enabled and also scan unsafe operations in function code written by your organization, within the supported language scope. What should you add?

choices.text: Enable Lambda execution logs and conclude that a function has no source-code issues if it has no runtime errors.
choices.explanation: Runtime logs alone cannot establish that the code contains no issues.

choices.text: Enable Lambda code scanning in the target account and Region.
choices.explanation: This scans the organization's application code separately from the dependency scanning performed by standard scanning.

choices.text: Enable only enhanced scanning in ECR and assume that ZIP-format function code is also evaluated in the registry.
choices.explanation: ECR scanning does not include proprietary source code from Lambda ZIP functions that are not stored in the registry.

choices.text: Move the proprietary code to a Lambda layer and assume that standard scanning performs source analysis for all implementations.
choices.explanation: Standard scanning examines dependencies; it does not replace code scanning.

learning.reason: This scans the organization's application code separately from the dependency scanning performed by standard scanning.
learning.concept: Inspector standard Lambda scanning and code scanning

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Efficiently searching for the same identifier across many audit log groups
prompt: In CloudWatch Logs Insights, you need to find exact traceId values across many Standard-class log groups. The investigation covers the most recent 7 days, and the same field indexing policy already exists in all groups. Events were ingested after the policy was created. How should you search to reduce the amount of scanning without missing matches in scope?

choices.text: Match every substring of traceId with a regular expression and treat it as equivalent to an exact match using the index.
choices.explanation: A substring search is not the same equality search on the specified field.

choices.text: Parse the entire raw message with a regular expression and then compare the value instead of using the indexed traceId.
choices.explanation: Matching a value extracted by parsing does not search the field index created at ingestion.

choices.text: Search all groups, then use sort and limit to reduce only the number of returned results.
choices.explanation: Reducing the number of returned results does not select which groups to scan by using the target field's index.

choices.text: Search the log groups by specifying the target traceId in an equality condition for filterIndex.
choices.explanation: Using the target field's index can exclude groups without the matching value from the scan.

learning.reason: The target field's index can exclude log groups without the matching value from the scan.
learning.concept: Logs Insights field indexes and equality searches

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Do not treat gaps in flow logs as evidence that no communication occurred
prompt: For an ENI under audit, the expected records are missing during the target period. Some aggregation intervals contain log-status=SKIPDATA. What is the appropriate way to handle this when determining whether the application had no communication at all?

choices.text: Assume that interpolating the byte counts of other recorded flows can accurately reconstruct the content and source of the missing communication.
choices.explanation: The individual details of omitted flows cannot be reconstructed from other records.

choices.text: Treat SKIPDATA as having the same meaning as NODATA and conclude that there were no packets at that time.
choices.explanation: An omitted collection state is different from an observed state in which there was no network communication.

choices.text: Assume that flows may exist that were not recorded during that interval, and correlate the data with other observation records.
choices.explanation: SKIPDATA indicates that some records were omitted, so you cannot conclude that there was no communication.

choices.text: Assume that SKIPDATA represents all communication rejected by security groups.
choices.explanation: log-status describes collection status and is separate from the action indicating whether packets were allowed or rejected.

learning.reason: SKIPDATA indicates that some records were omitted, so it does not prove that no communication occurred.
learning.concept: The meanings of SKIPDATA and NODATA in Flow Logs

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Analyze multiple AWS audit sources with a common schema
prompt: An audit team wants to analyze the corresponding CloudTrail management events and VPC Flow Logs from S3. The team wants to minimize maintenance of source-specific transformations and subscribe another analytics platform to the same open schema. What should it use?

choices.text: Enable the target AWS sources in Amazon Security Lake and configure a subscription to the normalized data.
choices.explanation: It can collect the supported AWS data in OCSF format and provide access to the defined subscriber.

choices.text: Use only Security Hub CSPM and reconstruct all original APIs and network flows from configuration findings.
choices.explanation: Aggregating findings does not store the original audit events in a common format.

choices.text: Collect the existing S3 logs under different prefixes in the same bucket and assume that the schemas of the log contents will then be the same.
choices.explanation: Using a common storage location does not transform the source-specific log structures.

choices.text: Change only the custom format of VPC Flow Logs and assume that the same setting is automatically applied to CloudTrail events.
choices.explanation: The output formats of VPC Flow Logs and CloudTrail are separate.

learning.reason: Supported AWS data can be collected in OCSF format and made available to defined subscribers.
learning.concept: AWS sources in Security Lake and normalization to OCSF

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Some allowed traffic does not appear in the firewall FLOW log
prompt: In a VPC under management, test traffic passing through AWS Network Firewall is allowed. One stream is fully processed by an allow action at the stateless stage and does not appear in the FLOW log. What should you verify to include the traffic in the FLOW-log audit scope while preserving the allowed behavior?

choices.text: Continue allowing it only at the stateless stage and change FLOW to ALERT.
choices.explanation: ALERT is also associated with stateful processing and does not record traffic that completes at the stateless stage.

choices.text: Continue allowing it only at the stateless stage and change the destination from CloudWatch Logs to S3.
choices.explanation: Changing the log destination does not change the fact that the traffic does not enter stateful processing.

choices.text: Pass the traffic being audited to the stateful engine and apply the allow condition through the corresponding stateful rule.
choices.explanation: FLOW logs are generated from traffic that passes through stateful processing.

choices.text: Fill in the unrecorded interval later by extending the log retention period.
choices.explanation: Retention settings do not create logs that were not generated at the time.

learning.reason: FLOW logs are generated from traffic that passes through stateful processing.
learning.concept: Network Firewall log generation and the stateful engine

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Applying sensitive-field protection to sampled request displays
prompt: A specific field has been masked in AWS WAF logs, but the same information protection is also required when operators view sampled requests. Sampling must remain enabled for investigation. What should be added?

choices.text: Display the original field to users who read the samples and protect it only by hiding the column in the investigation screen.
choices.explanation: Removing collected information only from one display does not protect it when other display methods are available.

choices.text: Keep only the existing log field-editing configuration and assume that the same setting is automatically applied to samples.
choices.explanation: Editing log fields alone does not mask information in sampled requests.

choices.text: Shorten the log retention period and assume that the information will not be displayed in samples within that period.
choices.explanation: The retention period is not a protection rule for fields in sampled requests.

choices.text: Configure AWS WAF data protection on the target field so that it also applies to sampling.
choices.explanation: Separate from log field editing, the applicable protection can also be applied to sampled requests.

learning.reason: Separate from log field editing, the applicable protection can also be applied to sampled requests.
learning.concept: Scope of AWS WAF log field editing and data protection

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Finding prohibited reachability paths without enumerating individual connection tests
prompt: A network team wants to examine configuration paths that could allow traffic from an internet gateway to target ENIs across multiple VPCs in the same account and Region. They want to define the prohibited reachability scope and identify candidates without testing each specific source-destination pair individually. What should they use?

choices.text: Output only DNS server name-resolution results and determine that a destination with no returned name is necessarily unreachable over the network.
choices.explanation: Whether a name resolves is independent of reachability through configured network paths.

choices.text: Search VPC Flow Logs for only paths that were actually used and determine that paths with no access history are impossible in the configuration.
choices.explanation: A path can be reachable even if it has not been used.

choices.text: Use Reachability Analyzer to test only one permitted pair and assume that no prohibited paths exist if that connection is possible.
choices.explanation: Reachability for one pair does not prove that there are no abnormal paths throughout the defined scope.

choices.text: Define the evaluation criteria in a Network Access Analyzer scope and examine findings for paths that could be reachable.
choices.explanation: It can identify unintended reachability in aggregate by using conditions such as the applicable sources and destinations.

learning.reason: It can identify unintended reachability in aggregate by using conditions such as the applicable sources and destinations.
learning.concept: Network Access Analyzer access scopes

category: 検出
examDomain: 検出
title: Integrating internal inspection findings into existing security operations
prompt: A company's configuration inspection periodically generates findings. How can it directly import those findings into the Security Hub CSPM used by the organization, from the same AWS account as the inspected resources, so that they appear in the same list and workflow as findings from AWS services?

choices.text: Convert the findings to ASFF and call BatchImportFindings with the default product ARN for the same account.
choices.explanation: A custom source can be integrated with Security Hub CSPM by using ASFF and the default product ARN for the same account.

choices.text: Insert the company's findings into the CloudTrail event history so that the same data is automatically registered as AWS operation records.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail operation history is not an ingestion path for arbitrary inspection findings.

choices.text: Send custom JSON to EventBridge and use an existing rule that distributes Security Hub CSPM findings to import the findings in the reverse direction.
choices.explanation: Existing rules distribute published findings; they do not import findings from a custom product.

choices.text: Write the company's JSON to S3 and assume that Security Hub CSPM will detect findings in every bucket automatically.
choices.explanation: Placing inspection results in S3 is separate from importing findings into Security Hub.

learning.reason: A custom source can be integrated with Security Hub CSPM by using ASFF and the default product ARN for the same account.
learning.concept: ASFF and finding import for custom sources

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Investigation window for messages moved to a DLQ
prompt: Messages that fail while processing audit notifications are moved from an SQS standard queue to a standard DLQ. They may remain in the original queue for up to 72 hours before being moved, and investigators must be able to retrieve them for an additional 96 hours after the move. No separate storage in S3 will be used. Which setting meets the requirement?

choices.text: Set the retention period of both the original queue and the DLQ to 96 hours, and send a CloudWatch alarm notification when a message is moved.
choices.explanation: Recording the notification time does not extend the expiration. The time already elapsed in the original queue must be added.

choices.text: Set the DLQ retention period to 96 hours.
choices.explanation: The 96 hours is not measured from entry into a standard DLQ. If 72 hours have elapsed before the move, only 24 hours remain.

choices.text: Set the DLQ retention period to 96 hours and extend the visibility timeout to its maximum.
choices.explanation: The visibility timeout controls how long a message is hidden from other consumers after receipt. It does not extend the retention-period expiration.

choices.text: Set the DLQ retention period to 168 hours.
choices.explanation: Moving a message to a standard DLQ does not change its enqueue timestamp. A total of 168 hours from the initial enqueue ensures that even a message moved at the latest possible time remains available for 96 hours.

learning.reason: Moving a message to a standard DLQ does not change its enqueue timestamp. A total of 168 hours from the initial enqueue ensures that even a message moved at the latest possible time remains available for 96 hours.
learning.concept: Retention for a standard queue's DLQ is measured from the initial enqueue time

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Stop New Launches of a Public AMI
prompt: A validation AMI in the company's account is public in a Region. The incident response team must stop new launches of this AMI by the public, preserve the AMI as evidence, and prevent accidental public exposure in the future. Explicit sharing with approved accounts must continue. Which combination of changes should be made? Select two.

choices.text: Leave the AMI unchanged and enable Block public access on the associated EBS snapshots.
choices.explanation: Snapshot sharing settings and AMI launch permissions are separate controls.

choices.text: Leave the existing AMI public and use the company's Organizations to restrict launches by member accounts.
choices.explanation: The organization's SCPs do not apply to users outside the organization, and this does not remove the AMI's public launch permission.

choices.text: Enable Block public access for AMIs in the target Region and restrict configuration changes to approved administrators.
choices.explanation: The Regional setting prevents new public exposure. Private launch permissions that specify accounts can remain in place.

choices.text: Deregister the target AMI and continue sharing only the associated EBS snapshots.
choices.explanation: Deregistering the AMI does not preserve the AMI itself or allow approved accounts to continue launching it.

choices.text: Remove the public group from the target AMI's launch permissions while retaining the entries for approved accounts.
choices.explanation: Removing the public launch permission stops new launches by the public without deregistering the existing AMI.

learning.reason: Removing the public launch permission stops new launches by the public without deregistering the existing AMI. The Regional setting prevents new public exposure. Private launch permissions that specify accounts can remain in place.
learning.concept: Removing public access from an existing AMI and blocking future public exposure are separate operations.

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Remove an Accidentally Public Document from the Delivery Cache
prompt: A document that should have remained private is being delivered through CloudFront, and its TTL still has several days remaining. The origin can stop serving the document's response. Other publicly available documents must continue to be served from the same distribution. Which approach will quickly remove the target document from the managed delivery path?

choices.text: Invalidate the target path in CloudFront, leave the document at the origin, and review the access logs.
choices.explanation: A request after the invalidation could retrieve the document again from the origin and cause it to be delivered again.

choices.text: Stop serving the document at the origin and monitor CloudFront until the next TTL expiration.
choices.explanation: Changing the origin does not prevent a valid cache already at the edge from being returned until it expires.

choices.text: Stop serving the document at the origin and invalidate the target path in CloudFront.
choices.explanation: Stopping retrieval from the origin and then invalidating the target path removes the existing edge cache without waiting for TTL expiration. Other paths remain available.

choices.text: Prepare a new filename for the document, change the navigation, and leave the existing cache at the original path.
choices.explanation: Versioned filenames help with ordinary updates, but they do not stop a response already exposed at the original URL.

learning.reason: Stopping retrieval from the origin and then invalidating the target path removes the existing edge cache without waiting for TTL expiration. Other paths remain available.
learning.concept: Stop new retrievals at the origin before removing the cache for the target path.

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Withhold S3 Reads Until Scan Results Are Available
prompt: A business partner uploads documents to a dedicated S3 prefix. GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3 is configured to add result tags. The existing IAM policy for the business application allows reads, but new objects should be readable only when GuardDuty has inspected them and no threat was detected. Select two.

choices.text: Send the application a notification when an inspection fails, and later deny each corresponding object individually.
choices.explanation: This cannot prevent reads that occur before the asynchronous notification and policy change are complete.

choices.text: For reads by the application, use a bucket policy to deny access when the result tag is anything other than NO_THREATS_FOUND or is absent.
choices.explanation: The explicit deny takes precedence over the existing Allow, so uninspected, failed, and threat-detected objects cannot be read. Access for the inspection role remains available.

choices.text: Deny reads only when the result is THREATS_FOUND, and retain the application's existing access until a tag is added.
choices.explanation: Uninspected objects and objects whose processing failed could still be read, so this does not require inspection to be complete.

choices.text: Control the setting, modification, and deletion of result tags, including during uploads, so that the business application and submitter cannot change the result.
choices.explanation: This protects the integrity of the value used for the read decision. The GuardDuty role retains the legitimate tag permissions.

choices.text: Allow access when the application sends NO_THREATS_FOUND as a request tag during the read.
choices.explanation: The condition must use the inspection result stored on the object, not a declaration made by the reader.

learning.reason: The explicit deny takes precedence over the existing Allow, so uninspected, failed, and threat-detected objects cannot be read. Access for the inspection role remains available. Protecting the integrity of the value used for the read decision is also required. The GuardDuty role retains the legitimate tag permissions.
learning.concept: Release reads only when the object explicitly has a no-threat result, rather than allowing reads for every result except a positive detection.

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Preserve Multiple Disks of a Running EC2 Instance as Evidence
prompt: The Linux EC2 instance under investigation writes data and journal information to separate EBS volumes. The volumes must be captured without stopping the instance, and the disk state from the same point in time must later be examined in an isolated environment. Application consistency is not required; crash consistency is sufficient. Which method should be used?

choices.text: Capture only the data volume and use the latest journal, updated while the instance was running, when restoring it in the isolated environment.
choices.explanation: Combining data and journal information from different capture points cannot reproduce the disk state at the time of interest.

choices.text: Select the existing individual snapshot from each volume whose completion time is closest to the others.
choices.explanation: Even if completion times are close, the snapshots are not necessarily records of a common point in the source volumes' states.

choices.text: Issue CreateSnapshot in parallel for each volume and record the same investigation ID and request time in tags.
choices.explanation: Issuing requests at nearly the same time does not guarantee a common capture point across independent snapshots.

choices.text: Capture snapshots of multiple volumes for the EC2 instance and store their IDs as one evidence set.
choices.explanation: CreateSnapshots creates crash-consistent snapshots for multiple EBS volumes attached to an instance as a group.

learning.reason: CreateSnapshots creates crash-consistent snapshots for multiple EBS volumes attached to an instance as a group.
learning.concept: Capture multiple EBS volumes from the same instance as one consistent set.

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Identifying the Boundary Where Containment Notifications Fail
prompt: An EventBridge rule asynchronously invokes a Lambda function that performs containment actions. During the investigation, the team needs to distinguish delivery rejection by the target from processing failure after Lambda has accepted the event, and recover the original events. Which design is appropriate?

choices.text: Configure a DLQ for the EventBridge target, and make the Lambda function raise an exception so that all failures are returned to that DLQ.
choices.explanation: Handler exceptions that occur after the invocation has been accepted are handled on the Lambda side and are not returned to the rule's DLQ.

choices.text: Configure Lambda's destination for asynchronous failures, and disable retries and the DLQ on EventBridge.
choices.explanation: When delivery is rejected, Lambda does not retain the event, so it cannot be recovered from a Lambda destination.

choices.text: Configure a DLQ for the rule's target and configure a separate failure destination for Lambda's asynchronous invocation.
choices.explanation: EventBridge retains events that it could not deliver, while Lambda separately sends records of executions that have exhausted their post-acceptance retries.

choices.text: Collect matching events in an EventBridge archive and use their presence in the archive as the condition for determining target failure.
choices.explanation: An archive does not classify events according to the rule's delivery result or the execution result after acceptance.

learning.reason: EventBridge retains events that it could not deliver, while Lambda separately sends records of executions that have exhausted their post-acceptance retries.
learning.concept: Capture event-delivery failures and asynchronous Lambda-processing failures at separate boundaries

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Escalating an Internal Investigation Case to AWS Support
prompt: In AWS Security Incident Response, a team creates a case for internal handling only and records the response history and approved investigation materials. The severity increases, and after obtaining internal approval, the team requests assistance from a dedicated AWS engineer. How can the investigation continue in the same case?

choices.text: Resolve the existing case and open a separate AWS-supported case with the same description.
choices.explanation: The team can request AWS assistance, but the case history would be split. The existing case does not need to be closed to preserve the history.

choices.text: Set the case severity to the highest level, keep it Self-managed, and wait for a response from an engineer.
choices.explanation: Updating the severity alone cannot change an internally managed case to an AWS-supported case.

choices.text: Escalate through “Get help from AWS” in the existing case.
choices.explanation: A case that started as Self-managed can be switched to AWS support when necessary, allowing the investigation to continue in the existing case.

choices.text: Change related findings to NOTIFIED in Security Hub CSPM and wait for the same case to be transferred to AWS automatically.
choices.explanation: The workflow status of a finding is not linked to a request for assistance from AWS Security Incident Response.

learning.reason: A case that started as Self-managed can be switched to AWS support when necessary, allowing the investigation to continue in the existing case.
learning.concept: A Self-managed case can be escalated to AWS support from the existing case

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Verifying a Preventive Measure Before Closing the Incident
prompt: A configuration-distribution issue caused some monitored resources not to send notifications, and monitoring was restored manually. During the post-incident review, the team proposed an automated measure to detect cases in which the configuration is correct but notifications do not reach their destination. Which method verifies that the preventive measure actually works before determining that the action is complete?

choices.text: Have the feature owner update the monitoring runbook and mark the action complete when everyone on call has read the explanation.
choices.explanation: Training helps responders, but it does not verify that the new mechanism automatically detects an abnormal notification path.

choices.text: Assign an owner and a due date, reproduce the notification-path failure in a controlled exercise, and retain evidence that the new detection was delivered.
choices.explanation: This approach tracks the action from the root cause and makes successful operation from detection through notification delivery under the same failure condition a completion criterion.

choices.text: Ask the operations team to perform manual checks temporarily and mark the action complete if no similar reports occur for a specified period.
choices.explanation: A period without a naturally recurring incident does not prove that the mitigation is effective.

choices.text: Make successful execution of the configuration-distribution pipeline the completion criterion and record that the same definition was applied to every account.
choices.explanation: Successful distribution shows the monitoring configuration state, but does not verify that the notification path at issue actually works.

learning.reason: This approach tracks the action from the root cause and makes successful operation from detection through notification delivery under the same failure condition a completion criterion.
learning.concept: Assign an owner and due date for a preventive measure, then reproduce the failure to verify its effectiveness

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Terminating Remaining Sessions of a Compromised Database User
prompt: A password used by an old application user in RDS for PostgreSQL has been exposed. The application has been switched to a new user and new logins by the old user have been blocked, but a database administrator discovers sessions belonging to the old user that were established before the switch. Which method disconnects the remaining sessions without stopping other applications?

choices.text: Use pg_stat_activity to filter connections for the old user and terminate only the matching sessions.
choices.explanation: By identifying the user in the connection list and limiting pg_terminate_backend to the matching sessions, connections for other users can remain active.

choices.text: Restart the DB instance to disconnect all connections and have the connection pools reconnect.
choices.explanation: This disconnects the old sessions, but it also disconnects healthy application connections. Session-level handling is possible.

choices.text: Change the old user's password again and wait for existing sessions to require reauthentication.
choices.explanation: Changing the password affects authentication for new connections; it does not forcibly disconnect connections that have already authenticated.

choices.text: Cancel only the SQL currently running for the old user and confirm that the remaining connection is not used as is.
choices.explanation: Canceling a query does not terminate the session, so another operation can be performed over the same connection.

learning.reason: By identifying the user in the connection list and limiting pg_terminate_backend to the matching sessions, connections for other users can remain active.
learning.concept: Terminate only the targeted sessions that remain after an authentication change

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: CloudFront-Only Private Origin
prompt: A public web service is protected by AWS WAF on CloudFront. The backend for a new API is an internal ALB in a private subnet in the corresponding Region and meets the prerequisites for a VPC origin. The ALB must not be directly reachable from the internet. Which design allows CloudFront to reach this ALB?

choices.text: Use an internet-facing ALB and allow only CloudFront’s origin-facing prefix list.
choices.explanation: The source can be restricted, but this does not meet the requirement to keep the backend as a private internal ALB.

choices.text: Place a NAT gateway in front of the internal ALB and use its Elastic IP as a standard CloudFront origin.
choices.explanation: A NAT gateway is used for connections initiated from inside. It is not an entry point for an origin connection from outside to an internal ALB.

choices.text: Specify the internal ALB’s DNS name as a standard custom origin and add an alias for the ALB in public Route 53.
choices.explanation: Registering a name in DNS does not make the internal ALB routable from the public side.

choices.text: Register the internal ALB as a CloudFront VPC origin and allow inbound traffic from the VPC origin at the ALB.
choices.explanation: A VPC origin provides a path from CloudFront to a private ALB. The ALB does not need to be internet-facing.

learning.reason: A VPC origin provides a path from CloudFront to a private ALB. The ALB does not need to be internet-facing.
learning.concept: Reach an internal load balancer through a CloudFront VPC origin

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Separating Tasks on the Same ECS Host by Communication Requirements
prompt: With the ECS EC2 launch type, tasks for an order-management service and a notification service are placed on the same EC2 instance. Only the order-management tasks should be allowed to make TCP connections to RDS. How can this restriction be maintained even if task placement changes during scaling, without placing the services on separate hosts in the same VPC?

choices.text: Keep bridge mode and allow the ECS host’s security group as a source in the RDS security group.
choices.explanation: Using the host’s security group cannot separate the two services for network control when they use the same host.

choices.text: Allow RDS IAM database authentication only for the order-management tasks’ IAM role, and allow traffic from the host in the RDS security group.
choices.explanation: IAM authentication controls login. The notification service would still have TCP reachability, so the network requirement would not be met.

choices.text: Configure outbound rules in the host subnet’s network ACL for the container ports used by the order-management tasks.
choices.explanation: A network ACL applies to a subnet and cannot use the identity of a task or a container name on the same host as a condition.

choices.text: Use awsvpc and allow inbound traffic in the RDS security group only from the security group assigned to the order-management tasks.
choices.explanation: With awsvpc, ENIs and security groups can be applied to tasks, allowing RDS to distinguish the sources even when the services run on the same host.

learning.reason: With awsvpc, ENIs and security groups can be applied to tasks, allowing RDS to distinguish the sources even when the services run on the same host.
learning.concept: Restrict database reachability with task-level ENIs and security groups in awsvpc

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Enabling DNSSEC for a Delegated Subdomain
prompt: The authoritative zones for a parent domain and a child subdomain are managed by different teams. DNSSEC is functioning correctly for the parent zone, and signing is already configured for the child’s Route 53 public hosted zone. What should be done so that external validating resolvers can validate responses for the child from the parent?

choices.text: Shorten the TTL of the parent zone’s NS record so that the child zone’s signed responses propagate faster.
choices.explanation: Adjusting the TTL does not register the trust relationship required to validate signed responses.

choices.text: Create a DS record at the apex of the child zone and leave the delegation from the parent zone’s NS record unchanged.
choices.explanation: The DS record that establishes the chain of trust from the parent to the child must be provided in the parent. Publishing it in the child does not make the delegation verifiable.

choices.text: Distribute the child zone’s DNSKEY in a TXT record in the parent and have DNSSEC-enabled resolvers reference it.
choices.explanation: DNSSEC validation does not treat an arbitrary TXT record as delegation information; it uses the DS record in the parent zone.

choices.text: Have the DS value provided by Route 53 for the child zone registered at the delegation name in the parent zone.
choices.explanation: A signed DS record in the parent lets resolvers verify the key used to sign the child zone.

learning.reason: A signed DS record in the parent lets resolvers verify the key used to sign the child zone.
learning.concept: Link DNSSEC delegation through the parent’s DS record and the child’s DNSKEY

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Redundancy That Accounts for On-Premises VPN Device Failure
prompt: A Site-to-Site VPN connects an on-premises network to a VPC, and both tunnels and BGP terminate on a single edge device. This provides redundancy for an AWS-side tunnel failure, but encrypted communication must continue even if that edge device fails. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Add a separate VPN connection from a second customer gateway to the same VPC side.
choices.explanation: A separate device and VPN connection separate the failure points. Configure both devices so that BGP leaves usable routes available.

choices.text: Configure different preshared keys for the two tunnels of the existing VPN connection, terminating both on the same edge device.
choices.explanation: Using different keys does not prevent both tunnels from being lost when the physical device fails.

choices.text: Create a second VPN connection on the same edge device and terminate each connection on a different interface.
choices.explanation: Separating the connections or interfaces still leaves the single-device failure point because the device is shared.

choices.text: Adjust BGP attributes for the two tunnels on the existing edge device and make one a backup route.
choices.explanation: Changing route preference handles a tunnel failure but cannot absorb the failure of the single device.

learning.reason: A separate device and VPN connection separate the failure points. Configure both devices so that BGP leaves usable routes available.
learning.concept: On-premises device redundancy is required in addition to AWS-side VPN tunnel redundancy

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Using WAF classification results as conditions for subsequent rules
prompt: An AWS WAF custom rule group adds classification labels to requests from a partner system but does not terminate evaluation. In the same Web ACL, you want to apply an action only to requests that have this label and use a specified URL path. Which design avoids duplicating the classification logic?

choices.text: After the classification group, match the original request's header against the label name.
choices.explanation: A WAF label is metadata within the same evaluation; it is not automatically added as a request header.

choices.text: Place an AND condition for the label name and URL path at the beginning of the Web ACL, and place the classification group after it.
choices.explanation: The classification group has not yet run when the label is evaluated, so the label being matched does not yet exist.

choices.text: Evaluate the classification group first, then use an AND condition for the fully qualified label name and URL path in a subsequent rule.
choices.explanation: Labels are visible to subsequent rules in the same Web ACL. A label from another group must be specified with a name that includes its issuing source.

choices.text: Write the rule group's label to logs and apply the previous log value to the next request using the same URL.
choices.explanation: Classification must be applied to the current request. A previous log value cannot determine the current evaluation.

learning.reason: Labels are visible to subsequent rules in the same Web ACL. A label from another group must be specified by its fully qualified name, including the issuing source.
learning.concept: Referencing a label added in an earlier context by its fully qualified name in a subsequent rule

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Maintaining contractor access through Client VPN in two Availability Zones
prompt: A Client VPN that authenticates users with SAML has subnets in two Availability Zones associated with it. You must preserve access for existing employees while allowing a contractor group to access only the peer VPC's 10.50.20.0/24. Routes and security groups on the destination side are already configured, and the contractors have no other applicable permissions. Which changes are required in Client VPN? Select two.

choices.text: Add only an authorization rule for the contractors and rely on automatic route discovery by the client devices for the peer VPC.
choices.explanation: A route to a destination outside the associated VPC must be configured separately; an authorization rule alone does not provide forwarding.

choices.text: Add a Client VPN route to 10.50.20.0/24 to both associated subnets.
choices.explanation: If the route is added to only one subnet, the destination may be unreachable depending on which subnet the connection uses.

choices.text: Use DNS to switch the route to each network and grant the contractors the same destination authorization as the employees.
choices.explanation: DNS resolution does not restrict access permissions. Using the same authorization as the employees would broaden the allowed destinations.

choices.text: Add an authorization rule explicitly allowing 10.50.20.0/24 for the contractors' SAML group.
choices.explanation: SAML authentication and authorization to a destination network are separate. The permission must be limited to the group and destination.

choices.text: Add an authorization rule for all users allowing 10.50.0.0/16 from Client VPN and rely on the contractors' client subnet settings to limit access.
choices.explanation: Client-side settings cannot enforce the contractor group's access scope on the server.

learning.reason: The same destination route must be added to each associated subnet, and SAML authentication is separate from authorization to the destination network. Permission should be limited to the target group and destination.
learning.concept: Configuring the same destination route for every associated subnet and granting targeted authorization to the intended group

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Protecting services individually within the same VPC Lattice network
prompt: Multiple departmental VPCs are connected to a shared VPC Lattice service network. An internal shared service should allow all approved service roles, but the payment service must be limited to payment-specific caller roles. Both services must continue using the same network. Which approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Use AWS_IAM for both: allow the approved roles at the network level and limit the payment service to the payment-specific roles.
choices.explanation: Combining network-level and service-level policies preserves shared connectivity while applying granular authorization to the payment service.

choices.text: Allow only the payment-specific roles across the network and add the other department roles to the shared service's service-level policy.
choices.explanation: A service-level policy cannot override a network-level restriction. The other departments would lose access to the shared service.

choices.text: Leave the payment service's authentication type as NONE and notify only the payment team of the service's DNS name.
choices.explanation: Knowing a name does not verify that the request was made by an approved role.

choices.text: Allow the source VPC CIDRs in the security groups for the service network's VPC associations and open the payment service to every role that can connect to the network.
choices.explanation: Security groups control the source network. They cannot restrict payment-service calls to specific IAM roles.

learning.reason: Combining network-level and service-level policies preserves shared connectivity while applying granular authorization to the payment service.
learning.concept: Combining broad service-network permissions with service-level authorization

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Separating an existing S3 access point by network boundary
prompt: An S3 bucket shared by multiple departments has department-specific access points. The research department's existing access point has an Internet network origin. You want to block direct external calls using an access-point attribute that will not depend on future policy changes. The access points for the other departments must remain unchanged. What should you do?

choices.text: Enable Block Public Access on the existing access point and retain only the research department roles' current permissions.
choices.explanation: This can suppress public policies, but it does not set an attribute that restricts authenticated traffic to a specific VPC.

choices.text: Add a condition for the research VPC to the existing access point policy while leaving its network origin as Internet.
choices.explanation: The condition can be used for restriction, but this still depends on an access-point policy and does not provide the required policy-independent boundary.

choices.text: Change the existing access point's network origin to VPC while retaining the access point ARN.
choices.explanation: An access point's network origin cannot be changed after the access point is created.

choices.text: Create an access point dedicated to the research VPC, migrate usage to it, and remove permissions from the old access point.
choices.explanation: A VPC network origin can be fixed only when the access point is created. S3 verifies the source of requests sent through the new access point.

learning.reason: A VPC network origin can be fixed only when the access point is created. S3 verifies the source of requests sent through the new access point.
learning.concept: A VPC origin can be specified only when an access point is created

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Validate security settings by booting an AMI before distribution
prompt: Linux AMIs are distributed monthly to each department. The configuration commands during image creation succeeded, but a security agent once failed to start automatically when a distributed AMI was booted. You want to distribute only images that pass validation in an environment booted from the AMI after the build. Which measure is appropriate?

choices.text: During the Validate phase, check the services currently running and skip the Test phase for the built AMI.
choices.explanation: The current service can be running even if the saved automatic-start configuration is incorrect. This does not satisfy the requirement to validate booting from the AMI.

choices.text: During the Image Builder Test phase, boot from the created AMI and verify the agent.
choices.explanation: The Test phase launches a new environment from the image after it is built, so you can decide whether to distribute it after verifying behavior that includes a restart.

choices.text: During the Build phase, check the installation command's exit code and distribute the image to all accounts when it succeeds.
choices.explanation: Successful installation does not prove that the service will run when the built image is booted.

choices.text: After distribution, verify the approved image ID in Config and consider every instance launched from an approved ID to have passed.
choices.explanation: Checking the AMI ID does not test the configuration or agent behavior, and it cannot prevent a failed AMI from being distributed.

learning.reason: The Test phase launches a new environment from the image after it is built, so you can decide whether to distribute it after verifying behavior that includes a restart.
learning.concept: Boot and verify the built image during the Image Builder Test phase

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: HTTPS times out at a private endpoint
prompt: An EC2 instance in an isolated VPC uses a Secrets Manager interface endpoint. DNS resolves to the endpoint's private IP, and HTTPS egress is allowed for the client. The ACL and VPC routing have been verified, but the security group attached to the endpoint has no inbound rules. Which change restores communication with the smallest scope?

choices.text: Add inbound TCP 443 from the client's security group to the endpoint's security group.
choices.explanation: The endpoint ENI is the receiving side of the connection. The source can be restricted to the client security group in the same VPC.

choices.text: Add outbound TCP 443 to the client security group in the endpoint's security group, without opening inbound traffic.
choices.explanation: Allowing egress is opposite to the direction in which the connection is initiated, so a new connection from the client remains blocked on the receiving side.

choices.text: Add inbound TCP 443 from the endpoint's security group to the client's security group.
choices.explanation: The client initiates the TCP connection, and security groups automatically allow return traffic for an allowed connection.

choices.text: Add GetSecretValue for the EC2 role to the endpoint policy and leave the endpoint security group unchanged.
choices.explanation: The endpoint policy authorizes API calls. It does not override the security group rejecting the inbound TCP connection.

learning.reason: The endpoint ENI is the receiving side of the connection. The source can be restricted to the client security group in the same VPC.
learning.concept: Allow inbound HTTPS from the client at the interface endpoint ENI

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Restrict a REST API to an approved custom-domain entry point
prompt: Users of a public REST API have completed migration to an approved custom domain. Operational policy requires rejecting calls through the default endpoint at every stage while preserving the existing authentication method and domain mappings. Which two administrative actions are required? Select two.

choices.text: Reissue the ACM certificate for the custom domain and associate it with the same domain again.
choices.explanation: Updating the certificate does not control whether the default endpoint is enabled.

choices.text: Change the base path of the API mapping while leaving existing client paths unchanged.
choices.explanation: An API mapping selects the route for the custom domain; it does not disable the generated endpoint.

choices.text: Redeploy the REST API to the stage so that the change takes effect.
choices.explanation: For a REST API, updating the stage by redeploying makes disabling the default endpoint effective.

choices.text: Disable the default endpoint in the REST API settings.
choices.explanation: This rejects calls to the default endpoint generated for the API while preserving the existing custom-domain mapping.

choices.text: Delete only the custom-domain alias from Route 53.
choices.explanation: This breaks name resolution for the approved custom domain and does not disable the default endpoint generated by API Gateway.

learning.reason: You can reject calls to the default endpoint generated for the API while preserving the existing custom-domain mapping. For a REST API, updating the stage by redeploying makes the change effective.
learning.concept: Apply default-endpoint disabling through a stage update

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Enable spoke-domain control in a shared inspection VPC
prompt: The security team deployed a stateful domain list in Network Firewall in a central inspection VPC. Traffic from spokes through Transit Gateway reaches the inspection path in both directions, but only requests originating in the inspection VPC are evaluated against the domain list. How should the approved spokes also be inspected by the same policy?

choices.text: Keep only the inspection VPC in HOME_NET and add the spoke CIDRs only to the Transit Gateway propagated routes.
choices.explanation: Reachability is already established. Changing routes does not change the source range used for domain evaluation.

choices.text: Set the inspection VPC and the CIDRs of the spokes to be inspected in HOME_NET of the rule group.
choices.explanation: The default source range for a domain list is the VPC where it is deployed. Explicitly add the source CIDRs that should be inspected.

choices.text: Add each spoke CIDR as a dimension to the rule group's CloudWatch metrics.
choices.explanation: Monitoring classification does not change the traffic evaluation range.

choices.text: Add the spokes' DNS suffixes to the domain list and restrict HOME_NET to the inspection VPC.
choices.explanation: The domain list matches destination names. HOME_NET determines the source range subject to inspection.

learning.reason: The default source range for a domain list is the VPC where it is deployed. Explicitly add the source CIDRs that should be inspected.
learning.concept: Include the spoke and inspection-VPC CIDRs in HOME_NET for the domain list

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Checking That an IAM Policy Revision Does Not Expand Permissions
prompt: A team is organizing the statements in an IAM policy it manages. The team wants CI to verify before deployment that the proposed policy does not add any permissions that are not in the current version. Which method does not rely on CloudTrail usage data or sampled requests?

choices.text: Attach the revised policy to a production role and wait for the result to appear in IAM Access Analyzer unused access findings.
choices.explanation: Unused access findings use usage information. They do not meet the requirement to compare whether new permissions were added before production deployment.

choices.text: Pass the current version as the reference and the proposed version as the comparison policy to CheckNoNewAccess, and stop CI if the new-access check fails.
choices.explanation: This checks whether the proposed policy grants new access compared with the existing policy, rather than comparing the policy text.

choices.text: Use ValidatePolicy to confirm that there are no errors or warnings, and conclude that there are no new permissions if the result is empty.
choices.explanation: General validation checks syntax and recommendations. It does not determine whether access has increased compared with the current version.

choices.text: Use IAM Access Analyzer policy generation to reference historical CloudTrail data and use the result as the proposed policy.
choices.explanation: This feature creates a candidate policy from observed access; it does not comprehensively compare the permissions in the current and proposed policies.

learning.reason: The check evaluates whether the proposed policy grants new access compared with the existing policy, rather than comparing the policy text.
learning.concept: Validating changes against a baseline with IAM Access Analyzer custom policy checks

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Immediately Disabling Only Legacy Public ACLs in S3
prompt: A legacy system's S3 bucket uses ACLs, and private ACL permissions for a contracting partner's AWS account must remain in place until migration is complete. Some existing objects have public ACLs, and there is no public bucket policy. Which setting immediately disables the existing public ACLs without affecting other buckets in the same account?

choices.text: Enable BlockPublicPolicy on the target bucket.
choices.explanation: This setting rejects new public bucket policies; it does not control existing object ACLs.

choices.text: Change the target bucket to Bucket owner enforced and continue using the existing private ACLs as the contracting partner's permissions.
choices.explanation: Bucket owner enforced disables ACLs themselves, so the private ACL permissions required for the business would also be lost.

choices.text: Enable only BlockPublicAcls on the target bucket.
choices.explanation: This rejects new public ACLs, but the effect of public ACLs that already exist remains.

choices.text: Enable IgnorePublicAcls on the target bucket.
choices.explanation: S3 ignores ACLs that allow public access even when those ACLs already exist. Private ACLs targeting a specific account can be preserved.

learning.reason: S3 ignores ACLs that allow public access even when those ACLs already exist, while private ACLs targeting a specific account can be preserved.
learning.concept: IgnorePublicAcls excludes existing public ACLs from evaluation while preserving private ACLs

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Shortening Only the Session Duration of a Privileged AWS Role
prompt: IAM Identity Center users are assigned a read-only permission set and a production-maintenance permission set. The access portal and the read-only role must retain their current usage periods, but future AWS console and CLI sessions for production maintenance must be limited to one hour. Where should this be configured?

choices.text: Add read-only access to the IAM policies in the production-maintenance permission set and give both permission sets the same session duration.
choices.explanation: Changing policies that grant access does not control the expiration of the privileged role sessions that are issued.

choices.text: Set the reauthentication time to one hour for every CLI profile that obtains the production-maintenance role.
choices.explanation: Local profile settings cannot enforce this for AWS console role sessions as well.

choices.text: Change the session duration of the production-maintenance permission set to one hour and apply the change to the AWS accounts to which it is assigned.
choices.explanation: The permission-set setting controls AWS federated sessions for that role without affecting the read-only permission set or the portal's authentication duration.

choices.text: Set the IAM Identity Center access portal session duration to one hour for all users.
choices.explanation: The access portal's authentication duration is separate from the AWS account session duration obtained from a permission set.

learning.reason: The permission-set setting controls the AWS federated session for that role without affecting the read-only role or the portal authentication duration.
learning.concept: AWS account role sessions are controlled by the permission-set session-duration setting

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: A Permission Set Cannot Be Deployed to a Specific Member Account
prompt: An IAM Identity Center permission set references customer managed IAM policies by name and path, prepared to match the resource ARNs in each AWS account. In a new account, the policy itself has been created, but the assignment fails because the policy with the same name was placed at the default root path. How should this be restored without changing existing accounts?

choices.text: In the new account, prepare a policy with the same name and path as the reference, configure the account-specific permissions, and retry the assignment.
choices.explanation: IAM Identity Center looks for a policy with the matching name and path in the account to which the permission set is assigned. The policy contents can be tailored to that account.

choices.text: Stop deployment until the policies in every existing account have been recreated at the root path, then change the permission-set reference everywhere.
choices.explanation: Reconfiguring every account is unnecessary. Matching the new account to the existing reference preserves the assignments in existing accounts.

choices.text: Change the document Version of the policy at the new account's default path to enable name-only resolution.
choices.explanation: The policy language version does not change how the name and path of a customer managed policy reference are matched.

choices.text: Share the policy referenced by the management account with the new account and retry the assignment without creating an additional local policy.
choices.explanation: A permission set requires a local policy with the same name and path in the account where it is deployed.

learning.reason: IAM Identity Center looks for a customer managed policy with the required name and path in each account to which the permission set is assigned; its contents can be account-specific.
learning.concept: Referenced customer managed policies must have matching names and paths in each target account

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Limit shared Pod read permissions in EKS to a specific namespace
prompt: An EKS cluster has a shared ClusterRole that allows only getting and listing Pods. An investigation ServiceAccount needs to view only the workload Pods in one namespace. Which approach meets this requirement without duplicating the existing rule definitions or expanding read permissions to other namespaces?

choices.text: Create a ClusterRoleBinding for the shared ClusterRole and specify the ServiceAccount namespace in the subject.
choices.explanation: The namespace of the subject only identifies the ServiceAccount; the granted scope remains the entire cluster.

choices.text: Copy a Role with the same permissions into the namespace containing the target Pods and associate the ServiceAccount with it through a dedicated RoleBinding.
choices.explanation: This can limit the viewing scope, but it does not meet the requirement to avoid duplicating the existing shared rules.

choices.text: Associate the ServiceAccount with an IAM role for viewing through EKS Pod Identity and use that role to allow listing Pods.
choices.explanation: Pod Identity provides a role for workloads to access AWS APIs; viewing Pods through the Kubernetes API is controlled by RBAC.

choices.text: Place a RoleBinding in the target namespace and specify the shared ClusterRole and the investigation ServiceAccount.
choices.explanation: A RoleBinding can refer to a ClusterRole while granting its permissions only within the namespace where the RoleBinding exists.

learning.reason: A RoleBinding can refer to a ClusterRole while granting its permissions only within that namespace.
learning.concept: Referencing a shared ClusterRole with a namespace-scoped RoleBinding

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Separate API keys for usage management from authorization
prompt: A company wants to track usage by partner for a REST API in API Gateway. Tokens issued by a Cognito User Pool must be validated for partner users, and OAuth scopes for each operation must be enforced. Which configuration performs identity verification while continuing to track usage?

choices.text: Configure a Cognito authorizer and scopes on the method, and also require a usage-plan key.
choices.explanation: The authorizer determines access, while an API key can be associated with a usage plan for each partner.
