learning.reason: Restricting retries to transient errors prevents unlimited re-execution for permanent errors such as insufficient permissions. The original ID can be preserved while passing on the failure reason, and an error does not need to proceed through the success path.
learning.concept: Combining Retry for transient errors only with Catch that preserves the input

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Separating Approval Units for Collection and Isolation in Automated Forensics
prompt: An organization operates EC2 forensics based on AWS Automated Forensics Orchestrator. It performs approved evidence collection even for low-confidence detections, but performs isolation only when approved conditions are met. Which design avoids launching both actions uniformly based on the detection result?

choices.text: Pass every detection result directly to the isolation action, and have a person decide whether isolation is necessary after evidence collection.
choices.explanation: Isolation that affects the service would run before the approval conditions are evaluated.

choices.text: Combine collection and isolation in the same processing role and have the IAM policy automatically infer the approved operation for each case.
choices.explanation: A role defines the scope of operations that can be permitted. Selecting the approved response for an individual case requires a separate decision.

choices.text: Pass only detections that meet the isolation conditions to the workflow, excluding low-confidence observations from evidence collection.
choices.explanation: This prevents unapproved isolation, but it also fails to collect evidence for low-confidence cases whose collection was approved.

choices.text: Evaluate the detection result and target information during triage, separate the conditions for collection and isolation, and select the appropriate response flow.
choices.explanation: Collection and isolation have different purposes and operational impacts. Triage can select the flow so that collection occurs without launching unapproved isolation.

learning.reason: Collection and isolation have different purposes and operational impacts. Triage can select the flow so that collection occurs without launching unapproved isolation.
learning.concept: Evaluate collection and isolation conditions separately during triage

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Restoring Part of EFS Without Colliding with Existing Files
prompt: After an accidental modification to an internal file, you want to restore one directory from an AWS Backup EFS recovery point. You want to keep the current version at its original location for incident investigation, avoid creating a separate file system, and return the restored version to operations after validation. What should you do?

choices.text: Make the original mount target read-only and have the restore operation write into the same directory.
choices.explanation: The mount configuration does not change the restore-destination rules, so the original location and restored version cannot be handled independently.

choices.text: Restore the entire EFS file system to a new file system, then change the mount targets for all clients after validation.
choices.explanation: Creating a new file system and changing all clients exceeds the requirement to restore one directory into the existing EFS file system.

choices.text: Delete the original directory, perform an item-level restore to the same absolute path, and begin the audit afterward.
choices.explanation: This would lose the data retained for the investigation. AWS Backup item-level restore outputs the items to a separate restore directory.

choices.text: Perform an item-level restore of the directory into the existing EFS file system and validate it in the separate restore directory that is created.
choices.explanation: AWS Backup places the restored items in a restore directory under the file system root without overwriting the original path.

learning.reason: AWS Backup places the restored items in a restore directory under the file system root without overwriting the original path.
learning.concept: EFS item-level restore uses a new restore directory under the root even in an existing file system

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Providing an Emergency Access Path When the Identity Provider Is Unavailable
prompt: When the internal IdP went down, responders could not sign in to AWS, delaying recovery. While maintaining normal federation, prepare in advance so that, during an emergency, responders can access only the roles required for recovery through an auditable method. What should be done? Select two.

choices.text: Create a second emergency group within the current IdP that uses the same federation infrastructure.
choices.explanation: Even if the groups are separate, they are still affected by the IdP outage.

choices.text: Distribute the root credentials for every affected account to all on-call responders and compile their use after recovery.
choices.explanation: This broadly shares permanently powerful credentials, so the operations and users cannot be limited to the necessary scope.

choices.text: Rehearse the access procedure without the IdP and verify that assuming the emergency roles can be audited and notifications can be sent.
choices.explanation: Configuring permissions alone does not guarantee that emergency access will work. A rehearsal can verify the process from authentication through auditing.

choices.text: Prepare only a procedure for creating emergency roles after an outage and have the creator use the current federation.
choices.explanation: During the same IdP outage, the creator will not be able to obtain access to prepare a new role.

choices.text: Provide a separate emergency authentication path in a dedicated AWS account and permit only assumption of the roles required for the response.
choices.explanation: This separates the internal IdP from the failure point without adding permanently available permissions for routine administrative operations.

learning.reason: This separates the internal IdP from the failure point without adding permanently available permissions for routine administrative operations. Configuring permissions alone does not guarantee that emergency access will work. A rehearsal can verify the process from authentication through auditing.
learning.concept: Prepare, test, and audit an emergency access path that does not depend on authentication lost during an outage.

category: インシデント対応
examDomain: インシデント対応
title: Requesting the support team to investigate a DDoS affecting a site protected in an organization
prompt: A site in a member account where Shield Advanced was deployed through a Firewall Manager policy is unable to respond because of traffic suspected to be a DDoS attack. The support-request requirements for the SRT are met, and the protected resource and user impact have been identified. What is the correct contact procedure for the owner of the resource?

choices.text: Submit a single request from the Firewall Manager administrator account and use delegated administration as the basis for approving all WAF changes for the members.
choices.explanation: Delegated authority to manage organization policies is different from the authority to approve SRT support for an account-owned by someone else.

choices.text: Leave the owning member account unchanged, add only a Route 53 health check, and wait for the assigned contact to reach out.
choices.explanation: Adding a health check alone does not constitute requesting SRT assistance for the current event.

choices.text: Request assistance from AWS Support through the owning member account, provide the target and impact, and authorize the required support permissions.
choices.explanation: Even when Firewall Manager policies are managed centrally, the account that owns the protected resource must contact the SRT and authorize access.

choices.text: Temporarily remove Shield Advanced protection and move only the SRT contact point to the Firewall Manager account.
choices.explanation: Removing the current protection is unnecessary. The support request can be made by the account that owns the protected resource.

learning.reason: Even when Firewall Manager policies are managed centrally, the account that owns the protected resource must contact the SRT and authorize access.
learning.concept: Shield SRT assistance is requested at the account level by the account that owns the protected resource, which must authorize the required permissions.

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Preventing traffic from passing over a dedicated connection when encryption fails
prompt: MACsec is being introduced on the corresponding dedicated Direct Connect connection between an on-premises environment and AWS. The connection-device and key configuration is complete. If negotiation fails, the organization is willing to tolerate an outage but does not want traffic to switch to plaintext. Which mode should be selected?

choices.text: Use HTTPS for only part of the application and set the dedicated connection's MACsec mode to no_encrypt.
choices.explanation: Application-level TLS and link-wide encryption are different; this does not satisfy the requirement to protect all traffic on the dedicated connection.

choices.text: Strengthen BGP authentication on the virtual interface and leave the MACsec mode at should_encrypt.
choices.explanation: BGP peer authentication does not change link encryption for forwarded data or the fallback policy.

choices.text: Set the connection's MACsec mode to must_encrypt.
choices.explanation: This makes MACsec establishment mandatory and prevents fallback to an unencrypted connection when negotiation does not succeed.

choices.text: Set the connection's MACsec mode to should_encrypt.
choices.explanation: This attempts encryption, but if negotiation fails, traffic may fall back to an unencrypted connection.

learning.reason: This makes MACsec establishment mandatory and prevents fallback to an unencrypted connection when negotiation does not succeed.
learning.concept: must_encrypt does not allow traffic to continue in plaintext when MACsec cannot be established.

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Quickly reestablishing a connection that has lost its inspection state
prompt: A Network Firewall using a Next Generation policy has lost the inspection state of an existing TCP connection because of a temporary failure. The investigation requires the endpoint to be notified of failure immediately, rather than continuing the same connection, so that a new connection can be fully inspected. Which stream exception policy should be used?

choices.text: Enable FLOW logs, set the stream exception setting to Drop, and wait for the endpoint to detect the event from the logs.
choices.explanation: Audit logs do not reset the client's TCP connection.

choices.text: Use Drop to discard packets without sending a response.
choices.explanation: This blocks packets without an inspection state, but it does not explicitly notify the endpoint of failure, so reconnecting may be delayed.

choices.text: Use Continue to evaluate the connection from its current point without reestablishing it.
choices.explanation: Continue cannot be selected with a Next Generation policy. It also does not satisfy the requirement to reinspect from a new connection.

choices.text: Use Reject to return a TCP reset to the client.
choices.explanation: The client can start a new connection that can be inspected without silently waiting for a timeout.

learning.reason: The client can start a new connection that can be inspected without silently waiting for a timeout.
learning.concept: Reject returns a TCP reset and prompts the client to start a new connection with inspection.

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Completing browser verification before calling a JSON API
prompt: An internal application running in a browser displays a sign-in page and then calls a JSON API from JavaScript. The organization wants to retain WAF protection against malicious automation, but the code that reads the JSON cannot handle an HTML Challenge page. Which design is appropriate for authorized browser users?

choices.text: Configure a static custom response for the JSON API in all cases and have legitimate browsers trust only the status value.
choices.explanation: A static response does not provide a token that verifies an individual legitimate browser.

choices.text: Change the JSON API's WAF rules to Count only and have the application continue making calls as before.
choices.explanation: This avoids the incorrect response but removes the requirement to perform verification with the WAF.

choices.text: Configure the AWS WAF client integration in the browser and obtain a token before the first call to the protected API.
choices.explanation: Verifying the user's browser and attaching the token avoids requiring the JSON-processing code to handle an interstitial response.

choices.text: Process every JSON API response as HTML and parse normal JSON responses and challenge responses in the same way.
choices.explanation: Changing the response type alone does not perform browser verification correctly and would break the existing API usage.

learning.reason: Verifying the user's browser and attaching the token avoids requiring the JSON-processing code to handle an interstitial response.
learning.concept: Obtain a token in the browser before sending requests to the API.

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Avoid sharing the host kernel between ECS tasks
prompt: Workers that process submissions from different customers run on ECS. In addition to network restrictions between tasks, the execution boundary must ensure that a task does not use the same OS kernel as another task. The team must not operate EC2 hosts or kernels. Which configuration meets the requirements?

choices.text: Place containers for multiple customers in a shared Fargate task and provide each container with separate environment variables.
choices.explanation: The isolation boundary in Fargate is the task, so containers in the same task do not obtain that boundary from one another.

choices.text: Run the workload on ECS on Fargate as an independent task for each customer.
choices.explanation: Fargate provides an isolation boundary for each task, avoiding kernel sharing with other tasks while delegating host management.

choices.text: Place ordinary ECS tasks on a shared EC2 instance and attach a different awsvpc security group to each task.
choices.explanation: This provides network isolation, but the tasks still share the kernel of the same host.

choices.text: Separate tasks on an existing EC2 instance using only namespaces and create a dedicated IAM task role for each customer.
choices.explanation: Separating processes or AWS authorization is different from providing a task boundary that uses a separate OS kernel.

learning.reason: Fargate provides an isolation boundary for each task, avoiding kernel sharing with other tasks while delegating host management.
learning.concept: ECS on Fargate provides a hardware virtualization boundary for each task.

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Provide approved SSH access to an EC2 instance without a public IP
prompt: Operators need an IAM-managed connection path, and neither a public IP address on the target EC2 instance nor a bastion server may be used. SSH authentication on the operating system is already configured, and the EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint does not preserve the client IP address. Which settings are required for the connection? Select two.

choices.text: Add an internet gateway to the VPC route and have the target EC2 instance receive SSH connections through that route without a public IP address.
choices.explanation: This does not create a configuration for directly connecting over SSH from the internet to a target without a public IP address.

choices.text: Allow OpenTunnel only in the EC2 IAM instance profile and do not change the operator's IAM policy.
choices.explanation: The operator starts the tunnel, so granting the permission only to the EC2 instance role does not authorize the call.

choices.text: Allow the operations role to use OpenTunnel on the approved Endpoint.
choices.explanation: To start an IAM-controlled tunnel, authorize access while restricting it to the intended Endpoint.

choices.text: Remove all inbound SSH access from the target EC2 security group and rely on IAM tunnel authorization so that no inbound rule is needed.
choices.explanation: IAM authorization and network permission to the target ENI are evaluated separately.

choices.text: Configure the Endpoint and EC2 security groups to allow TCP 22 from the Endpoint to the target EC2 instance.
choices.explanation: When the client IP is not preserved, the target EC2 instance must allow SSH connections from the Endpoint.

learning.reason: To start an IAM-controlled tunnel, authorize access while restricting it to the intended Endpoint. When the client IP is not preserved, the target EC2 instance must allow SSH connections from the Endpoint.
learning.concept: Provide both OpenTunnel authorization for an EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint and inbound SSH network permission.

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Monitor suspicious unregistered-domain patterns
prompt: A production VPC uses Route 53 Resolver. The organization also wants to monitor DGA-originated queries for domains that are not in the known-domain list. Initially, it will record detection results without blocking responses in order to assess the impact on normal traffic. Which rule should be associated?

choices.text: Save Resolver query logs and determine whether DGA activity exists using only a threshold for the total number of requests.
choices.explanation: The total query count alone does not evaluate the threat signature in question.

choices.text: Configure a DGA-detection Advanced rule with BLOCK from the start and investigate false positives after operations begin.
choices.explanation: This satisfies the detection requirement but violates the constraint not to block queries during the initial phase.

choices.text: Configure a DGA-detection DNS Firewall Advanced rule with ALERT and associate it with the target VPC.
choices.explanation: The rule evaluates suspicious patterns rather than only matching a known-domain list, and it can record results initially without blocking responses.

choices.text: Configure a DNS Firewall rule that uses a known list of suspicious domains with ALERT.
choices.explanation: This is effective for known matching names, but it does not evaluate patterns in domains that are not registered in the list.

learning.reason: The rule evaluates suspicious patterns rather than only matching a known-domain list, and it can record results initially without blocking responses.
learning.concept: Introduce DNS Firewall Advanced DGA protection gradually by using ALERT.

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Apply browser HSTS centrally through a shared ALB
prompt: Several web applications use the HTTPS listener of the same ALB. A common Strict-Transport-Security header must be configured in HTTPS responses to browsers, and the application code and containers must not be changed. Where should it be configured?

choices.text: Register Strict-Transport-Security as a host condition in the listener rule and send matching requests to the target.
choices.explanation: Routing incoming requests does not add HSTS to the response returned to the browser.

choices.text: Configure Strict-Transport-Security through response header modification on the HTTPS listener.
choices.explanation: The ALB can add a common header value, so the code of each backend does not need to change.

choices.text: Update the listener's TLS security policy and raise the minimum TLS version.
choices.explanation: This controls communication protocols and ciphers; it does not add an HTTP response header.

choices.text: Specify an HSTS path in the target group's health check and send requests to all targets at the same interval.
choices.explanation: Health checks verify target availability and do not change responses to users.

learning.reason: The ALB can add a common header value, so the code of each backend does not need to change.
learning.concept: Configure the HSTS response header on the ALB HTTPS listener.

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Allow S3 access only to buckets in an approved account from an isolated VPC
prompt: Applications in private subnets have no route to S3 other than an S3 gateway endpoint. They must be allowed to use only buckets in one account owned by the company. Which network-side boundary is unaffected by future changes to the permissions of the calling IAM role?

choices.text: Allow only outbound traffic from the application's security group to the S3 prefix list, and leave the endpoint open to all buckets.
choices.explanation: The prefix list identifies network reachability to the S3 service; it does not identify the bucket owner.

choices.text: In the S3 endpoint policy, restrict s3:ResourceAccount to the company's target account.
choices.explanation: For S3 requests using the same path, this restricts the owner of the destination bucket rather than the account to which the calling role belongs.

choices.text: In the endpoint policy, restrict only the caller's aws:PrincipalAccount to the company account.
choices.explanation: Although this restricts the caller, it does not prevent the same role from accessing S3 owned by another account.

choices.text: Add an aws:SourceVpce condition to each approved S3 bucket and make no changes to the egress-side policy.
choices.explanation: This restricts entry to the company's buckets, but it does not restrict access from the same VPC to buckets owned by other parties.

learning.reason: For S3 requests using the same path, the destination bucket owner can be restricted rather than the account to which the calling role belongs.
learning.concept: Restrict the S3 resource-owner account in the endpoint policy

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Keep Lambda connected to a VPC while using external HTTPS
prompt: Lambda must connect to a private database in a VPC while sending IPv4 HTTPS traffic to approved external services. Associating the function with a public subnet does not provide connectivity, and the function does not need to accept direct inbound connections from outside. Which configuration is most appropriate?

choices.text: Associate the function with private subnets and send external traffic through a NAT gateway in a public subnet.
choices.explanation: This preserves the function's VPC connectivity to the database and translates IPv4 traffic originating from the function's private IP for outbound access.

choices.text: Place the function in the same public subnet and enable automatic assignment of public IP addresses for the subnet.
choices.explanation: AWS does not assign public IP addresses to the VPC network interfaces managed by Lambda. The function therefore cannot reach the internet this way.

choices.text: Assign an Elastic IP directly to the function's network interface and remove the private route used for the database.
choices.explanation: An Elastic IP cannot be assigned directly to a Lambda-managed interface, and this would also break the database connectivity requirements.

choices.text: Remove the VPC configuration from the function and leave the private DNS name of the database configured while connecting externally.
choices.explanation: Although this provides internet access, it removes the VPC path to the private database.

learning.reason: This preserves VPC connectivity to the database while translating IPv4 traffic originating from the function's private IP for outbound access.
learning.concept: VPC-connected Lambda functions do not receive public IPs; use NAT from private subnets

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Restrict Transit Gateway destinations to a specific workload security group
prompt: Two VPCs in the same Region are directly connected to the same Transit Gateway. Traffic does not pass through inspection appliances or peering. HTTPS in the destination VPC must be allowed only from the security group of a specific application in the source VPC, without updating CIDRs whenever IP addresses change. Which settings are required? Select two.

choices.text: Open inbound access on the destination to the entire VPC CIDR, and configure the source security group's outbound rule to reference the destination security group.
choices.explanation: Security group referencing through a Transit Gateway cannot be used in outbound rules. Opening inbound access to the entire VPC also broadens the permitted range.

choices.text: Specify the source application's security group in the HTTPS inbound rule of the destination security group.
choices.explanation: Transit Gateway security group referencing is available in inbound rules, so source IP addresses do not need to be enumerated.

choices.text: Allow a broad CIDR in the destination security group and restrict access by specifying the source security group in the Transit Gateway route.
choices.explanation: Route tables forward traffic based on IP prefixes; they cannot grant access based on a source security group.

choices.text: Enable security group referencing on the Transit Gateway itself and on both VPC attachments.
choices.explanation: Referencing through a Transit Gateway requires the feature to be enabled on the gateway and the relevant attachments.

choices.text: Leave referencing disabled on the Transit Gateway and enable it only on the destination attachment.
choices.explanation: The gateway and the required attachments must both have the feature enabled.

learning.reason: Transit Gateway security group referencing must be enabled on the gateway and the relevant attachments, and it can be used in an inbound rule so source IPs do not need to be listed.
learning.concept: Enable security group referencing on the Transit Gateway and both attachments, then reference the source group in the inbound rule

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Do not redirect HTTP requests to an administrative path
prompt: The default viewer path in CloudFront must continue redirecting HTTP to HTTPS. A specific administrative path must accept only requests made over HTTPS and must return a rejection rather than a redirect for plaintext HTTP requests. Where should this be controlled?

choices.text: Create a behavior dedicated to the administrative path and set Viewer Protocol Policy to HTTPS Only.
choices.explanation: HTTP requests to the administrative path are rejected with 403, without affecting redirects configured for other behaviors.

choices.text: Select Redirect HTTP to HTTPS for the administrative-path behavior and use the same host as the redirect destination.
choices.explanation: Even with the same host, this returns a redirect for HTTP requests and therefore does not meet the requirement to reject them.

choices.text: Set only the origin protocol policy to HTTPS Only and retain the viewer-side redirect for the administrative path.
choices.explanation: This encrypts the origin connection but does not change the requirement for rejecting HTTP requests from viewers.

choices.text: Change the entire default behavior to HTTPS Only and do not create a dedicated administrative-path behavior.
choices.explanation: This affects the administrative path but also removes the existing HTTP-to-HTTPS redirects for the normal viewer path.

learning.reason: HTTP requests to the administrative path are rejected with 403, while redirects for other behaviors remain unchanged.
learning.concept: Select HTTPS Only in Viewer Protocol Policy for a dedicated cache behavior

category: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
examDomain: インフラストラクチャのセキュリティ
title: Choose a Session Manager connection that preserves administrative-operation records
prompt: An audit requirement states that interactive commands and output during Linux maintenance must be stored in CloudWatch Logs. Administrators currently use an SSH tunnel through Session Manager. CloudWatch Logs configuration is already in place, and the connection path and execution permissions will continue to be managed with IAM. What change is required?

choices.text: Keep the SSH tunnel, change the log destination to Amazon S3, and expect all interactive activity to be saved.
choices.explanation: Changing the destination does not enable Session Manager to record interactions inside the SSH tunnel.

choices.text: Send the target instance's VPC Flow Logs to CloudWatch and reconstruct the interactive commands and standard output.
choices.explanation: Interactive content cannot be obtained from network-flow records.

choices.text: Move the maintenance activities that must be recorded to the Session Manager standard shell with session logging enabled.
choices.explanation: The standard shell can record interactive data. Through SSH, Session Manager operates as a tunnel and cannot capture shell commands or output.

choices.text: Keep using SSH, store session start and end events in CloudTrail, and obtain the interactive commands and output from the same history.
choices.explanation: API activity records can show who connected and when, but they do not include shell input and output.

learning.reason: The standard shell can record interactive data. Through SSH, Session Manager operates as a tunnel and cannot capture shell commands or output.
learning.concept: Configure recording for the Session Manager standard shell and exclude SSH tunnels from the audit path.

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Prevent pending transactions from being edited even by users with an approval role
prompt: An application uses Amazon Verified Permissions to determine whether edits are allowed. The approver's permit must remain in place, but editing pending transactions must be forbidden for all users, including approvers. The application sends the pending status as a trusted attribute. Which implementation is appropriate?

choices.text: Add an edit forbid conditioned on the pending status, and have the application proceed only when the authorization result is allowed.
choices.explanation: A matching forbid takes precedence over a matching permit. The existing approval-role permissions can remain in effect for transactions that are not pending.

choices.text: Always skip the authorization API for pending transactions and reject them in the application only when the user's token lacks an approver group.
choices.explanation: This does not reject pending-record edits for all users, including approvers.

choices.text: Add an edit permit that matches only pending transactions, broaden the conditions for the same operation, and leave the decision to the application.
choices.explanation: A new permit does not deny the operation. Editing while a transaction is pending would also be covered by an allow.

choices.text: Hide the edit button for pending transactions in the UI and leave the backend authorization policy and existing endpoint unchanged.
choices.explanation: UI-only control cannot cause edit requests to be denied during backend authorization.

learning.reason: A matching forbid takes precedence over a matching permit. The existing approval-role permissions can remain in effect for transactions that are not pending.
learning.concept: Use a Cedar forbid to override permits for the applicable resource.

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Test login risk evaluation without affecting existing users
prompt: The applicable Cognito User Pool plan supports adaptive authentication. The security team wants to collect risk-evaluation results in the production standard login flow and review false positives. During the trial period, risk-based blocking and additional MFA must not be applied. Which setting is appropriate?

choices.text: Run threat protection for standard authentication in Audit only mode and review the evaluation results.
choices.explanation: This collects risk information without enforcing mitigations based on the risk determination.

choices.text: Set high-risk behavior in Full function mode to block, then re-register legitimate users after they are denied.
choices.explanation: Legitimate users could be rejected during the risk-evaluation trial, which conflicts with the requirement not to apply mitigations.

choices.text: Disable threat protection and treat risk evaluation as enabled only when the number of authentication failures exceeds a threshold.
choices.explanation: Although failure counts may be available, this does not collect Cognito's per-login risk evaluations.

choices.text: Require MFA for every user in the User Pool and estimate risk scores only from the MFA notifications received.
choices.explanation: This changes the authentication experience for all users and does not provide adaptive risk evaluations for each login.

learning.reason: This collects risk information without enforcing mitigations based on the risk determination.
learning.concept: Use Cognito threat protection in Audit only mode for an initial evaluation.

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Integrate AWS applications with an existing AD without copying directory data
prompt: A company uses an internal Microsoft Active Directory and wants to use an AWS application that supports AD Connector. Connectivity from AWS to the internal domain controllers is already available. How can the company use the existing authentication without copying users' directory data to a separate AWS directory?

choices.text: Create a new Simple AD in AWS and authenticate users with the same names as their internal accounts.
choices.explanation: Creating accounts with the same names does not connect the application to the existing on-premises authentication.

choices.text: Configure AD Connector and use its connection to the existing domain controllers.
choices.explanation: This uses the existing directory without replicating data to a new directory for users.

choices.text: Create IAM users in each AWS account and manage their passwords the same way as the internal AD accounts.
choices.explanation: This adds separately managed credentials and does not authenticate users through the existing AD.

choices.text: Create users with the same names in AWS Managed Microsoft AD and periodically export and synchronize the accounts.
choices.explanation: This creates user data in a separate directory and does not use the existing directory directly as the authentication source.

learning.reason: This uses the existing directory without replicating data to a new directory for users.
learning.concept: AD Connector brokers authentication with an existing AD while leaving directory data on the domain controllers.

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Use MFA Completed by an External IdP as an AWS-Side Condition
prompt: An AWS operations role is used through SAML federation. A policy for privileged operations should allow only sessions issued after the corporate IdP actually verified MFA. Users must not be able to set their own value indicating that MFA was completed. Which design is appropriate?

choices.text: Set the privileged-operation condition to aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent=true and assume that it automatically becomes true when authentication is performed through SAML.
choices.explanation: The IAM MFA context key does not automatically represent MFA performed by the federation IdP.

choices.text: Pass an attribute managed by the IdP that identifies the authentication method as a trusted session tag, and check that value in the privileged-operation condition.
choices.explanation: Authentication for federation occurs at the IdP. An attribute assigned by a trusted IdP that users cannot overwrite can be used for evaluation in AWS.

choices.text: Let the user specify the SAML RoleSessionName and allow the operation for sessions whose name ends with mfa.
choices.explanation: A name that the user can specify is not evidence that MFA was performed by the IdP.

choices.text: Set the IAM role's maximum session duration to one hour to identify sessions in which MFA was performed.
choices.explanation: Session duration is unrelated to the authentication method and cannot determine whether MFA was used.

learning.reason: Federated authentication occurs at the IdP. An attribute assigned by a trusted IdP and protected from user modification can be used for evaluation in AWS.
learning.concept: Evaluate federated MFA by passing an attribute from a trusted IdP as a session tag

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Give a Contract Partner Only One Approved Version of an S3 Object
prompt: An S3 delivery file with versioning enabled has multiple versions. A review role for a contract partner, created in the bucket-owning account, must read only the audit-approved version ID of the same key. The role has no other S3 permissions. Which permission should be granted?

choices.text: Allow s3:GetObjectVersion for the key and add a condition requiring s3:VersionId to match the approved ID.
choices.explanation: This evaluates both the key being accessed and the requested version ID, preventing reads of other versions.

choices.text: Allow s3:GetObject for the key and operate the object so that its current version points to the approved version.
choices.explanation: A change to the latest version can change what is allowed. This does not bind the permission to a specific version ID.

choices.text: Allow s3:GetObjectVersion for the key without conditions and remove only the permission to list versions.
choices.explanation: Even without listing permissions, a known different version ID could still be used. A read condition is required.

choices.text: Restrict bucket-list operations using the approved ID string and allow reads of all versions of the key.
choices.explanation: A listing condition does not affect permission to retrieve object versions.

learning.reason: In addition to the key being accessed, evaluate the requested version ID so that reads of other versions are not allowed.
learning.concept: Restrict GetObjectVersion to a specific object and s3:VersionId

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Pin External-Account Invocation to a Lambda Production Alias
prompt: An application in an external account should invoke only the production interface of a Lambda function operated by the owning account. The owning account should not require changes to the external permission whenever the version is updated, and calls to a test alias or to the unqualified function must not be allowed. The external IAM permission is already prepared. How should the owning account configure its resource permission?

choices.text: Grant permission only to the ARN of the current version, and configure the external application to invoke that ARN.
choices.explanation: Pinning the version requires changing the permission and invocation target whenever the deployment is migrated.

choices.text: Allow invocation of the entire function and document in the operating procedures that the external application must use only production.
choices.explanation: An operational agreement cannot enforce that the permission applies only to the production alias.

choices.text: Grant invocation permission on the production alias to the approved external principal, and require the external application to use that ARN.
choices.explanation: Binding permission to the alias preserves the invocation contract even when the version referenced by the alias changes.

choices.text: Trust the external account in the function's execution role and add permission to invoke another Lambda function to that role.
choices.explanation: The execution role controls operations performed by the function at runtime; it does not restrict external invocation requests to this alias.

learning.reason: Binding permission to the alias preserves the invocation contract even when the version referenced by the alias changes.
learning.concept: Attach a resource-based invocation permission to a Lambda alias

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Limit the RDS Database User for IAM Authentication to One User
prompt: IAM database authentication is enabled for RDS for PostgreSQL, and report_reader has been configured on the database. The EC2 application role should be allowed to connect to one RDS instance only as that database user. How should the IAM policy be written?

choices.text: Grant IAM permission to connect as every database user on the target instance, and fix the user in the application's configuration file.
choices.explanation: Even if the application configuration is protected, the IAM permission covers every database user and is not limited to one specific user.

choices.text: Grant rds:DescribeDBInstances and specify only the standard RDS instance ARN.
choices.explanation: Retrieving instance information and permission to connect to a database through IAM authentication are separate permissions.

choices.text: Allow rds-db:connect and set the display database instance identifier and the application's IAM role name in the dbuser resource.
choices.explanation: The required values are the immutable DB resource ID and the actual database username. An IAM role name or display name cannot substitute for them.

choices.text: Allow rds-db:connect and specify the database instance's resource ID and report_reader in the dbuser resource.
choices.explanation: For IAM database authentication, the resource combines the DB resource ID of the target instance with the database user.

learning.reason: For IAM database authentication, the resource combines the DB resource ID of the target instance with the database user.
learning.concept: Specify the DB resource ID and database username in the rds-db:connect resource

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Preventing credentials from being attached to a Pod that does not need the Kubernetes API
prompt: In the same EKS namespace, one batch job does not use the Kubernetes API. The batch must use the same ServiceAccount as the other Pods, and existing Pod connections must remain working. How can you prevent an API token from being automatically injected into new Pods for this batch?

choices.text: Set automountServiceAccountToken to false in the batch Pod specification.
choices.explanation: Only the target Pods skip the normal automatic mount, so the behavior of other Pods using the ServiceAccount does not change.

choices.text: Block inbound traffic from the batch at the security group for the Kubernetes API, regardless of whether the token enters the container.
choices.explanation: Whether network communication is allowed and whether credentials are attached to the Pod are separate matters.

choices.text: Remove the ServiceAccount name environment variable from the Pod container while leaving the default automatic mount enabled.
choices.explanation: Token mounting is determined by the Pod specification and ServiceAccount settings; removing an arbitrary environment variable does not stop it.

choices.text: Disable automatic mounting for the shared ServiceAccount without checking the configuration of existing shared workloads.
choices.explanation: Changing the shared setting would also affect other Pods when they are recreated.

learning.reason: Only the target Pods skip the normal automatic mount, so the behavior of other Pods using the ServiceAccount does not change.
learning.concept: Turn off automatic injection with the Pod-level automountServiceAccountToken setting

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Restricting rows and columns in the same table at the same time
prompt: An Athena user queries a Lake Formation-managed sales table. Staff members should see only rows for their assigned regions, and the payment identifier column should also be excluded. Do not create another copy of the data, and the staff role does not have permission to read S3 directly. How should access be granted?

choices.text: Create a data filter with a row expression for the assigned region and the permitted columns, then grant SELECT with that filter.
choices.explanation: The filter can apply conditions to catalog-table rows and columns, limiting Athena output against the same data to the required scope.

choices.text: Distribute a saved query that includes the assigned region in a WHERE clause while retaining SELECT on the entire table.
choices.explanation: A shared query is only a convenience configuration. The remaining permission would still allow the entire table to be read through another query.

choices.text: Apply the assigned region as an LF-Tag on the table and grant the role SELECT without a filter.
choices.explanation: Table tags govern authorization for the table as a whole; they do not individually restrict rows or columns.

choices.text: Configure only a column-restriction filter and record the region in an Amazon S3 bucket tag.
choices.explanation: A bucket tag does not exclude regional rows from an Athena table.

learning.reason: The filter can apply conditions to catalog-table rows and columns, limiting Athena output against the same data to the required scope.
learning.concept: Use a Lake Formation data filter to configure row expressions and column restrictions together

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Preparing IAM to target a secret before it is created
prompt: An application IAM role must be allowed to access only the Secrets Manager secret named app/report-db in a specific Region and account. The secret does not yet exist, and its ARN suffix, which is assigned at creation time, cannot be known in advance. Do not extend permission to other secrets with very similar names. Which Resource specification should be used?

choices.text: Use secret:app/report-db* as the secret ARN, matching other secrets that begin with the same string.
choices.explanation: This extends permission to similarly named secrets that are not managed by the application.

choices.text: Allow GetSecretValue on every secret in the target account and restrict access using the application configuration's reference name.
choices.explanation: Runtime configuration is not an IAM permission boundary.

choices.text: End the secret ARN with secret:app/report-db and assume that IAM implicitly excludes the random characters.
choices.explanation: The six-character suffix is included in the ARN used for authorization matching. The name alone does not match the complete ARN.

choices.text: Use secret:app/report-db-?????? for the relevant part of the secret ARN, while fixing the account and Region.
choices.explanation: This matches the variable random six-character suffix without broadly specifying other longer names.

learning.reason: This matches the variable random six-character suffix without broadly specifying other longer names.
learning.concept: Fix the name and match only the six characters added by Secrets Manager with IAM's single-character wildcard

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Excluding only one device certificate from new sessions
prompt: IAM Roles Anywhere uses certificates issued by an internal CA. The certificate for one retired device has been revoked. Keep trust for the other devices and reject issuance of new sessions. The CA's CRL distribution point cannot be reached from AWS, but signed CRLs can be retrieved internally on a regular basis. What should be configured?

choices.text: Shorten only the IAM role session duration until the retired device's certificate expires.
choices.explanation: Shortening the duration does not change whether new sessions can be issued from the revoked certificate.

choices.text: Import the latest signed CRL into Roles Anywhere, enable it, and update it regularly.
choices.explanation: This stops new authentication with certificates listed in the CRL while preserving the trust anchor. No configuration that references a publicly distributed endpoint is required.

choices.text: Enable automatic checking using only the unpublished CRL distribution point and do not import the signed CRL obtained internally.
choices.explanation: An accessible distribution point is required for that approach. Explicitly importing the CRL available internally meets the requirement.

choices.text: Disable the trust anchor to stop sessions for the retired device while having the other devices use the same anchor.
choices.explanation: Once the trust anchor is disabled, devices that have not been retired cannot obtain new sessions either.

learning.reason: This stops new authentication with certificates listed in the CRL while preserving the trust anchor. No configuration that references a publicly distributed endpoint is required.
learning.concept: Associate a signed CRL with the trust anchor and reject revoked certificates in new authentication requests

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Preventing AWS credentials when Cognito cannot select a role
prompt: A Cognito Identity Pool uses the roles in the groups contained in a User Pool token. A user's token contains multiple candidates, and no preferred role is configured. The application does not explicitly specify a role and must not fall back to the default authenticated role when the candidates are ambiguous. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Use token-based selection and return AuthenticatedRole when role resolution is ambiguous.
choices.explanation: This assigns the default authenticated role to an ambiguous user, which is the opposite of the required behavior.

choices.text: Use token-based role selection and set the behavior for ambiguous role resolution to Deny.
choices.explanation: When there is no preferred role and multiple candidates exist, this prevents temporary credentials for the default role from being issued.

choices.text: Shorten the User Pool ID token lifetime without changing the role priority.
choices.explanation: The token lifetime does not change how multiple role candidates are resolved.

choices.text: Only disable guest access and leave the resolution setting for multiple role candidates at its default.
choices.explanation: Unauthenticated guests and authenticated users with ambiguous roles are separate cases.

learning.reason: When there is no preferred role and multiple candidates exist, temporary credentials for the default role are no longer issued.
learning.concept: Set the Identity Pool's AmbiguousRoleResolution to Deny

category: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
examDomain: アイデンティティとアクセス管理
title: Reading data with each user's permissions from a shared analytics tool
prompt: An internal BI tool queries a shared data lake through Athena. Currently, all queries arrive under the same application role, so Lake Formation cannot distinguish between different user groups. Which approach, using a compatible client, authorizes access for individual IAM Identity Center users federated from the corporate IdP?

choices.text: Set both group names as fixed tags on the application role and infer which group each user belongs to for every query.
choices.explanation: Because every request uses the same tags, the originating user or group cannot be distinguished.

choices.text: Keep the users consolidated in the existing workgroup, encrypt the results in S3, and make no changes to user-specific access policies.
choices.explanation: Encrypting results at rest does not provide per-user authorization to query the tables.

choices.text: Grant the shared role table permissions for both groups and hide table names only in the BI interface.
choices.explanation: The underlying service still does not distinguish users and operates with a broadly permitted role. This is not per-user authorization at the data layer.

choices.text: Configure trusted identity propagation from the BI tool to Athena and grant permissions in Lake Formation to IAM Identity Center users or groups.
choices.explanation: This lets the data services identify end users and eliminates the state in which only one shared role is evaluated for everyone.

learning.reason: This lets the data services identify end users and eliminates the state in which only one shared role is evaluated for everyone.
learning.concept: Pass user identities to Athena and Lake Formation through trusted identity propagation

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Keeping selected form fields encrypted until the final application
prompt: HTTPS form POST requests received by CloudFront use the standard URL-encoded format and pass through a relay application. You want only the final processing service, which holds the private key, to be able to read the form's verification number. Which configuration meets the requirement?

choices.text: Configure the target form field and a public key in CloudFront, and place the corresponding private key only in the final processing service.
choices.explanation: CloudFront encrypts the target field, so even if TLS is terminated at the relay, the field remains unavailable in plaintext.

choices.text: Configure the target field for log masking in WAF and leave form forwarding unchanged.
choices.explanation: Reducing exposure in logs does not encrypt the form field as it passes between applications.

choices.text: Enable CloudFront signed cookies and require a cookie for every request containing the verification number.
choices.explanation: Cookies authorize access to resources; they do not encrypt a specific form field.

choices.text: Use HTTPS between CloudFront and the origin, terminate TLS at each relay, and process the form as before.
choices.explanation: TLS on each hop protects the connection, but it does not protect the plaintext field that each relay can read after termination.

learning.reason: CloudFront encrypts the target field, so relays that terminate TLS still cannot obtain the field in plaintext.
learning.concept: Use CloudFront field-level encryption and keep the private key in the final processing service

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Revalidating only migrated files after transfer
prompt: A large file share is migrated regularly by using an AWS DataSync incremental task. In addition to verification during transfer, you want to confirm after processing that the files transferred this time match the destination. There is not enough time to reread every unchanged file on each run. Which setting is appropriate?

choices.text: Select POINT_IN_TIME_CONSISTENT for VerifyMode and compare the entire dataset, including files not transferred this time.
choices.explanation: This verifies the entire dataset and therefore does not meet the requirement to avoid checking unchanged files every time.

choices.text: Leave VerifyMode set to NONE and only confirm that the DataSync transferred-volume metric matches the total volume planned for migration.
choices.explanation: Matching byte counts does not prove that file contents match.

choices.text: Select ONLY_FILES_TRANSFERRED for VerifyMode.
choices.explanation: This performs post-transfer verification on the data that was transferred without requiring the entire dataset to be reverified on every run.

choices.text: Select NONE for VerifyMode and record that post-transfer comparison was completed whenever the task succeeds.
choices.explanation: NONE can still perform integrity checks during transfer, but it does not perform a post-transfer comparison.

learning.reason: This performs post-transfer verification on the transferred data without requiring the entire dataset to be reverified on every run.
learning.concept: DataSync post-transfer verification limited to transferred data

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Set a validity limit for certificates issued to internal services
prompt: A service that runs only for a short period uses TLS certificates from an existing organizational CA hierarchy. Even if the issuing service accidentally requests a long validity period, certificates issued by the CA for this purpose must not be valid for more than 7 days. Issuance uses the Private CA API directly. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Operate a CA in general-purpose mode and set the validity period of normal issuance jobs to 7 days.
choices.explanation: Although normal requests can be configured with a short validity period, the CA would still be able to process an accidentally submitted long-term request.

choices.text: Update the service name using a short DNS TTL and leave the certificate validity period unchanged.
choices.explanation: The DNS cache duration and the TLS certificate validity period are separate settings.

choices.text: Issue long-lived certificates from a general-purpose CA, enable OCSP when the service ends, and check the certificates.
choices.explanation: Configuring certificate revocation checking does not limit the maximum validity period of certificates that can be issued.

choices.text: Create a dedicated Private CA in short-lived certificate mode and use it for issuance.
choices.explanation: In this CA mode, the validity period of issued certificates is limited to a maximum of 7 days.

learning.reason: In this CA mode, the validity period of issued certificates is limited to a maximum of 7 days.
learning.concept: Use a dedicated Private CA in short-lived certificate mode

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Recover keys from a CloudHSM backup
prompt: A cluster used by an application that accesses CloudHSM directly rather than through KMS is no longer usable. An approved backup contains the required HSM users and keys, and recovery will be attempted in a separate healthy private subnet from the original cluster. Which combination of steps should be used? Select two.

choices.text: Grant a new IAM role all CloudHSM API permissions and omit reconfiguring the HSM users and specifying the backup.
choices.explanation: AWS API permissions do not restore the users and keys inside the HSM.

choices.text: Generate keys with the same labels in a new empty cluster and assume that the key material is the same.
choices.explanation: A label is identification information. Newly generated key material with the same name cannot reproduce cryptographic operations on existing data.

choices.text: Select a backup containing the required keys and users, and create a new CloudHSM cluster from it.
choices.explanation: Using the backup as the starting point restores the same key material and user configuration to the new cluster.

choices.text: Add an HSM to the new cluster, connect the application to the recovery environment, and validate it.
choices.explanation: The backup contents are restored to the added HSM, allowing cryptographic operations to be verified through the cluster.

choices.text: Extract the key material from the CloudHSM backup file and distribute it as plaintext files for the application.
choices.explanation: This recovery method restores the backup inside the HSM. Distributing plaintext key material to the application is unnecessary.

learning.reason: Using the backup as the starting point restores the same key material and user configuration to the new cluster. The backup contents are restored to the added HSM, allowing cryptographic operations to be verified through the cluster.
learning.concept: Create a cluster from an existing CloudHSM backup and add an HSM

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Restrict S3 ingestion to a specified encryption key
prompt: New PutObject requests to an audit prefix in S3 must explicitly specify the full ARN of a designated customer managed KMS key in a header. Only some clients send the correct header. How should this be configured to reject missing configuration or uploads using another key while avoiding impact on other uses of the same bucket?

choices.text: Require only the SSE-KMS algorithm setting and allow users to choose the KMS key ID.
choices.explanation: Requests that use a different key with the same encryption method cannot be excluded.

choices.text: Use S3 Inventory to inspect the encryption state after ingestion and have operators correct different keys later.
choices.explanation: Post-ingestion checks cannot stop a noncompliant upload at the time it is accepted.

choices.text: Set the bucket's default encryption to the specified KMS key and do not check the upload header.
choices.explanation: Default encryption does not require the header to be explicit, nor does it restrict a different encryption setting specified by the client.

choices.text: For the targeted PutObject requests, reject requests that do not specify SSE-KMS or whose KMS key ARN is missing or does not match.
choices.explanation: Without relying only on default encryption, the policy can check the ARN of the key specified for requests to the target prefix and reject noncompliant requests.

learning.reason: Without relying only on default encryption, the policy can check the ARN of the key specified for requests to the target prefix and reject noncompliant requests.
learning.concept: Use a prefix-scoped bucket policy to Deny an unspecified or mismatched KMS ARN

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Use a rotated secret in a running Pod
prompt: An application running on an EC2 node in EKS mounts a Secrets Manager value as a file through ASCP. Rotation in Secrets Manager succeeds, but the application continues using the old value until the Pod is redeployed. Without embedding the value in the image, what should be done to make the new value available to the running application? Select two.

choices.text: Only shorten the Secrets Manager rotation interval and leave the Pod's file ingestion configuration unchanged.
choices.explanation: Increasing how often the service changes the value does not add a mechanism for delivering the new value to the Pod.

choices.text: Rebuild the container image with the latest secret value and store it in the registry each time.
choices.explanation: This puts the secret in the image and satisfies neither confidentiality nor dynamic updates.

choices.text: Configure the application to detect changes to the mounted file and reload the value.
choices.explanation: Even if the file is updated, the process will not switch values if it retains the value read at startup. It must actually read the new value again.

choices.text: Copy the mounted value into an environment variable at startup and assume that the existing process environment variable will update automatically when the file changes.
choices.explanation: The updated file and the environment variables of an existing process are separate. The application will not obtain the new value.

choices.text: Enable the rotation reconciler of the Secrets Store CSI Driver.
choices.explanation: It can retrieve the new Secrets Manager value and continuously reflect it in the mounted file.

learning.reason: The rotation reconciler retrieves the new Secrets Manager value and reflects it in the mounted file. If the process retains the value read at startup, the application must also read the new value again when the file changes.
learning.concept: Combine CSI rotation with application-side file reloading

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Creating Encrypted Analytical Data from an RDS Snapshot
prompt: An auditor needs to use Athena to inspect only the required tables from the corresponding RDS snapshot. Without keeping a new database running continuously, export Parquet files to an approved S3 bucket in the same Region, encrypted with a specified KMS key. How should this be implemented?

choices.text: Re-encrypt the DB snapshot with KMS to create another snapshot, then register that backup as Parquet.
choices.explanation: Re-encryption does not convert the snapshot format. Data must be exported to generate Parquet files.

choices.text: Retrieve the snapshot metadata from CloudTrail, grant only access to S3, and recreate the original tables.
choices.explanation: Operation history and metadata do not contain the tables themselves.

choices.text: Use RDS snapshot export to select the target tables, S3, the IAM role for the export, and the specified KMS key.
choices.explanation: For supported engines, the selected data can be exported as Parquet, and the specified key can be used for SSE-KMS during export.

choices.text: Add snapshot-sharing permissions to the auditor role and register the snapshot ARN as the location of an Athena table.
choices.explanation: Athena cannot read an RDS snapshot ARN directly as a table. An analyzable output in S3 is required.

learning.reason: For supported engines, the selected data can be exported as Parquet, and the specified key can be used for SSE-KMS during export.
learning.concept: Specify the target tables, S3, IAM role, and KMS key in RDS snapshot export.

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Keeping Plaintext Keys Away from the Application During Key Changes
prompt: A service stores many ciphertexts of data keys encrypted with a symmetric KMS key. The service must migrate to a new management key, and the migration process must not retrieve the plaintext data keys. Which approach grants only the minimum required operations on the old and new keys?

choices.text: Call KMS ReEncrypt, allowing the migration role to use ReEncryptFrom with the old key and ReEncryptTo with the new key.
choices.explanation: KMS performs decryption and re-encryption internally and returns only the new ciphertext to the migration process.

choices.text: Configure automatic rotation for the old KMS key and treat it as having changed to a new management key while remaining the same KMS key.
choices.explanation: Automatic rotation updates key material for the same KMS key. It does not migrate to a different management key.

choices.text: Add the new key ARN to the metadata, leave the existing ciphertexts unchanged, and decrypt them with the new key.
choices.explanation: The ciphertexts are protected by the old key. Changing external configuration does not make them decryptable with the new key.

choices.text: Have the migration role call Decrypt on the old key, keep the returned plaintext key in memory, and call Encrypt with the new key.
choices.explanation: Even if the plaintext is not persisted, it appears in the migration process, violating the requirement that the process not retrieve plaintext.

learning.reason: KMS performs decryption and re-encryption internally and returns only the new ciphertext to the migration process.
learning.concept: Use ReEncrypt to switch the key protection of ciphertext key material inside KMS.

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Masking Personally Identifiable Information While Preserving the Response
prompt: Responses from an internal help service using Bedrock sometimes include test-data email addresses in plain text. The requirement is to display the response without rejecting it entirely, while anonymizing only the email addresses. Which approach does not rely solely on instructing the model?

choices.text: Apply the Guardrails sensitive information filter to the response and set the output action for detected email addresses to Mask.
choices.explanation: The target PII is replaced with type-appropriate symbols, while the rest of the response can be presented to the user.

choices.text: Encrypt the model invocation logs with KMS and leave the response displayed to the user unchanged.
choices.explanation: Encrypting stored logs does not anonymize the response body.

choices.text: Set the sensitive information filter output action to Block and reject every response containing an email address.
choices.explanation: This prevents the information from being returned, but it does not meet the requirement to present the rest of the response.

choices.text: Tell the model in its system instructions not to display email addresses, without performing any additional inspection of the response.
choices.explanation: Model instructions alone are not an independent inspection condition that masks target information in the output.

learning.reason: The target PII is replaced with type-appropriate symbols, while the rest of the response can be presented to the user.
learning.concept: Mask output PII with the Bedrock Guardrails sensitive information filter.

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Applying Encrypted Password Settings to an Existing Glue JDBC Connection
prompt: The Glue Data Catalog contains an existing JDBC connection whose connection-password encryption was not enabled when the connection was created. The requirement now is to encrypt the password with a specified KMS key. Which approach applies this to the existing connection while preserving its authentication method and target database?

choices.text: Change the current connection string to require only JDBC TLS and do not save the connection password again.
choices.explanation: TLS protects data in transit. It does not encrypt the stored Glue connection password with the configured KMS key.

choices.text: Configure connection-password encryption and the key to use in the Data Catalog, then update and save the existing JDBC connection.
choices.explanation: Encryption is applied when a connection is created or updated. Updating the existing connection applies the current settings.

choices.text: Configure the specified KMS key as the default encryption for S3 where Glue jobs write data and assume that the connection password inherits the key.
choices.explanation: S3 encryption for the data destination does not apply to connection information in the Glue Data Catalog.

choices.text: Enable only Data Catalog metadata encryption and leave the connection-password settings and existing connection unchanged.
choices.explanation: Connection-password encryption is an independent setting, so this does not provide the required application method.

learning.reason: Encryption is applied when a connection is created or updated. Updating the existing connection applies the current settings.
learning.concept: Configure connection-password encryption in the Data Catalog and update the connection.

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Prevent accidental deletion of an entire DynamoDB table
prompt: A business team continues to update and delete DynamoDB items as part of lifecycle management. The existing table itself must not be accidentally deleted with DeleteTable while deletion protection is enabled, even if operators already have broad permissions. What should be used?

choices.text: Disable the table's TTL and leave the administrator's DeleteTable permission unchanged.
choices.explanation: TTL handles item expiration; it does not prevent deletion of the entire table.

choices.text: Create an on-demand backup of the table and assume that DeleteTable will be denied as long as the backup exists.
choices.explanation: A backup can be used for recovery, but it is not a setting that denies DeleteTable.

choices.text: Remove only the DeleteItem permission for the target table while continuing to allow DeleteTable as before.
choices.explanation: This prevents the required item deletions while doing nothing to prevent accidental deletion of the table.

choices.text: Enable deletion protection for the target DynamoDB table.
choices.explanation: While protection is enabled, deletion of the table itself is denied, while existing item operations can continue under their respective permissions.

learning.reason: While protection is enabled, deletion of the table itself is denied, while existing item operations can continue under their respective permissions.
learning.concept: Table deletion protection applies at the table level and does not apply to item operations.

category: データ保護
examDomain: データ保護
title: Configure encryption according to EMR destinations and communication paths
prompt: On an EMR cluster running on EC2, encrypt EMRFS S3 output, local data on the nodes, and communication between nodes. Match each protection target with the feature to enable in the EMR security configuration.

choices.text: Local disk encryption in the security configuration
choices.explanation: Enables encryption for the disks where EMR nodes store intermediate data.

choices.text: Amazon S3 SSE-KMS for EMRFS
choices.explanation: Applies server-side encryption at rest using a KMS key to data in S3 accessed through EMRFS.

choices.text: Encryption in transit in the security configuration
choices.explanation: Encrypts communication between the supported distributed-processing components.

learning.reason: Amazon S3 data accessed through EMRFS uses server-side encryption at rest with a KMS key. Local disk encryption protects the disks where EMR nodes store intermediate data. Encryption in transit protects network communication between supported distributed-processing components.
learning.concept: EMR security configuration features have distinct roles for EMRFS S3 data, local disks, and data in transit.

prompts.text: Analytics results output by EMRFS to the shared bucket
In-process data written to the disks of EC2 nodes
Network communication between supported distributed-processing components

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Prevent DB replacement and deletion when updating a production stack
prompt: CloudFormation manages a web application and an RDS database in the same stack. Normal releases must be able to update the application, but updates that replace or delete the DB must not run without approval. The changes must also be reviewed before deployment. Which combination should be used? Select two.

choices.text: Use a change set to review whether the DB will be replaced or deleted, and execute only an approved change set.
choices.explanation: The impact can be reviewed before changes are applied. Creating a change set alone does not modify the stack.

choices.text: Set the DB's DeletionPolicy to Retain and assume that the entire update will be rejected when the change set includes a replacement.
choices.explanation: This setting specifies what happens to an existing resource during deletion; it does not restrict replacement in a change set or the update itself.

choices.text: Enable only CloudFormation termination protection and assume that it will also prevent an individual DB from being replaced during a stack update.
choices.explanation: Termination protection applies to deletion of the stack itself. It does not similarly restrict resource replacement during a normal update.

choices.text: Deny Update:Replace and Update:Delete for the DB logical resource in the normal stack policy.
choices.explanation: For the DB, this enforces that CloudFormation stack updates cannot replace or delete the resource.

choices.text: Run drift detection after deployment and treat a successful application update as evidence that DB replacement was approved.
choices.explanation: A post-deployment check cannot prevent the accident and is not evidence that approval was obtained.

learning.reason: A change set allows the impact to be reviewed before application, and creating one alone does not modify the stack. A stack policy can enforce that CloudFormation stack updates do not replace or delete the DB.
learning.concept: Use a change set to review update impact and a stack policy to deny DB replacement and deletion.

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Include template-omitted defaults in drift detection
prompt: A CloudFormation-managed resource has a security-sensitive property that supports drift detection. At creation time, the desired service default was used, so the property was omitted from the template. How can a manual change to a different value be reflected in CloudFormation drift detection?

choices.text: Record the expected value in the template's Description, leave the property omitted, and run drift detection.
choices.explanation: Descriptive text is not evaluated as the expected state of a property.

choices.text: Specify the expected value in the template, apply it, and then compare it during drift detection.
choices.explanation: CloudFormation treats a property explicitly specified in the template as the expected value. Explicitly stating the default makes it part of the comparison.

choices.text: Only change drift detection to run on a schedule and wait for the service-side default to be automatically added to the template.
choices.explanation: Increasing the frequency does not change which explicitly specified properties CloudFormation compares.

choices.text: Put the same default value in a parameter but do not reference that parameter from the resource property.
choices.explanation: Defining a parameter alone does not set the expected value of the resource property.

learning.reason: CloudFormation treats a property explicitly specified in the template as the expected value. Explicitly stating the default makes it part of the comparison.
learning.concept: Explicitly include even default values in the template for properties that must be monitored.

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Restricting Organization-Wide Use of Input Data to Improve AWS AI Services
prompt: An organization uses Amazon Transcribe across multiple accounts. It must continue using an existing feature that processes business audio while centrally enforcing that content is not used to improve the applicable AWS AI service, including in accounts added in the future. Which setting should the organization use?

choices.text: Use an SCP for all accounts to deny calls to transcribe.
choices.explanation: This would stop use of the service itself, which does not meet the requirement to exclude only improvement-related use.

choices.text: Delete input audio early with the current S3 lifecycle configurations in each account, and configure the setting after each new account is created.
choices.explanation: This controls S3 object retention; it is neither a centralized setting for improvement use nor automatically inherited by new accounts.

choices.text: Encrypt the S3 keys for the audio and transcription results, without configuring the AI service data-use setting.
choices.explanation: Encrypting customer-managed inputs and outputs does not establish a policy for how the applicable AI service may use data for improvement.

choices.text: Continue using the service and configure an AI services opt-out policy at the Organizations root.
choices.explanation: This centrally controls improvement-related use of content by the applicable AI services while allowing the services' processing capabilities to continue.

learning.reason: The organization can control improvement-related use of content across the organization while continuing to use the services' processing capabilities.
learning.concept: Apply an Organizations AI services opt-out policy at the root

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Continuously Evaluating Backup Plan Frequency and Retention
prompt: An organization wants to periodically verify that AWS Backup plans owned by multiple teams are configured for at least daily backups and retention of at least 90 days. It will report plans that do not meet the requirements but must not automatically change any team's plan. Which approach is appropriate?
