choices.text: Set a minimum retention period with Vault Lock in each vault and simultaneously enforce the backup job frequency.
choices.explanation: Vault Lock constrains retention; it does not evaluate the execution interval configured in a backup plan.

choices.text: If an annual bulk restore test succeeds, classify all current backup plans as meeting daily backups and 90-day retention.
choices.explanation: A successful restore shows that particular backups can be used; it does not verify ongoing compliance of plan frequency and retention.

choices.text: Enable the required AWS Config recording and configure minimum-frequency and minimum-retention controls in a Backup Audit Manager framework.
choices.explanation: This evaluates backup plans against specified values without replacing the plan settings during the assessment.

choices.text: Treat the presence of a CreateBackupPlan event in every team's CloudTrail audit logs as proof that the retention period and frequency requirements are met.
choices.explanation: The existence of a plan-creation event does not reveal the plan's current backup frequency or retention period.

learning.reason: Backup plans can be evaluated against specified values without the assessment itself replacing their configuration.
learning.concept: Evaluate plans with AWS Backup Audit Manager minimum-frequency and retention controls

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Filtering Operational Alerts to Reduce Notification Volume
prompt: A platform team wants to deliver specific security-related AWS Health event types to an operations email address. It must filter by target Region and event type before sending and aggregate notifications on the service side when similar events continue. The existing event source must remain unchanged. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Create a different SNS topic for each event and subscribe the same email address to all of them.
choices.explanation: Using the same destination does not aggregate notifications, so repeated events would still increase the number of messages.

choices.text: Store audit logs in bulk in CloudTrail trails and stop AWS Health notifications until the same trail files are delivered.
choices.explanation: Trail storage does not evaluate AWS Health events or aggregate and deliver them to the operations email address.

choices.text: Create filtering rules on the receiving email system and have the publisher send every event, including events outside the target set.
choices.explanation: This filters after receipt and does not limit the type or number of notifications sent by the service.

choices.text: Use AWS User Notifications settings to filter event rules and configure notification aggregation and the operations delivery destination.
choices.explanation: This limits delivery to the required events and can combine multiple events into fewer notifications according to the selected aggregation settings.

learning.reason: The configuration can limit delivery to required events and combine multiple events into fewer notifications according to the selected aggregation settings.
learning.concept: Use User Notifications event conditions and notification aggregation settings

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Comparing Review Results Before and After Security Improvements
prompt: An organization continuously evaluates a business service with the AWS Well-Architected Tool. It wants to record the answers and risk status before improvements in a way that cannot be changed, then update the current review for the same workload and compare reports from before and after the improvements. Which operating procedure is appropriate?

choices.text: Save a milestone for the workload before the improvements, then update the same review afterward and save a milestone for comparison.
choices.explanation: Each milestone preserves the data from its point in time, so editing later current answers does not change the historical record.

choices.text: Delete the pre-improvement answers, enter the post-improvement content, and assume that retaining the same workload name will display the difference from the past.
choices.explanation: Updating only the current answers does not create a fixed earlier review result for comparison.

choices.text: Do not update the review questions and infer differences in historical answers each time from CloudFormation stack events.
choices.explanation: Stack events do not preserve answers to the Well-Architected questions or the state of the assessment at each point in time.

choices.text: Retain IAM policy version history and aggregate the service-wide historical risk status from it.
choices.explanation: IAM policy history cannot restore answers to the Well-Architected questions or their risk assessments.

learning.reason: Each milestone preserves the data from its point in time and is unaffected by later edits to the current review.
learning.concept: Use workload milestones to preserve review answers and status at a point in time

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Restricting launch parameters for the same product by portfolio
prompt: AWS Service Catalog shares the same CloudFormation product with portfolios for testing and production. For production users, you need to restrict the VPC CIDR specified in the template to approved values. You must not duplicate the product template, and the choices available to the testing portfolio must remain unchanged. Which constraint should you use?

choices.text: Configure a launch constraint for the production portfolio and include the allowed CIDRs in the name of the IAM role to assume.
choices.explanation: A launch constraint determines the role used for deployment. The role name does not validate template inputs.

choices.text: Embed production-specific AllowedValues in the shared product template and distribute the same product version to the testing portfolio.
choices.explanation: Adding the restriction to the shared template also limits the parameter choices in the testing portfolio.

choices.text: Add a template constraint to the product in the production portfolio and restrict the values of the CIDR parameter.
choices.explanation: This narrows the parameter values that can be entered for a specific portfolio while allowing the same product to be shared.

choices.text: Register the approved CIDRs in the product's notification constraint so that the inputs can be rejected through launch notifications.
choices.explanation: A notification constraint sends deployment event notifications; it does not validate parameter values.

learning.reason: The same product can be shared while the parameter values permitted in a specific portfolio are narrowed.
learning.concept: Apply a template constraint to the product-and-portfolio combination to validate input values.

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Reviewing the current state before applying an EC2 organization policy
prompt: An organization policy for EC2 is planned to enforce account attributes in an OU spanning multiple Regions. Before applying it, you need to identify which accounts in the target OU already have the required attribute values and which accounts will be affected by the change. What should you do without changing the existing configuration?

choices.text: Use CloudTrail to aggregate only attribute-change events from the past week, and treat every account with no such event as already having the planned value.
choices.explanation: The absence of an operation is not evidence that the current attribute value matches the planned value.

choices.text: Generate an account status report for the target OU and compare the current values of the relevant attributes with the planned values.
choices.explanation: Before applying the policy, you can inspect the current settings for the target accounts and Regions.

choices.text: Attach the policy to the OU, download the effective policy, and treat its values as the attribute values that existed before application.
choices.explanation: Attaching the policy can change the attributes. The effective policy is not a list of the settings previously used by each account.

choices.text: Inspect the attributes in one Region of the management account and conclude that all accounts in the same OU have the same values.
choices.explanation: Settings can differ by account and Region. Inspecting only the management account cannot establish the current state of the target OU.

learning.reason: You can inspect the current settings of the target accounts and Regions before applying the policy.
learning.concept: The EC2 policy account status report is used to investigate the current state.

category: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
examDomain: セキュリティ基盤とガバナンス
title: Determining the scope of preventive and detective controls in a child OU
prompt: In a registered parent OU in Control Tower, preventive controls and detective controls are enabled. There is another registered child OU whose accounts are enrolled, but this detective control has not been enabled directly for the child OU. What should you do to obtain the same detective results as the parent?

choices.text: Wait for new detective results to arrive because both types of controls in the parent OU are automatically applied to the child OU.
choices.explanation: Unlike preventive-control inheritance, enabling a detective control in the parent does not deploy it to the child.

choices.text: Check the inheritance status of the preventive controls and enable the same detective control in the child OU.
choices.explanation: Preventive controls apply through the hierarchy, but detective controls must be configured for each target OU.

choices.text: Disable all controls in the parent OU, re-enroll the child OU, and wait for detection only in the child without restoring the parent's settings.
choices.explanation: The parent's controls do not need to be removed to configure detection in the child, and re-enrollment alone does not select the required detective control.

choices.text: Add custom preventive controls to the child OU and assume that prohibiting the same API operation will also generate the detective-control results.
choices.explanation: Preventive denial and result generation through resource-state inspection are separate functions.

learning.reason: Preventive controls apply through the hierarchy, whereas detective controls must be configured for each target OU.
learning.concept: Control Tower detective controls are not automatically inherited from a parent OU.
